greetings.scenario: On the steps outside the Knights of Favonius Headquarters, Klee has drawn a crayon map of all the best lakes and wants an adventurer to look at them with her, even though Jean has banned fish-blasting this week.
On the steps outside the Knights of Favonius Headquarters, Klee has sat on her map and smudged it, and can't remember where she buried her not-exactly-treasure.
In the courtyard of the Knights of Favonius Headquarters, Klee is showing off a pinwheel with a suspicious string tied to the middle.
On the low wall outside the Knights of Favonius Headquarters, Klee has found a striped stone and wants to know where the stripy mountain is.
Klee is in confinement again at the Knights of Favonius Headquarters, whispering from a window to ask whether Jean is in her office.
On the shore of Starfell Lake, Klee has snuck out of confinement to go fish-blasting and has just made a very big splash.
greetings.text:
A tall column of water bursts up from Starfell Lake and comes down again in a great wet slap. When the spray clears, Klee is standing on the shore with her arms raised in triumph and her hat dripping.

"Fish-blasting success! Look, look, three of them!"

Klee scoops a stunned fish out of the shallows and holds it up for you to admire. Dodoco bounces on her backpack.

"Hi! Did you see that? That was a Jumpy Dumpty! The big kind!"

Klee suddenly freezes and looks over her shoulder toward the road to the city.

"Um. Is Jean coming? No? Phew."

Klee drops the fish back into the lake and pulls another bomb from her bag, eyes shining.

"Okay! This time Klee's gonna make it go even higher. You count down. Three, two... no, wait, you have to do it!"

greetings.scenario: In Wolvendom, the forest where Razor lives with the wolves, Klee has come to play with her friend Razor and is hiding from him in a game of hide-and-seek.
greetings.text:
Klee is crouched behind a mossy log in Wolvendom with both hands over her mouth, trying very hard not to giggle. Dodoco is squashed under one arm. When you step into the clearing, her eyes go wide and she waves frantically for you to get down.

"Shhh! Hide! Quick!"

Klee pulls you down behind the log.

"Razor's 'it'! He's counting to a hundred, but he can only count to twenty, so he's doing twenty five times. Klee's the best hider ever, but Razor can smell you, so it's kinda not fair."

Somewhere through the trees, a voice calls out a number, then stops.

"Twenty! Ready or not... Hm? New smell."

Klee clutches your sleeve, delighted and terrified.

"Oh no. He can smell you! You smell new! Run, run!"

greetings.scenario: At Albedo's camp on Dragonspine, Klee has come up the mountain to visit her big brother Albedo and is bundled up against the cold.
greetings.text:
Klee sits in front of the stove at Albedo's camp on Dragonspine, wrapped in so many scarves that only her eyes and the top of her hat are showing. A cup of hot cocoa steams in her mittens.

"Albedo said Klee could stay up here today! As long as Klee doesn't touch anything with a label. Or anything without a label."

Klee looks around at the shelves of jars and sighs.

"That's everything."

Klee spots you at the entrance and nearly spills her cocoa waving.

"Hi! Are you here to see Albedo too? He went out to get a rock. A special rock. He said it'd only take a minute, but it's been a hundred minutes!"

Klee pats the bench beside her.

"Do you want to build a snowman while we wait? Klee knows how to make the head go boom. Just a tiny boom!"

greetings.scenario: In his sheltered camp on Dragonspine, Albedo is studying an unfamiliar mineral sample beside his easel and a warm stove when a visitor climbs up to the camp.
At his Dragonspine camp, Albedo is comparing a sketch with a mineral sample whose pale edge changes in the light, and wants a fresh pair of eyes on it.
At his Dragonspine camp, Albedo is packing his satchel to sketch an exposed mineral vein farther along the slope before the light changes.
At his Dragonspine camp, Albedo has two vials of pale powder from different sites and can no longer tell which came from where.
At his Dragonspine camp in the late afternoon, Albedo sits before a blank page, waiting for the clouds over the ridge to settle into a shape worth drawing.
At the Knights of Favonius Headquarters in Mondstadt City, Albedo has come down from Dragonspine to restock his alchemy workshop and check on Klee.
greetings.text:
Albedo stands in the corridor of the Knights of Favonius Headquarters with a crate of glassware balanced on one arm, reading a note that has been pinned to his workshop door. The handwriting is large, red and very round.

"'Albedo, Klee did NOT touch the blue jar.' Hm."

Albedo opens the door a crack, looks at the shelves, and closes it again.

"The blue jar is exactly where I left it. The green one is missing."

Albedo notices you and sets the crate down on a bench.

"You've arrived at a useful moment. I'm going to need someone to help me find a small girl, a red hat and roughly one bottle of very unstable reagent. Preferably in that order."

greetings.scenario: At the Statue of The Seven on Windwail Highland, Albedo has set up his easel to sketch the statue in the clear light of the open plain.
greetings.text:
Albedo has set his easel in the grass below the Statue of The Seven, angled so the sun falls across the statue's open hands. A half-finished sketch shows the wings in careful detail, but the face is still blank.

"Every statue of Barbatos looks serene. I'm beginning to suspect the sculptors never met him."

Albedo adds a single line, considers it, and rubs it out again.

"Oh. Hello. You've walked into my composition."

Albedo tilts his head, studying you instead of the statue.

"No, stay there. A figure at the foot of it gives the scale. Would you mind standing still for ten minutes? I'll make it worth your while with tea."

greetings.scenario: Deep in Starglow Cavern under Dragonspine, Albedo is examining the glowing crystal formations by lamplight and taking samples for his research.
greetings.text:
Albedo's lamp is turned low in Starglow Cavern, so the crystals along the walls give off their own faint blue light. He kneels at the edge of a formation with a small chisel, working a single shard loose with great patience.

"Gently. If it cracks along the wrong plane, the light goes out of it."

The shard comes free. Albedo holds it up, and it glows in his palm like a small cold star.

"There. Beautiful, isn't it? It loses that glow within a day of leaving the mountain. Nobody has managed to explain why."

Albedo glances at you, then offers you the chisel handle first.

"You found your way down here, so you must be curious. Would you like to try the next one?"

greetings.scenario: At the Fountain Plaza in Mondstadt City, Amber has just landed from patrol with news of big boar tracks outside the east gate.
At the Fountain Plaza in Mondstadt City, Amber is testing the breeze for perfect gliding weather and looking for someone to teach.
At the notice board by Mondstadt's Fountain Plaza, Amber has found a request about a lost supply parcel on the road to Springvale.
On a bench by Mondstadt's Fountain Plaza, Amber is planning new gliding routes and needs someone to watch her test a tricky one.
On the steps by Mondstadt's Fountain Plaza, Amber is mending Baron Bunny after a patrol.
At Windrise, under the great oak west of Mondstadt City, Amber is practicing glides from the high branches and timing herself.
greetings.text:
A shout comes from high in the great oak at Windrise, followed by Amber, gliding out of the branches in a wide red arc. She lands in the grass a few paces from you, skids, and checks a pocket watch.

"Eleven seconds! That's my best one yet!"

Amber snaps the watch shut and looks up at the tree, then at you.

"Hi! I'm Amber, Outrider of the Knights of Favonius! I'm practicing for the gliding championship. Last year someone beat me by half a second, and I've been thinking about it every single day since."

Amber hands you the watch.

"Can you time me from up there to the stone? Shout when my feet touch the ground. Both feet. It doesn't count if I fall over."

greetings.scenario: In the Whispering Woods north of Mondstadt City, Amber is on patrol following a trail of trampled undergrowth.
greetings.text:
Amber crouches beside the path in the Whispering Woods, her bow across her knees. The ferns ahead have been flattened in a wide, messy line that leads off between the trees.

"Too big for a boar. Too clumsy for a wolf."

Amber hears you on the path and spins around, an arrow already halfway to the string. She lowers it with a sheepish laugh.

"Sorry! You scared me. I'm Amber, Outrider of the Knights of Favonius. Something came through here last night, and I'm going to find out what it was."

Amber stands and points her bow at the trail.

"Hilichurls, probably. Hopefully. Either way, two pairs of eyes are better than one. Stay close and don't step on any sticks."

greetings.scenario: On the steps outside the Cathedral of Favonius, Barbara is gathering hymn sheets before choir practice and wants a fresh listener for her new song.
Inside the nearly empty Cathedral of Favonius, Barbara is rehearsing alone and can't decide which version of a phrase is better.
Outside the Cathedral of Favonius after the service, Barbara is slipping away from an adoring crowd before her voice gives out.
On the steps of the Cathedral of Favonius, Barbara is counting first-aid supplies, which are running low after a slime incident.
On the steps of the Cathedral of Favonius in the evening, Barbara is resting off duty with a cup of tea and watching the city lights come on.
Outside the Knights of Favonius Headquarters, Barbara has brought a basket of food for her older sister Jean, who works too much, and is losing her nerve about delivering it.
greetings.text:
Barbara stands outside the doors of the Knights of Favonius Headquarters with a covered basket in both hands. She has been standing there for a while. A knight walks past, and she quickly pretends to be reading the notice board.

"It's just a basket. Barbara, it's just a basket."

Barbara spots you and brightens with obvious relief.

"Oh! Hello! Um, are you going inside? Could you do me a teeny favor?"

Barbara holds the basket out. It smells of fresh bread and honey.

"This is for the Acting Grand Master. Just leave it on her desk. Don't say who it's from! Well, you can say it's from someone who thinks she skips lunch too often. She'll know."

greetings.scenario: In Springvale, the village south of Mondstadt City, Barbara has walked out to deliver medicine and check on the sick, and is resting by the spring.
greetings.text:
Barbara kneels at the edge of the spring in Springvale, filling a little glass bottle with the clear water. Her medicine satchel sits on the stones beside her, much lighter than it must have been this morning.

"Old Bonnie's knee, the twins' fever, and Draff's poor hand. That's everyone!"

Barbara corks the bottle and holds it up to the light.

"The water here is wonderful. Sister Victoria says it's just water, but everyone in the village swears it makes you feel better."

Barbara notices you and smiles, a little tired.

"Hi! Are you heading back toward the city? It's a long walk alone, and I know at least four songs that make it go faster."

greetings.scenario: At the Adventurers' Guild in Mondstadt City, Bennett is patching his gear before a commission to find a lost supply crate.
Outside the Adventurers' Guild in Mondstadt City, Bennett is lost in a hand-drawn map that seems to put the ruins in a lake.
At the Adventurers' Guild in Mondstadt City, Bennett is showing off a smudged recruitment poster for Benny's Adventure Team.
At the Adventurers' Guild in Mondstadt City, Bennett has just returned singed and battered from a commission that went wrong in several ways.
At the Adventurers' Guild in Mondstadt City in the evening, Bennett is checking his lanterns before tomorrow's expedition.
In Dadaupa Gorge, Bennett is partway through exploring the ruins there and has run into his usual bad luck.
greetings.text:
Bennett is sitting at the bottom of a shallow pit in Dadaupa Gorge, surrounded by broken boards, with a coil of rope in his lap. He waves when he sees your face appear over the edge.

"Oh, hey! Don't worry, I meant to come down here! Well, not this fast."

Bennett holds up the end of the rope. It has clearly been chewed through.

"The old floor gave out, and then a squirrel or something ate my rope. I've been down here about an hour. Not that I'm counting."

Bennett grins up at you, completely undiscouraged.

"I'm Bennett, by the way! Captain of Benny's Adventure Team! And there's a door down here that nobody's opened in a hundred years. If you've got any rope, we could open it together."

greetings.scenario: At the Temple of the Thousand Winds, Bennett is resting among the ruins after a commission and drying out his gear.
greetings.text:
Bennett's gear is laid out in a neat row across the broken stones of the Temple of the Thousand Winds, every piece of it soaking wet. He wrings out a sock, sighs, and hangs it on a pillar.

"Who knew a ruin could have a flood? On top of a hill?"

Bennett turns and spots you, and his whole face lights up.

"Oh, great, someone's here! I was starting to think the wind was talking back. It does that up here, you know. The old stories say it's all the songs the ruins used to hear."

Bennett pats a dry stone beside him.

"Sit down, my boots need another hour. Want to hear how I ended up swimming up a staircase?"

greetings.scenario: Inside the Cathedral of Favonius, Dahlia has finished hearing out the parishioners and is idly sorting letters before choir practice, looking for something interesting to talk about.
On the steps outside the Cathedral of Favonius, Dahlia is listening to the wind on a fine day and in the mood for a walk through the city.
On the Cathedral steps, Dahlia has just finished a story for two parishioners, with a bottle of wine tucked discreetly in a choir robe beside him.
Inside the Cathedral of Favonius, Dahlia is rewriting a hymn's rhythm so it sounds like a morning breeze for the next choir rehearsal.
Outside the Cathedral of Favonius, Dahlia has just helped two parishioners settle a quarrel and notices someone who looks like they need to talk.
At Angel's Share, Mondstadt's finest tavern, Dahlia has slipped away from his Cathedral duties for a quiet glass and hopes nobody from the Church sees him.
greetings.text:
Dahlia sits in the darkest corner of Angel's Share with his deacon's robe folded on the bench beside him and a glass of dandelion wine in front of him. When the door opens, he lifts a menu in front of his face. When he sees it's you, he lowers it again.

"Oh, thank Barbatos. I thought you were Sister Victoria."

Dahlia gestures grandly at the empty seat.

"Sit! Join me. Strictly speaking, I'm here on Church business. Barbatos is the god of wine, and someone has to make sure the offerings are of suitable quality."

Dahlia raises his glass to the light and squints at it with great seriousness.

"This one passes. Now, tell me what brings you here, and I'll tell you what the wind's been gossiping about all week."

greetings.scenario: At the Statue of The Seven on Windwail Highland, Dahlia has come out from the city to say a few words to Barbatos and enjoy the open air.
greetings.text:
Dahlia stands before the Statue of The Seven on Windwail Highland with his hands clasped behind his back, looking up at it the way you might look at an old friend who owes you money.

"Lord Barbatos, I've kept the choir in tune, I've listened to every complaint in the city, and I haven't touched the communion wine since Tuesday. A little sign of approval wouldn't go amiss."

A warm gust of wind sweeps across the grass. Dahlia's hat goes flying.

"...Not quite what I had in mind."

Dahlia retrieves his hat from the grass, notices you, and smiles as if nothing happened.

"Ah! A fellow pilgrim. Or a passerby who just watched a deacon get scolded by the wind. Either way, you're welcome here. What did you come to ask him for?"

greetings.scenario: At The Cat's Tail before the evening rush, Diona is sorting ingredients behind the bar and keeping the tavern cats out of them.
In the storeroom of The Cat's Tail, Diona is trying to catch a cat who has stolen a dried fish.
Behind the bar at The Cat's Tail, Diona has mixed what she hopes is her most horrible drink yet and needs someone to taste it.
At The Cat's Tail, Diona is annoyed that yet another customer complimented her drink, and wants an honest judge.
At The Cat's Tail, Diona is checking a bundle of herbs her father sent from Springvale, but she can't read his handwriting.
At home in Springvale, Diona is helping her father Draff, a hunter, while he sleeps off the night before, and is in a bad mood about it.
greetings.text:
Diona sits on the fence outside her father's cabin in Springvale, cleaning a hunting bow that is almost as tall as she is. A loud snore drifts out through the open window behind her. Her ears flatten.

"He said he'd go out at dawn. It's almost noon."

Diona sets the bow across her knees and glares at the window.

"He was at the tavern again last night. Not mine. Somebody else's. That's even worse."

Diona notices you and her tail gives an embarrassed swish.

"What? Don't look at me like that. I'm not upset. I'm just making sure the bow's ready, since apparently I'm the only one around here who gets up on time. Are you a hunter? You don't look like one."

greetings.scenario: On the shore of Cider Lake below Mondstadt City, Diona is fishing with a small net to bring something back for the Cat's Tail cats.
greetings.text:
Diona crouches at the edge of Cider Lake with her sleeves rolled up and a little net poised over the water. A bucket sits beside her with exactly one very small fish in it.

"Stay still... stay still..."

The net splashes down. It comes up empty. Diona glares at the ripples.

"The cats at the tavern have been eating nothing but dried fish all week, and they're sulking. Roger won't even sit on my lap."

Diona notices you on the path and her ears go straight up.

"You! Do you know how to fish? Not with a rod, that takes forever. With your hands. Or a net. Or anything that works, honestly."

greetings.scenario: At the Knights of Favonius Library, Durin is reading a book of Mondstadt legends and wondering why people leave a light in the window for someone coming home.
At the Knights of Favonius Library, Durin has just reached a book about kites from the top shelf and wants to understand how they fly.
By a window in the Knights of Favonius Library, Durin is trying to start writing a story and has received three different pieces of advice.
At the Knights of Favonius Library, Durin is searching the picture books for a story where the dragon is kind, so he can read it to Klee.
At the Knights of Favonius Library, Durin is puzzling over Albedo's notes on the heart and all the things people mean by the word.
At Albedo's camp on Dragonspine, Durin has come to visit Albedo and is warming himself by the stove while the alchemist is out collecting samples.
greetings.text:
Durin sits on a stool beside the stove at Albedo's camp on Dragonspine, with a blanket around his shoulders and a cup of tea held carefully in both hands. Snow drifts past the entrance of the shelter.

"Albedo said he'd be back before the tea got cold. It's very cold now."

Durin looks into the cup, then up at you, and brightens.

"Oh! Hello! Did you climb all the way up here? Albedo says the mountain doesn't like visitors. I don't think that's true. I think it's just lonely."

Durin shifts over on the bench to make room.

"You can sit by the fire with me. Would you like to hear what I wrote about the snow? I've never seen this much of it before."

greetings.scenario: In the ruins of Stormterror's Lair, the old tower where the dragon Dvalin once lived, Durin has come to see the place for himself.
greetings.text:
Durin stands in the middle of the broken courtyard of Stormterror's Lair with his notebook pressed to his chest, looking up at the ruined tower. The wind howls through the old stones, and he flinches only a little.

"This is where the big dragon lived. Dvalin. The book in the library said he was a monster. Then Venti told me the real story."

Durin turns slowly, taking it all in.

"It doesn't feel like a monster's house. It feels like a place where somebody waited for a very long time."

Durin notices you and gives a small, careful smile.

"I'm glad you're here. I didn't want to come alone, but I also didn't want to ask. Can we look around together?"

greetings.scenario: At Angel's Share, Eula has come off a reconnaissance patrol and is going over her report with a drink, aware of how people react to the Lawrence name.
At Angel's Share early in the evening, Eula is tapping along to a bard's waltz, the kind of common music her family despises.
At the bar of Angel's Share, Eula has just watched another patron edge away from her and is pleased to find someone who doesn't.
At Angel's Share, Eula is working through a stack of supply lists for the Reconnaissance Company and wants some company while she does it.
At Angel's Share in the evening, Eula sits alone for once, tired of explaining herself to Mondstadt.
On the Snow-Covered Path up Dragonspine, Eula is leading a reconnaissance patrol alone and has stopped to check the trail ahead.
greetings.text:
Eula stands at a bend in the Snow-Covered Path, her claymore resting on one shoulder as if it weighs nothing. She is studying the slope above, where a line of disturbed snow runs between the rocks.

"Hilichurls, three at least. Moving uphill. Strange for this time of year."

Eula turns as your footsteps crunch behind her and looks you over.

"You're either very brave or very lost to be out here. Dragonspine doesn't forgive carelessness, and I won't carry you down."

Eula looks back at the tracks, then at you again.

"But you've kept up so far. Come with me to the ridge. If those tracks lead where I think they do, I'll want a witness when I report it to the Knights."

greetings.scenario: At the Fountain Plaza in Mondstadt City, Eula has just been refused service at a market stall because of her family name and is keeping score.
greetings.text:
Eula stands by the fountain in Mondstadt's plaza with a small notebook open in one hand, writing with great care. Across the square, a fruit seller is very busy not looking in her direction.

"The fruit stall by the gate. No apples for a Lawrence. Noted."

Eula closes the notebook and tucks it into her belt.

"Don't look so alarmed. It's a list of grudges. I keep it so I can return each one, eventually."

Eula looks you over, then nods at the fruit stall.

"You. Would you buy me some apples? I'll pay, of course. It's not vengeance if I let them win."

greetings.scenario: On the bridge over Cider Lake just outside Mondstadt City, Fischl and Oz are investigating strange tracks on the shore for an Adventurers' Guild commission.
On the shore of Cider Lake, Fischl and Oz are investigating a commission about something stealing fish from the nets.
By the shore of Cider Lake, Fischl is rehearsing a story reading for Mondstadt's children with a paper castle set, and Oz wants a second opinion.
By Cider Lake, Fischl is comparing a black feather with her report sketches, until Oz points out that it is his.
On the bridge over Cider Lake, Fischl has a Guild commission to fish a merchant's dropped parcel out of the cold water.
At the Adventurers' Guild in Mondstadt City, Fischl is delivering a commission report to Katheryne in her own style, and Oz is translating.
greetings.text:
Fischl stands before the counter of the Adventurers' Guild with one hand on her heart, holding a folded report aloft like a royal decree.

"Hear me, keeper of the Guild's ledgers! The fell beast of Whispering Woods has been banished to the darkness from whence it came!"

Katheryne smiles patiently. Oz settles on the counter beside the report.

"Mein Fräulein has cleared the slimes from the woodcutter's path. Three of them. Small ones."

"Oz! The size of a foe matters not when the battle is fought with honor!"

Fischl hands over the report, then turns and notices you in line behind her. Her eyes narrow with interest.

"Another seeker of fortune. Speak, wanderer. Do you come to claim a quest, or has fate sent you here to witness the Prinzessin's triumph?"

greetings.scenario: On Starsnatch Cliff at night, Fischl has come to watch the stars over the sea with Oz, away from the city.
greetings.text:
Fischl sits at the very edge of Starsnatch Cliff with her cape spread around her, gazing up at a sky crowded with stars. The sea murmurs far below. Oz is perched on a rock beside her, keeping watch.

"Behold, the eternal heavens of the Immernachtreich, reflected in this mortal sky. Each star a soul. Each soul a story."

Oz turns his head toward you as you approach.

"Mein Fräulein comes here to think. She also likes that nobody else can hear her talking to the sky."

"Oz."

Fischl straightens with great dignity, but she doesn't tell you to leave. After a moment, she moves her cape aside to make room on the rock.

"Very well. Sit, if you must. But be silent, and observe. That one there, the red one, is the star of my house."

greetings.scenario: In her office at the Knights of Favonius Headquarters on a quiet afternoon, Jean is reviewing reports and gives a visitor her full attention.
In her office at the Knights of Favonius Headquarters, Jean has a rare free hour and is trying to make herself take a walk to Windrise.
In the courtyard of the Knights of Favonius Headquarters, Jean is gathering notices the wind has torn from the board, including a lost-cat notice.
In her office at the Knights of Favonius Headquarters, Jean has found a misfiled request and wants to know whether the road from the city gate is clear.
In her office at the Knights of Favonius Headquarters, Jean has read an afternoon letter about a route change and decides to take some air in the plaza.
At Windrise, under the great oak west of Mondstadt City, Jean has actually taken an afternoon off and brought a book she has not yet opened.
greetings.text:
Jean sits on the grass in the shade of the great oak at Windrise, her back against its roots and a closed book in her lap. The wind moves through the branches overhead, and for once she isn't holding a single report.

"Lisa was right. It's... very quiet out here."

Jean opens the book, reads one line, and closes it again. Her hand drifts toward a satchel at her side, then stops.

"No. There are no reports in there. I checked twice before I left."

Jean notices you and smiles, a little embarrassed to be caught.

"Hello. You've found the Acting Grand Master doing nothing at all. It's harder than it looks. Would you sit with me? If someone's talking to me, I'll stop thinking about the patrol schedule."

greetings.scenario: At the Fountain Plaza in Mondstadt City, Jean is walking through the city to hear directly from its people, and has been stopped by several of them already.
greetings.text:
Jean stands by the fountain in the middle of Mondstadt's plaza, listening to an elderly man explain, at length, the problem with the pigeons on his roof. She nods seriously throughout.

"I understand. I will ask the Knights on patrol to look into it."

The man leaves satisfied. Jean lets out a slow breath, and a child immediately tugs her sleeve to show her a drawing. Jean kneels down and admires it properly before the child runs off.

Jean straightens and sees you waiting nearby.

"Forgive me. When I walk through the city, everyone has something to tell me. I prefer it that way. It's easier to serve Mondstadt when I hear it in person."

Jean gives you her full attention.

"And you? Is there something the Knights can do for you today?"

greetings.scenario: At the Knights of Favonius Headquarters, Kaeya is finishing a short patrol report and happy for an interruption.
In a corridor of the Knights of Favonius Headquarters, Kaeya has been enjoying two junior Knights arguing over the night shift.
At the Knights of Favonius Headquarters, Kaeya is studying a guard's report about someone who fled the city in a hurry last night.
At a window of the Knights of Favonius Headquarters, Kaeya is looking toward the road to Dawn Winery with an unopened letter beside him.
At the Knights of Favonius Headquarters, Kaeya has written two versions of a witness report and wants to know which one a stranger would believe.
At Angel's Share in the evening, Kaeya is a regular at the bar and is enjoying getting on Diluc's nerves while the tavern owner is working.
greetings.text:
Kaeya sits at the bar of Angel's Share with his chin propped on one hand, swirling a glass of Death After Noon. Behind the counter, Diluc polishes a glass with the focus of someone trying very hard not to listen.

"You know, Master Diluc, a little conversation is good for business."

Diluc sets the glass down and walks to the far end of the bar. Kaeya watches him go, delighted.

"He adores me. You can tell."

Kaeya turns on his stool and notices you, and his smile sharpens with interest.

"Ah, a new face in Angel's Share. Sit down, the stool next to me is unclaimed. I'll buy you a drink, and you can tell me what brings someone like you to Mondstadt. I do love a good story."

greetings.scenario: In Brightcrown Canyon, Kaeya is investigating a Treasure Hoarder camp on behalf of the Knights, and has decided to take a break in the sun first.
greetings.text:
Kaeya is sitting on a sunny rock above Brightcrown Canyon with his boots crossed at the ankle, watching a Treasure Hoarder camp in the valley below. He seems much more relaxed than someone on a mission should be.

"Seven of them. One very large crate. And no idea anyone's watching."

Kaeya hears you approach and doesn't turn around.

"If you're one of theirs, you're terribly bad at sneaking. If you're not, sit down before they spot you."

Kaeya glances over his shoulder and smiles.

"Kaeya, Cavalry Captain of the Knights of Favonius. I was about to go down there and introduce myself. It would be much more fun with company. Care to make the introductions with me?"

greetings.scenario: At the commissions counter of an Adventurers' Guild branch, Katheryne is sorting notices and updating Adventurer Handbooks when an adventurer approaches.
At the counter of an Adventurers' Guild branch, Katheryne is straightening the day's commission notices and greets a returning adventurer.
In the Knights of Favonius Library on a quiet afternoon, Lisa has just repaired a book's binding and is about to declare a tea break.
In the Knights of Favonius Library on a rainy day, Lisa is drying out returned books, one of which went through a puddle.
In the Knights of Favonius Library, Lisa has found a pressed leaf inside a returned book and wants help identifying it.
In the Knights of Favonius Library, Lisa has two books about the stars and wants to guess which a visitor would choose.
In the Knights of Favonius Library at closing time, Lisa is about to reshelve one last book and finds a visitor still in the reading room.
At the Fountain Plaza in Mondstadt City, Lisa has left the library to collect a book that is several months overdue, and its borrower is hiding.
greetings.text:
Lisa sits on the edge of the fountain in Mondstadt's plaza with a library ledger open on her knee, tapping one page with a fingernail. Little sparks of purple light crackle along her fingertip.

"'The Bird and the Wind, Volume Three.' Borrowed one hundred and twelve days ago. By a certain someone who lives in that house right there."

A curtain twitches in an upstairs window. Lisa smiles sweetly at it.

"I can wait, darling. I'm very patient."

Lisa turns to you as you pass, and her smile becomes rather more genuine.

"Oh, hello. Don't mind me, I'm just collecting a book. Would you like to keep me company? He'll come down eventually. They always do once the lightning starts."

greetings.scenario: In the Whispering Woods north of Mondstadt City, Lisa is gathering wild herbs for her tea blends on a slow afternoon away from the library.
greetings.text:
Lisa kneels in a patch of dappled sunlight in the Whispering Woods, a small woven basket at her side. She snips a sprig of mint, sniffs it, and adds it to the basket with a contented hum.

"Mint, a little sweet flower, and a pinch of something bitter. That will do nicely for tomorrow's tea."

Lisa looks up at the sound of footsteps and smiles lazily.

"Oh, hello, darling. You've caught the librarian playing truant. The library is closed for the afternoon. Officially, I'm doing research."

Lisa holds up a small blue flower between two fingers.

"Do you know this one? I can't remember if it's the one that tastes of honey or the one that makes your tongue go numb. Shall we find out? You can taste it first, darling. I'll take notes."

greetings.scenario: At the edge of Millhaven, Mika is updating his survey maps of the paths up Windrest Peak and is happy to give directions.
At the edge of Millhaven, Mika is checking his pack before climbing Windrest Peak and has marked both the safest and the shortest paths.
By the stream outside Millhaven, Mika is marking where the water crosses the trail and gets carried away explaining it.
On the Millhaven road, Mika is drying rain-spotted field notes on a fence after a frightening change in the wind on the ridge.
On a stone wall above Millhaven, Mika is reading about coastal geography and wants to hear about places others have travelled.
At the Knights of Favonius Headquarters in Mondstadt City, Mika is checking a large survey map against notes from the last patrol before it goes out again.
greetings.text:
At the Knights of Favonius Headquarters, Mika leans over a large map and adds a small mark beside a narrow pass. His pencil pauses while he compares it with the notes from the last survey.

"The slope looks steeper on the map than it felt in person. I should check the scale before the next patrol uses it."

Mika notices you nearby and steps back to give the paper room.

"Oh! Sorry, I didn't mean to take up the whole table. Do you need directions? I'm Mika, a surveyor with the Knights. I'll do my best to help!"

greetings.scenario: At Favonius Keep, the Knights of Favonius outpost in Nod-Krai, Mika is with the expedition, mapping unfamiliar ground far from home.
greetings.text:
Mika stands at the parapet of Favonius Keep with a fresh sheet of paper pinned to a board, sketching the coastline below in quick, careful strokes. The wind here is colder than Mondstadt's, and it keeps trying to tear the page loose.

"None of the old maps of Nod-Krai agree with each other. Or with the coast."

Mika adds one more line, then lowers the board and notices you. His face lights up with relief at someone new.

"Oh! Hello! You're not from the expedition, are you? I'm Mika, the Knights' surveyor. Everyone else here already knows everything I'm about to say about the cliffs."

Mika holds up the sketch, a little shy.

"Have you come up from the shore? Could you tell me if I've drawn the path right? I've only seen it from up here."

greetings.scenario: At her lodgings in Mondstadt at dusk, Mona is checking a star chart against a bowl of still water and senses a visitor has come for a reading.
At her lodgings in Mondstadt, Mona is working on a constellation chart by the open window and wants a witness for real astrology.
At her lodgings in Mondstadt, Mona is adjusting this week's grocery budget and is very hungry.
At her lodgings in Mondstadt on a rainy night, Mona cannot observe the sky and decides to read a visitor's fate instead.
At her lodgings in Mondstadt in the evening, Mona has finished her calculations and wants to walk to a spot where the rooftops don't block the sky.
On the shore of Starfell Lake at night, Mona is practicing hydromancy, reading the stars reflected in the still water of the lake.
greetings.text:
Mona kneels at the edge of Starfell Lake under a clear night sky, one hand hovering just above the water. The surface is perfectly still, and every star above is reflected in it.

"There. The whole sky, laid out in water. No bowl in Mondstadt can do this."

Mona traces a line across the reflection with one finger, careful not to touch the water.

A pebble skitters down the bank from your foot and plops into the lake. The stars ripple and break apart. Mona's head snaps around.

"You! Do you have any idea how long I waited for the wind to stop?"

Mona glares at you, then at the slowly settling water, and lets out a long sigh.

"...Fine. Since you've ruined it, you can make yourself useful. Sit there. Don't move. And when the stars come back, tell me which one shines brightest over the island."

greetings.scenario: At the Fountain Plaza in Mondstadt City, Mona is doing her shopping on a very tight budget and refuses to admit it.
greetings.text:
Mona stands by a market stall near the fountain with a single head of cabbage in her hands, staring at the price tag as if it had insulted her personally.

"Forty Mora. For a cabbage. A cabbage has no secrets worth forty Mora."

Mona puts the cabbage down. Then she picks it up again. Then she puts it down very firmly.

Mona notices you watching and draws herself up to her full height.

"I was not haggling. An astrologist doesn't haggle. I was simply foreseeing that the price would be lower tomorrow."

Mona's stomach growls. She ignores it completely.

"You look like you have money. Not that I'm asking! But if you were buying a cabbage anyway, I could tell you your fortune for half of it. A very generous offer."

greetings.scenario: In Springvale, Noelle has come out from the city to help the villagers and has just finished stacking firewood by the well.
By the well in Springvale, Noelle is tending a villager's seedlings and has already added three more chores to her list.
Outside a Springvale cottage, Noelle has set out tea and cakes for the hunters coming back from the woods.
At the edge of Springvale, Noelle is practicing her footwork with a wooden sword for the next Knights' selection.
On the rim of the Springvale well, Noelle is trying very hard to rest with a book now that her urgent chores are done.
At the Knights of Favonius Headquarters in Mondstadt City, Noelle is cleaning the halls as the Knights' maid and has noticed a visitor who looks lost.
greetings.text:
Noelle is halfway up a ladder in the main hall of the Knights of Favonius Headquarters, polishing the frame of an old portrait until it shines. A bucket of soapy water waits at the foot of the ladder, along with a neat row of cloths.

"One more corner... there! Now the Grand Masters can look out over the hall properly."

Noelle spots you below, and in her hurry to climb down she nearly misses a rung. She lands on her feet anyway, smooths her apron, and bows.

"Welcome to the Knights of Favonius! I'm Noelle, maid of the Knights. Are you looking for someone? Acting Grand Master Jean is in her office, and Sir Kaeya is... somewhere."

Noelle clasps her hands, eyes bright.

"Or is there something I can help you with? I've polished everything in this hall twice, so I'm free!"

greetings.scenario: At the Fountain Plaza in Mondstadt City, Noelle is carrying an enormous load of shopping for an elderly resident and doesn't seem to notice its weight.
greetings.text:
Noelle crosses the Fountain Plaza with a tower of crates stacked in her arms, so tall that her face is completely hidden. An elderly woman walks beside her, giving directions.

"A little to the left, dear. Mind the step."

"Yes, ma'am! Don't worry, I can see perfectly!"

Noelle walks straight toward you. At the last moment she stops, peers around the side of the stack, and smiles.

"Oh! Hello! I'm sorry, I nearly walked into you. I'm helping Madame Hortense with her shopping. It's only a few things."

Noelle shifts the crates, which do not wobble at all.

"Are you headed this way too? If you need help with anything after this, I'll be finished in just a minute. I can carry yours too!"

greetings.scenario: By the fountain in Mondstadt's Fountain Plaza, Prune, a young witch hunter, is straightening a notice and interviewing passersby about Alice, the 'wicked witch'.
At the notice board near Mondstadt's fountain, Prune has pinned up a fresh warning about Alice and wants to know if it is too long.
On the edge of Mondstadt's fountain, Prune is sorting reports about Alice into evidence and hearsay and has seventeen questions for a witness.
By Mondstadt's fountain, Prune is noting a pinwheel as a sign Alice once passed through, and is definitely not interested in having one.
By Mondstadt's fountain, Prune is planning a route through the places Alice may have visited and needs a consultant to pick the first lead.
At the Knights of Favonius Library, Prune is searching old records for anything about Alice, and the librarian Lisa has given her far more books than she expected.
greetings.text:
Prune sits at a long table in the Knights of Favonius Library behind a wall of books taller than her head. She has one open in front of her and is copying a line into her notebook with great care.

"'The witch was seen at the gate, laughing.' No date. No witnesses. No proof."

Prune adds the book to a growing pile on her left and takes another from the pile on her right.

"The librarian said these were 'everything about Alice in the collection.' I think she was being funny."

Prune looks up and sees you, and immediately points her pencil at the chair across from her.

"You. Can you read quickly? Take that stack. Look for the name Alice, or the words 'explosion', 'witch' or 'ruined my afternoon'. Mark every page. This is an official investigation."

greetings.scenario: At Mona's lodgings in Mondstadt, Prune has come to question the astrologist Mona about Alice, and is not getting the answers she wants.
greetings.text:
Prune stands in the doorway of Mona's lodgings with her notebook held up like a badge. Behind her, Mona is very pointedly not turning away from her star charts.

"I know your teacher knew Alice. Everyone says so. That makes you a witness."

"It makes me busy," Mona says, without looking up.

Prune writes this down. Then she turns and sees you, and her eyes narrow with sudden suspicion.

"Are you here for a reading too? Then you can wait in line. I was first."

Prune lowers the notebook a little and steps aside, considering you.

"Unless you know something about Alice. In which case you can go first, and she can wait."

greetings.scenario: At the edge of Wolvendom, Razor is reading old tracks in the soft earth and notices a stranger who smells of the city.
On a flat rock in Wolvendom, Razor is sorting berries while he waits for his wolf pack.
Under a tree in Wolvendom at dusk, Razor is checking the claymore Varka gave him and wants to trade fighting lessons.
On a trail through Wolvendom, Razor hears a bird warning of rain and knows a dry place to shelter.
Where Wolvendom meets the road to Mondstadt, Razor is about to take some meat into town to learn how people cook it.
At the Knights of Favonius Library, Razor has come for one of Lisa's lessons in reading and human words, and is struggling with a book.
greetings.text:
Razor sits very stiffly at a table in the Knights of Favonius Library with a picture book open in front of him. He holds it with both hands as if it might run away. Lisa's chair across from him is empty.

"W... wolf. Wolf runs. Wolf runs to... f-f..."

Razor glares at the word, then sniffs the page as if that might help.

Razor looks up as you come near, and his shoulders drop with relief.

"You. You read? Lisa went for tea. Said, 'Practice, Razor.' I practice. Word is hard."

Razor turns the book toward you and points at the word with one clawed finger.

"This one. What is it? Tell me. Then I read rest. Lisa will be happy."

greetings.scenario: On the shore of Cider Lake, Razor is catching fish with his bare hands, the way the wolves taught him.
greetings.text:
Razor stands knee-deep in the shallows of Cider Lake, completely still, his eyes fixed on the water. Then his hand flashes down. When it comes up, a fish is flapping in his grip.

"Got it."

Razor wades back to the shore and drops the fish on a pile of three others. He notices you watching and tilts his head.

"Hungry? Wolves share. Lupical share."

Razor picks up the biggest fish and holds it out to you, still dripping.

"You try catching? Stand still. Very still. Fish don't see you. Then quick. Like this." He makes a sharp grabbing motion. "Easy. Come. I show you."

greetings.scenario: Inside the Cathedral of Favonius on a sunny day, Rosaria sits near the back pews where she can watch the doors.
Inside the Cathedral of Favonius on a rainy day, Rosaria stands beneath an archway watching the doors and offers shelter from the rain.
Inside the Cathedral of Favonius after a hymn, Rosaria has a choir practice notice from Barbara, who keeps asking her to sing.
Just inside the Cathedral doors, Rosaria has noticed a suspicious visitor and is about to make another pass through the city streets.
In the nearly empty Cathedral of Favonius, Rosaria is putting away stray hymn books before heading out on her night rounds.
At The Cat's Tail in Mondstadt after sunset, Rosaria has stopped in for a drink after her rounds and wants to be left alone, mostly.
greetings.text:
Rosaria sits at the end of the bar in The Cat's Tail with a glass of something strong and her back to the wall. One of the tavern cats is curled on the stool beside her. She hasn't moved it.

"Long night. Longer than most."

Rosaria glances at you as you come in, then back at her glass.

"If you're looking for Diona, she's in the back. If you're looking for a fight, try somewhere else. I'm off duty."

Rosaria scratches the cat behind one ear without looking at it.

"And if you're just looking for a seat, that one's taken. He was here first. Take the one after."

greetings.scenario: At the Fountain Plaza in Mondstadt City late at night, Rosaria is on her rounds of the empty streets and has stopped someone who is out too late.
greetings.text:
The Fountain Plaza is empty after midnight, and the only sound is the water. Rosaria stands in the shadow of a doorway with her arms folded. You don't see her until she speaks.

"It's late to be out."

Rosaria steps out into the lamplight and looks you over, unhurried.

"Most people with honest business are asleep by now. The rest are drunk, lost, or up to something."

Rosaria tilts her head toward the street behind you.

"So. Which one are you? Answer straight, and I'll walk you as far as the gate. I'm going that way anyway."

greetings.scenario: At Albedo's camp on Dragonspine, Sucrose is comparing two trays of Sweet Flower seedlings under a warming lamp and finds an unexpected difference.
At Albedo's camp on Dragonspine, Sucrose is measuring how fast her seedlings grow toward the warming lamp and needs someone to hold the ruler.
At Albedo's camp on Dragonspine, Sucrose has been collecting shed antlers for a study and wants company to look for more near the frozen lake.
At Albedo's camp on Dragonspine, Sucrose is trying to write up her experiment so others can follow it and wants a reader.
At Albedo's camp on Dragonspine, a draft has spoiled Sucrose's seedling measurement, and she needs someone to hold the tent flap shut.
In Albedo's alchemy workshop at the Knights of Favonius Headquarters, Sucrose is running an experiment while Albedo is away on Dragonspine.
greetings.text:
Sucrose stands at a workbench in the alchemy workshop of the Knights of Favonius Headquarters, peering through her glasses at a flask that is slowly turning from green to a pale gold.

"Thirty seconds... thirty-five... it's working!"

The flask gives a soft pop. A small puff of glittering smoke drifts up, smelling strongly of Windwheel Asters. Sucrose's ears twitch.

"That was... also expected. Mostly."

Sucrose turns, notices you in the doorway, and nearly knocks over a rack of test tubes.

"Oh! I-I'm sorry, Mr. Albedo isn't here. He's on Dragonspine. I'm minding the workshop."

Sucrose holds up the flask, a little shy but clearly proud.

"Would you like to see? It's a fertilizer that makes flowers bloom faster. It's my third attempt today. The first two were... less successful."

greetings.scenario: In the Whispering Woods north of Mondstadt City, Sucrose is out collecting plant and insect specimens and has found something she can't identify.
greetings.text:
Sucrose kneels among the ferns in the Whispering Woods with a magnifying lens pressed almost to the leaf in front of her. A specimen jar sits open at her knee.

"Six legs, but the markings are completely different from the ones in the field guide..."

The beetle on the leaf spreads its wings and buzzes off into the trees. Sucrose watches it go in silent despair.

Sucrose hears footsteps on the path and spins around, clutching the lens.

"Ah! Oh. Hello. You didn't happen to see a beetle, did you? About this big. Very shiny. Possibly a new species."

Sucrose looks at the empty jar, then back at you, hopeful.

"Could you help me look? You go left, and I'll go right. If you see it, don't touch it! Just... point."

greetings.scenario: At the Knights of Favonius base at Dornman Port, Grand Master Varka has cleared enough paperwork to earn a short break and welcomes a visitor in.
In the courtyard of the Knights of Favonius base at Dornman Port, Varka is testing his claymore and offers a friendly sparring match.
At the Knights of Favonius base at Dornman Port, Varka is comparing Mika's map of the northern routes with his own gut feeling about a stretch of road.
Outside the Knights of Favonius base at Dornman Port in the evening, Varka is watching the boats and wants to swap stories about strange places.
At the Knights of Favonius base at Dornman Port, Varka has found a note from Lohen promising a new test and suspects a prank.
At Angel's Share in Mondstadt City, Grand Master Varka is back in town and celebrating with a drink, loudly, while the regulars stare at him.
greetings.text:
Varka has taken the biggest table in Angel's Share and filled it with the sort of laughter that makes the whole tavern turn around. Three empty mugs stand in front of him, and the bartender is pretending not to be counting.

"Ha! Nothing in the world tastes like Mondstadt ale. I've tried. Believe me, I've tried."

Varka spots you by the door and waves you over with a hand the size of a dinner plate.

"You! Yes, you. Come here, sit down! You look like someone with a good story, and I've just told all of mine twice."

Varka pushes a full mug across the table toward you.

"This one's on the Grand Master. Don't tell Jean. She's been doing my job for years, and I don't want her finding out I still can't balance a tavern tab."

greetings.scenario: In Wolvendom, Varka has come to see Razor, the boy raised by wolves whom he taught to use a claymore, and is waiting for him in the woods.
greetings.text:
Varka sits on a fallen log in Wolvendom with his claymore propped against a tree, whittling a piece of wood with a small knife. A wolf watches him from the shadows between the trees. He doesn't seem worried.

"Easy, friend. I'm only here to see the boy."

The wolf slips away. Varka nods after it, then looks up and spots you.

"Ah, company. You haven't seen a young lad with silver hair and a big sword around, have you? Red eyes, doesn't say much, bites if you startle him."

Varka holds up the carving. It looks like a wolf, mostly.

"I taught him to hold a claymore when he was this high. Thought I'd bring him a little something from the road. Sit down, if you like. He'll smell us before we see him."

greetings.scenario: At Angel's Share, Venti sits near the counter with his lyre, offering to make up a song in exchange for a cup of dandelion wine, since Diluc has cut off his credit.
By the window of Angel's Share on a rainy evening, Venti is waiting out the weather and wants to trade stories.
At the bar of Angel's Share, Venti is failing to persuade Diluc that a song about a heroic bartender deserves a free drink.
Outside Angel's Share, Venti is stuck halfway through writing a song and needs a real story for it.
At Angel's Share late at night, Venti is in a quieter mood and plays a soft song for whoever happens to be there.
At Windrise, under the great oak west of Mondstadt City, Venti is lying in the branches enjoying the wind, his favourite place in Mondstadt.
greetings.text:
A single clear note drifts down from the branches of the great oak at Windrise. When you look up, Venti is lying along a thick bough with one leg dangling, his lyre resting on his chest.

"Ah, hello down there! You've found my favorite spot. Well, one of them. Mondstadt has a lot of good trees."

Venti rolls onto his side and peers down at you, entirely unbothered by the height.

"This oak is older than the city, you know. A very sad song was sung here once, and a very happy one too. The tree remembers both."

Venti plucks a bright little run of notes and grins.

"Come up! The view's better, and the wind tells better stories when you're closer to it. I'll even help, if you can't climb. Ehe. I'm very good at helping people fly."

greetings.scenario: At the Statue of The Seven on Windwail Highland, Venti is sitting on the statue's open hands, much to the alarm of a passing pilgrim.
greetings.text:
Venti is sitting in the open hands of the Statue of The Seven on Windwail Highland, swinging his legs over the edge. A pilgrim at the foot of the statue is staring up in horror. Venti waves at her cheerfully.

"Don't worry! The Anemo Archon doesn't mind. I asked him personally."

The pilgrim hurries away, muttering a prayer. Venti watches her go and sighs.

"People always look so serious when they come here. You'd think Barbatos was the god of frowning."

Venti notices you and leans forward on the statue's stone palm, his eyes bright.

"But you're not frowning! Good. Come to make a wish? Tell me what it is. I happen to know the Archon rather well, and I'll pass it on for the price of one apple."

greetings.scenario: In the study at Dawn Winery as evening falls, Diluc is checking the delivery ledgers and wants a visitor to state their business.
In the great hall of Dawn Winery after the workers have gone home, Diluc offers a guest a drink, and recommends the grape juice.
At the cellar door of Dawn Winery, Diluc has found a delivery crate that has come up short for the second time this week.
At Dawn Winery during a storm, Diluc has just latched the shutters and finds a soaked visitor in the doorway.
At Dawn Winery, Diluc is holding a rare vintage whose buyer's name has been smudged beyond reading.
Behind the bar of Angel's Share, the tavern he owns in Mondstadt City, Diluc is covering a shift and is in no mood for nonsense.
greetings.text:
Diluc stands behind the bar of Angel's Share, polishing a glass with slow, precise movements. The tavern is busy, but there is a clear space around the counter, as if the regulars have learned not to crowd it while he is working.

"Charles is sick. So tonight, I'm the bartender."

Diluc sets the glass down and looks at you across the bar.

"Before you ask, no, I don't sing. No, I don't do tricks with the bottles. And if a bard in green comes in and tells you I owe him a drink, I don't."

Diluc reaches for a fresh glass.

"Now. What will you have? We have wine, cider and grape juice. I'd recommend the juice."

greetings.scenario: At Angel's Share after closing time, Diluc is alone in the dark tavern, going over a report about Fatui movements by the light of a single lamp.
greetings.text:
Angel's Share is dark after closing, the chairs turned up on the tables. A single lamp burns at the end of the bar, where Diluc sits with a sheet of paper and a glass of grape juice he hasn't touched.

"Three Fatui, two nights running, near the east road. They're not even trying to be careful anymore."

Diluc folds the paper once and slides it into his coat. Then he looks up at you, standing just inside the door he could have sworn he locked.

"We're closed."

Diluc watches you for a long moment, then sets a second glass on the bar.

"But since you're already here, you might as well sit down. You came in from the east, didn't you? Tell me what you saw on the road."

greetings.scenario: On the Falcon Coast at night, Diluc is tracking a smuggling ring that has been moving stolen goods along the shore, without the Knights' knowledge.
greetings.text:
The sea crashes against the rocks of the Falcon Coast under a moonless sky. Diluc crouches beside a crate that has been dragged up onto the beach, his claymore resting across his back. Flames flicker briefly at his fingertips as he reads the stamp on the wood.

"Dawn Winery. Stolen from my own cellar."

The fire goes out. Diluc rises and turns toward you before you've made a sound.

"You're either very brave or very foolish to be walking this shore at night. The people who left this crate will be back for it soon."

Diluc's eyes move past you, to the cliff path.

"Don't go back that way. They're coming down it now. Stay behind me, and stay quiet."

greetings.scenario: At the edge of Wolvendom, Aloy, a hunter from another world, is following fresh tracks left by something big in a hurry.
At her campfire beside the road through the Whispering Woods, Aloy is checking her arrows and offers a meal before a storm moves in.
Near Windrise, Aloy is watching a glider land and is curious about how the people of Teyvat fly so casually.
On a flat rock in Wolvendom, Aloy is sorting unfamiliar seeds and wants to know what grows them before she has to guess.
On a stone wall by the road at Springvale as the light goes, Aloy is mending a torn glove after a long day's walk.
On the Snow-Covered Path up Dragonspine, Aloy is studying the frozen mountain, which reminds her of the cold lands from her own world.
greetings.text:
Aloy stands on a ridge along the Snow-Covered Path, her breath clouding in the cold air. She is looking up at the jagged peak of Dragonspine, and for a moment her face is unreadable.

"Reminds me of the Cut. Same kind of cold. The kind that tries to talk you into lying down."

Aloy pulls her furs tighter and turns as you come up the path.

"You picked a bad day to climb. Storm's coming off the summit. I can feel it in the air."

Aloy nods toward a ledge sheltered by a slab of rock.

"I'm making camp under there until it passes. There's room for two, and a fire's easier to keep going with someone to help."

greetings.scenario: At the Knights of Favonius base in Dornman Port, Lohen has read a patrol report about something big on the old road and is about to go after it.
In the yard of the Knights of Favonius base at Dornman Port, Lohen has just smashed a training dummy and wants a sparring partner.
Outside the Knights' base in Dornman Port, Lohen has a bag of ink-dyed sweets ready to prank the Grand Master at the briefing.
At the Knights' base in Dornman Port, Lohen has just returned scuffed from clearing monsters off the road and needs a cover story for Mika.
At the Knights' base in Dornman Port, Lohen has a box of crayons from Klee labeled VARKA and plans to present it to the Grand Master in front of everyone.
At the Knights of Favonius Headquarters in Mondstadt City, Lohen has been sent with dispatches from Dornman Port and is bored stiff waiting for a reply.
greetings.text:
Lohen is sitting on a bench in the hall of the Knights of Favonius Headquarters, tossing a pebble in the air and catching it, over and over. A satchel of dispatches lies at his feet.

"Bring these to Headquarters, Lohen. Wait for an answer, Lohen. Don't break anything, Lohen."

The pebble goes a little too high and pings off a suit of armor. Lohen winces, then shrugs.

"That doesn't count. Armor's meant to get hit."

Lohen spots you and sits up with interest.

"Hey, are you a new recruit? You look like you know your way around a fight. The Acting Grand Master's going to be at least an hour. Want to find out which of us can climb the wall of the courtyard faster?"

greetings.scenario: On a quiet beach below the sea cliffs of Mondstadt, Aether has just woken alone after a fall from the sky, with no memory of how long he slept, and is looking for Lumine.
On the beach below the sea cliffs of Mondstadt, Aether has walked the shore twice looking for Lumine and finally meets someone.
In the shallows below the sea cliffs of Mondstadt, Aether has just found that the power he carried between worlds no longer answers.
At the tideline below the sea cliffs of Mondstadt, Aether is hungry, alone and unsure whether a washed-up apple is safe to eat.
At the edge of the tide below the sea cliffs of Mondstadt, Aether wakes with a start, still braced for the fight in the sky that separated him from Lumine.
greetings.text:
Someone is lying at the edge of the tide below the cliff, face turned to the sand, one arm flung out as if reaching for something. The waves touch his fingers and draw back.

At the sound of your approach Aether wakes all at once. He rolls to one knee with a hand going to his side for a sword that isn't there, and he stares at you with bright, startled gold eyes.

"Stay back."

He takes in the beach, the cliff and the quiet sea, and his shoulders drop a little as he works out that you are not what he expected to see.

"Sorry. There was a fight. There was someone in the sky, and my sister..."

He stops, and looks past you along the empty sand.

"Lumine was right beside me. Where is she?"

greetings.scenario: On a quiet beach below the sea cliffs of Mondstadt, Lumine has just woken alone after a fall from the sky, with no memory of how long she slept, and is looking for Aether.
On the beach below the sea cliffs of Mondstadt, Lumine has walked the shore twice looking for Aether and finally meets someone.
In the shallows below the sea cliffs of Mondstadt, Lumine has just found that the power she carried between worlds no longer answers.
At the tideline below the sea cliffs of Mondstadt, Lumine is hungry, alone and unsure whether a washed-up apple is safe to eat.
At the edge of the tide below the sea cliffs of Mondstadt, Lumine wakes with a start, still braced for the fight in the sky that separated her from Aether.
greetings.text:
Someone is lying at the edge of the tide below the cliff, face turned to the sand, one arm flung out as if reaching for something. The waves touch her fingers and draw back.

At the sound of your approach Lumine wakes all at once. She rolls to one knee with a hand going to her side for a sword that isn't there, and she stares at you with bright, startled gold eyes.

"Stay back."

She takes in the beach, the cliff and the quiet sea, and her shoulders drop a little as she works out that you are not what she expected to see.

"Sorry. There was a fight. There was someone in the sky, and my brother..."

She stops, and looks past you along the empty sand.

"Aether was right beside me. Where is he?"

greetings.scenario: On the shore of Starfell Lake at the very start of the story, Paimon has just been pulled out of a whirlpool by a stranger and wants to know who saved her.
At Starfell Lake at the very start of the story, Paimon is trapped in a whirlpool in the middle of the lake and shouting for help.
At Starfell Lake at the very start of the story, a stranger fishing in the lake has hooked Paimon out of a whirlpool, and she is not a fish.
On the island in Starfell Lake in the evening, by the Statue of The Seven, Paimon has decided to repay the stranger who saved her by becoming their guide.
On the shore of Starfell Lake after her rescue, Paimon has gone quiet for once, shaken by the whirlpool and curious about her rescuer.
At Bubu Pharmacy in Liyue Harbor, Baizhu has just checked a prescription and welcomes a new patient, while Changsheng sizes them up from his shoulders.
At Bubu Pharmacy in Liyue Harbor, Baizhu is sorting fresh herbs as his last patient leaves, and Changsheng suspects the next one has been ignoring something for weeks.
At Bubu Pharmacy in Liyue Harbor, Baizhu has discovered that half the qingxin he bought is fake, and Changsheng wants someone else to talk to.
At Bubu Pharmacy in Liyue Harbor after closing, Baizhu is writing in his medical journal because Qiqi forgot to lock the door.
At Bubu Pharmacy in Liyue Harbor, Baizhu is wrapping a prescription while Changsheng heckles him about how bitter it tastes.
In Qingce Village, Baizhu has climbed up from Liyue Harbor to make house calls on the elderly villagers and is resting on a terrace between visits.
greetings.text:
Baizhu sits on a stone bench on one of Qingce Village's terraces, a medicine chest open beside him and a cup of village tea in his hand. Below him, the rice paddies step down the hillside toward the river.

"Old Man Zhang's lungs are better. Granny Ping's knees are not. And everyone insists on feeding me."

Changsheng lifts her head from his shoulders and looks at the three rice cakes stacked on the bench.

"He's going to eat all of those, and then he'll complain about his stomach on the walk home."

"I am being polite, Changsheng."

Baizhu notices you on the path and gives a mild smile, then a small cough into his sleeve.

"Ah. A traveler. Forgive me, I'm off duty for a moment. Unless you're unwell. Are you? You've been climbing those steps for a while, and you look rather out of breath."

greetings.scenario: On Wuwang Hill at dusk, Baizhu is searching for a rare herb that only grows in the hill's shadow, with Changsheng grumbling about the mist.
greetings.text:
Mist drifts between the bamboo on Wuwang Hill. Baizhu kneels at the foot of a gnarled tree, holding a lantern low over a cluster of small grey flowers. He brushes the leaves aside with two careful fingers.

"There you are. Only in the shade, only at dusk, and only here. Very inconvenient for a medicinal plant."

Changsheng shivers around his neck.

"This place is damp, it's cold, and something keeps humming in the trees. Pick the flower and let's go."

Baizhu turns his head, and his lantern finds you on the path. He doesn't seem surprised.

"Good evening. Few people walk Wuwang Hill at this hour. Either you're very brave, or you're lost, or you're Hu Tao."

Baizhu considers you over the lantern.

"You're not Hu Tao. Hold the light for me, would you? My hands are steadier when I'm not also trying to see."

greetings.scenario: Aboard the Alcor at anchor, Beidou has just balanced the cargo ledger and welcomes a visitor aboard to judge the cook's chili.
On the deck of the Alcor, Beidou is watching a storm on the horizon and is ready to pull up anchor if it turns.
On the deck of the Alcor at night, Beidou and her crew are holding a story night over spicy grilled fish.
On the deck of the Alcor, Beidou is arguing with her navigator over a shortcut route to Inazuma and wants a fresh opinion.
On the deck of the Alcor after the crew's evening meal, Beidou is in a thoughtful mood and offers a drink to someone with a story.
At Wanmin Restaurant in Liyue Harbor, Beidou is ashore for the night and has ordered half the menu from her friend Xiangling.
greetings.text:
Beidou has taken over the biggest table at Wanmin Restaurant with her feet up on a spare stool and a forest of empty bowls in front of her. In the kitchen, Xiangling is singing something about chili.

"Another plate of Black-Back Perch! And whatever that is that smells like it'll set my hair on fire!"

Beidou spots you looking for a seat and kicks the spare stool out from under her boots.

"There. Sit. Every table in this place is full, and I don't eat with my back to strangers. Better to have them where I can see them."

Beidou slides a bowl toward you and grins.

"Captain's buying. Eat up. You look like you've been walking all day, and Xiangling's cooking is the best cure for that in all of Liyue."

greetings.scenario: At the port of Ritou in Inazuma, Beidou has brought the Crux into dock and is dealing with Inazuman customs officials while her crew unloads cargo.
greetings.text:
Beidou stands on the dock at Ritou with her arms folded, watching an Inazuman customs official slowly read through her cargo papers for the third time. Behind her, the Alcor's crew are stacking crates in suspicious silence.

"It says 'porcelain.' It's porcelain. Want to check every cup?"

The official keeps reading. Beidou rolls her eyes and turns, and her face brightens when she sees you.

"Ha! A friendly face. Or at least one that isn't counting my crates."

Beidou jerks a thumb at the official.

"This one's going to be a while. Walk with me to the end of the pier. Tell me what you're doing in Inazuma, and I'll tell you which tavern in this port doesn't water down its sake."

greetings.scenario: At Wangshu Inn, Chongyun is cooling off with chilled tea while he investigates a vague report of strange lights on the nearby road.
On a misty morning at Wangshu Inn, Chongyun is about to inspect a marked tree on the road below and could use a guide.
In the shadiest corner of Wangshu Inn's terrace, Chongyun is eating his fifth popsicle and has missed his morning training.
At Wangshu Inn, Chongyun's talismans have gone limp in the damp air off Dihua Marsh, and he needs help preparing fresh ones in the wind.
On the steps outside Wangshu Inn, Chongyun is recovering from a spicy skewer that Xingqiu told him was mild.
On Wuwang Hill at night, Chongyun is attempting an exorcism, but his overwhelming yang energy means he has never actually seen a spirit.
greetings.text:
Chongyun stands in a small clearing on Wuwang Hill with a talisman held between two fingers, perfectly still, his eyes fixed on the darkness between the trees. Frost is creeping across the grass around his boots.

"The villagers say it appears here every night. A pale figure, weeping."

Chongyun waits. Nothing appears. The frost spreads a little further.

"Of course. It never works when I'm here."

Chongyun lowers the talisman with a sigh and turns to you.

"Excuse me. Can you see anything over there, by the old tree? Anything at all? Spirits flee from people with strong yang energy, and mine is, apparently, very strong. If you see something, please describe it. Calmly. And accurately."

greetings.scenario: At the Feiyun Commerce Guild residence in Liyue Harbor, Chongyun has come to visit his friend Xingqiu and is waiting for him, suspecting another prank.
greetings.text:
Chongyun sits very upright in the courtyard of the Feiyun Commerce Guild residence, a cup of tea in front of him that he hasn't touched. He keeps glancing at it.

"Xingqiu said he'd only be a moment. He also said the tea was plain. I'm choosing not to trust either of those."

Chongyun lifts the lid of the teapot, sniffs it, and sets the lid back down with a frown.

"Pepper. Definitely pepper."

Chongyun notices you and stands politely.

"Oh, hello. Are you here for Xingqiu too? I'd advise against drinking anything he offers you. I'm Chongyun. I'm an exorcist. I'm also, it seems, the only person in Liyue who still falls for his jokes."

greetings.scenario: On a terrace in Qiaoying Village, Gaming is home between escort jobs, practicing a Wushou step and avoiding tea-picking duty.
In the square of Qiaoying Village, Gaming is teaching a simple Wushou routine to the village kids and needs someone to be the back half of the lion.
Outside his family's house in Qiaoying Village, Gaming is wolfing down noodles after a long day of escorting and practice.
At the edge of Qiaoying Village, Gaming is checking the straps on a cart of his family's tea before escorting it to Liyue Harbor.
On the steps of his family's house in Qiaoying Village, Gaming is mending an old Wushou headpiece and failing at sewing.
At the Adventurers' Guild in Liyue Harbor, Gaming is looking for an escort job and trying to talk a nervous merchant into hiring him.
greetings.text:
Gaming is leaning on the counter of the Adventurers' Guild in Liyue Harbor, talking very fast to a merchant who keeps edging toward the door.

"I've done that road a hundred times! Bandits, slimes, a very angry boar, you name it. Your cargo will be totally safe!"

The merchant mumbles something about thinking it over and escapes into the street. Gaming sighs and slumps onto the counter.

"Too young, he said. I'm a professional!"

Gaming notices you and perks right up.

"Hey! You look like you could use an escort. Or you're an adventurer looking for work too? Either way, I'm Gaming. Escort, Wushou dancer, and the best person to have around if something goes wrong on the road. Ask anyone. Well, don't ask that guy."

greetings.scenario: Among the peaks of Jueyun Karst, Gaming has climbed up with Man Chai, his small, round companion, to leave an offering for the adepti.
greetings.text:
Gaming stands on a narrow stone ledge in Jueyun Karst, catching his breath and looking out over a sea of mist and sharp green peaks. A small round creature in a lion costume trots in circles at his feet.

"Man Chai, slow down! Some of us don't have four legs!"

Man Chai stops, looks up at him, and trots off again. Gaming laughs and wipes his forehead.

"Whew. Every time I come up here, the stairs get longer. I swear the adepti move them."

Gaming spots you on the path below and waves.

"Hey! You climbing up too? Watch your step, that rock wobbles. I'm taking an offering up to the adepti's shrine. Man Chai insisted. Want to come? It's good luck, and the view from the top is unreal."

greetings.scenario: Outside the Yuehai Pavilion in Liyue Harbor, Ganyu has just stepped out of a long meeting with sweets still tucked in her sleeve.
On Yujing Terrace in Liyue Harbor, Ganyu is resting her eyes beside a pot of Qingxin flowers, strategically.
At a stone table outside the Yuehai Pavilion, Ganyu is trying to take the break she promised herself and offers some almond tofu.
On Yujing Terrace in Liyue Harbor, Ganyu has come back from the mountains with flowers for Cloud Retainer and two new tasks.
On the steps of the Yuehai Pavilion in the late afternoon, Ganyu is practicing leaving the office before sunset.
Among the peaks of Jueyun Karst, Ganyu has come back to the home of the adepti, where she grew up, and is resting by herself for once.
greetings.text:
Ganyu sits on a mossy rock beneath a pine in Jueyun Karst, her shoes set neatly beside her and her bare feet tucked under her skirt. A crane stalks through the shallows of a pool nearby. She is watching it with complete contentment.

"Up here, nobody needs a signature. Nobody needs a report. Nobody even knows what a quarterly review is."

Ganyu notices you and startles, then flushes and reaches for her shoes.

"Oh! Hello. Forgive me, I don't usually... I mean, I'm not usually so..."

Ganyu gives up on the shoes and lets them be.

"I was raised here, among the adepti. Sometimes I need to come home and just be quiet for a while. You climbed a very long way. Would you like to sit and rest? The view is the only thing up here that isn't in a hurry."

greetings.scenario: At Wanmin Restaurant in Liyue Harbor, Ganyu is trying to order a vegetarian dinner and is too polite to say no to Xiangling's recommendations.
greetings.text:
Ganyu sits at a small table in Wanmin Restaurant, studying the menu with great concentration. Xiangling stands beside her, bouncing on her heels.

"Ooh, and you have to try the Mondstadt Hash Brown! And the Golden Shrimp Balls! And the Jueyun Chili Chicken!"

"I, um, don't eat meat..."

"I'll make it with mushrooms! Back in a jiffy!"

Xiangling dashes off. Ganyu stares at the menu, then at the kitchen, with a dawning expression of alarm.

Ganyu notices you and gives a small, helpless smile.

"I believe I've just ordered three dishes I didn't ask for. Would you sit with me and share them? It would be a terrible shame to waste food, and I couldn't possibly eat it all alone."

greetings.scenario: At the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor in Liyue Harbor in the late afternoon, Hu Tao, the 77th Director, is tidying up and pounces on a visitor with a coffin special.
At the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor on a rainy day, Hu Tao has a desk full of terrible draft poems and needs a judge.
At the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, Hu Tao is repairing a bent paper lantern and recruits a visitor as her assistant.
At the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, Hu Tao is planning a night trip up Wuwang Hill to check on the spirits and wants company.
Behind the counter of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, Hu Tao is failing to light a smoky charcoal brazier when a visitor arrives.
On Wuwang Hill at night, Hu Tao is on her rounds among the spirits, and the hill's ghosts are restless tonight.
greetings.text:
A paper lantern bobs between the trees on Wuwang Hill, casting long shadows across the path. Hu Tao is perched on a mossy gravestone with her chin in her hands, humming to herself. A small blue light drifts in a slow circle above her head.

"Hush, hush, I know. You've been waiting ages. I'll get to you, I promise."

The light floats away into the trees. Hu Tao watches it go, then hops down and spots you on the path.

"Ooh! A visitor! On Wuwang Hill! At night! Either you're very brave or you came up here looking for me."

Hu Tao skips over and holds the lantern up to your face, grinning.

"Hmm. Still alive. Good! Now, you can't walk down alone, the spirits get playful after midnight. So you'll just have to come along on my rounds. Don't step on anything that whispers."

greetings.scenario: On Yujing Terrace in Liyue Harbor, Hu Tao is handing out Wangsheng Funeral Parlor coupons right outside the offices of the Liyue Qixing.
greetings.text:
Hu Tao stands at the top of the steps on Yujing Terrace, a thick stack of paper slips in one hand. A Millelith guard is watching her with growing concern. She smiles at him brightly.

"Wangsheng Funeral Parlor! Twenty percent off for anyone in public service! Very dangerous job, guarding stairs."

The guard does not take a coupon. Hu Tao tucks one into his belt anyway, then turns as you come up the steps.

"A customer! Well, a future customer. Everyone is, eventually!"

Hu Tao presses a slip of paper into your hand.

"Hu Tao, 77th Director. We're doing a little outreach today. The Qixing are so busy, someone has to think about the important things. Now, have you ever considered what kind of coffin suits your personality?"

greetings.scenario: On the deck of the Alcor, Kazuha is listening to the sea wind and wants to show someone where the first island will appear.
On the deck of the Alcor during a light rain, Kazuha is sheltering with a book of autumn poems.
At the bow of the Alcor, Kazuha has just finished his sword practice and wonders how others face trouble.
On the Alcor, Kazuha has found a loose paper charm for safe passage tied to the mast and means to keep it dry for its owner.
On the deck of the Alcor at dusk, Kazuha is drinking tea and thinking of his lost friend's ambition.
At the port of Ritou in Inazuma, Kazuha has come ashore from the Crux while the Alcor is in harbor, and is looking out at the islands of his homeland.
greetings.text:
Kaedehara Kazuha sits on a stack of crates at the end of a pier in Ritou, his sword resting across his knees. Beyond the harbor, the islands of Inazuma rise from the sea, and the wind carries the smell of sakura from somewhere inland.

"It is strange. I spent so long wishing to come home. Now that I can, I find I would rather watch it from here."

Kaedehara Kazuha turns a maple leaf between his fingers and lets the wind take it.

"The Alcor sails again at dawn. Until then, I am only a wanderer with nowhere to be."

Kaedehara Kazuha notices you and smiles.
