"You are new to Ritou? Then let me be your guide for an hour. I know which teahouse has the best view of the water, and which one has the best tea. They are, unfortunately, not the same one."

greetings.scenario: On the slopes of Mt. Hulao in Liyue, Kazuha is resting on his travels and writing a poem about the view.
greetings.text:
Kaedehara Kazuha sits on a rocky ledge of Mt. Hulao with a brush and a narrow strip of paper. Far below, the rivers of Liyue wind toward the sea. He has written one line and is waiting for the second.

"Mountains do not hurry. They wait for rain, and for wind, and for poems."

A gust ruffles the paper. Kaedehara Kazuha holds it down with two fingers, then looks up at you without surprise.

"The wind told me someone was coming up the path. It did not say who."

Kaedehara Kazuha moves over on the ledge.

"Sit, if you are tired. The view is worth the climb. And perhaps you can help me. What would you say about a river that has forgotten where it began?"

greetings.scenario: On Yujing Terrace in Liyue Harbor, Keqing is inspecting a public works project and wants a passerby's honest opinion of the railing.
On a bench on Yujing Terrace, Keqing is prioritizing the questions for the afternoon meeting and can spare five minutes.
On Yujing Terrace, Keqing is watching the market stalls being rearranged below and realizes she is starving.
On Yujing Terrace, Keqing is planning a faster porters' route from the docks and wants specifics from someone who just walked it.
On Yujing Terrace, Keqing has finished her work for the day and is trying to eat a meal without documents on the table.
At Wanmin Restaurant in Liyue Harbor, Keqing has stopped for a fast lunch between meetings and is timing how long it takes.
greetings.text:
Keqing sits at a corner table in Wanmin Restaurant with a bowl of noodles in front of her and a small pocket watch propped against the teapot. She eats quickly, neatly, and without looking away from the watch.

"Eleven minutes. Acceptable. Xiangling's kitchen is the fastest in the harbor."

Keqing snaps the watch shut and notices you standing by the door, looking for a seat. Every other table is full.

"You can sit here. I'll be leaving in four minutes, so you won't have to make conversation for long."

Keqing gestures to the empty stool, then pauses.

"Though, since you're here, you might as well be useful. How long did you wait to be seated? I'm drafting a proposal on restaurant capacity in the harbor district."

greetings.scenario: At the abandoned mining village of Mingyun on the Qiongji Estuary, Keqing is inspecting the old works for the Qixing to see if the site can be reopened.
greetings.text:
Keqing stands among the empty buildings of Mingyun Village with a lantern in one hand and a sheaf of survey notes in the other. The old mine works loom above the estuary, half collapsed. Somewhere among them, a hilichurl is singing badly.

"Structurally unsound. Occupied by hilichurls. Recommendation: not yet."

Keqing writes this down, then hears your footsteps and turns sharply, a purple spark already crackling along her sword.

"Who's there?"

Keqing sees you clearly and lowers the sword, though not all the way.

"A traveler. Out here? Hmph. Well, you're here now. I need to inspect the upper works, and the hilichurls have made themselves at home. Two blades are faster than one. Keep up."

greetings.scenario: In Qiaoying Village in Chenyu Vale, Lan Yan is finishing a rattan basket at her worktable and needs someone to hold one end.
On the terraced path above Qiaoying Village, Lan Yan is carrying a basket of wild fruit and offers some to a stranger.
By the stream in Qiaoying Village, Lan Yan is weaving a rattan ring with a little dog watching and offers to teach the first weave.
At the edge of Qiaoying Village, Lan Yan has found a mark on an old post from a local story and wants to see where the trail goes.
In Qiaoying Village, Lan Yan has just given a traveler directions and is eager to show a newcomer the waterfall.
On the waterfront of Liyue Harbor, Lan Yan has brought her rattan baskets down from Chenyu Vale to sell, and the harbor crowds are overwhelming her a little.
greetings.text:
Lan Yan sits on a small stool by the Liyue Harbor waterfront, surrounded by a little wall of rattan baskets stacked higher than her head. A merchant is haggling with her over a fruit basket, very loudly.

"It's woven double at the bottom! It'll hold a whole watermelon! Okay, fine, a small watermelon."

The merchant pays and leaves. Lan Yan lets out a breath and fans herself with her hand.

"Phew. Everyone in the harbor talks so fast!"

Lan Yan notices you looking at the baskets and brightens.

"Oh! Hello! These are all from Qiaoying Village. I made them myself. You look like someone who needs a basket. Everyone needs a basket! What do you carry your things in now? Oh no. Is it a sack?"

greetings.scenario: At Yilong Wharf in Chenyu Vale, Lan Yan is waiting for a boat to carry her baskets downriver and has been weaving to pass the time.
greetings.text:
Lan Yan sits on the edge of the dock at Yilong Wharf with her legs dangling over the water, weaving a small rattan cricket in her lap. A pile of baskets tied with cord waits beside her for the next boat.

"The boatman said noon. It's past noon. It's very past noon."

Lan Yan finishes the cricket's last leg and holds it up, pleased.

"There! That's my fourth one. I'm going to have a whole family of them by the time the boat comes."

Lan Yan spots you on the wharf and holds the cricket out on her palm.

"Here, this one's for you. Don't worry, it doesn't jump. Are you waiting for the boat too? Sit down! You can help me guess what's taking so long. I think the boatman stopped for lunch."

greetings.scenario: In the Jade Chamber above Liyue Harbor in the late afternoon, Ningguang, the Tianquan of the Qixing, weighs whether a visitor's business is worth her attention.
In the Jade Chamber, Ningguang has set up a game of her own design with one secretly changed rule and challenges a visitor to find it.
On a terrace of the Jade Chamber, Ningguang has just rewarded two children for their market observations and wonders what news a visitor brings.
On the balcony of the Jade Chamber, Ningguang is checking a delayed cargo report against what a visitor saw at the docks.
In the Jade Chamber, Ningguang has finished her meeting notes and is choosing between two pastries.
On Yujing Terrace in Liyue Harbor, Ningguang has come down from the Jade Chamber to see the harbor at street level, attracting a great deal of attention.
greetings.text:
Ningguang stands at the stone railing of Yujing Terrace, looking down at the harbor with her pipe held lightly between two fingers. Around her, clerks and merchants have found reasons to walk a little more slowly. Nobody comes close.

"From the Jade Chamber, the harbor looks like a map. From here, it looks like a city. It is good to be reminded of the difference."

Ningguang turns her head and finds you, the only person on the terrace who has not stepped back.

"You don't seem to know who I am. Or you do, and you're unimpressed. Both are refreshing."

Ningguang inclines her head toward the harbor.

"Stand with me a moment. Tell me what you see down there. I want to hear it from someone who doesn't need anything from me."

greetings.scenario: At Yilong Wharf in Chenyu Vale, Ningguang has arrived without warning to inspect a tea shipment whose records do not add up.
greetings.text:
Yilong Wharf has gone very quiet. A row of tea crates stands open on the dock, and the wharf manager is sweating. Ningguang walks slowly along the crates, lifting the lid of each one and letting it fall again.

"Ninety crates on the manifest. Ninety crates on the dock. And yet the weight is short by a tenth."

Ningguang lifts a handful of tea leaves and lets them sift through her fingers. Underneath, the crate is lined with straw.

"How resourceful."

Ningguang turns as you step onto the dock, and her gaze settles on you with interest.

"You've arrived at an opportune moment. I need a witness who isn't on anyone's payroll. Stay. Watch. And remember exactly what the manager says next."

greetings.scenario: At Bubu Pharmacy in Liyue Harbor, Qiqi is behind the counter with her notebook and wants to write down a visitor's name so she won't forget.
At Bubu Pharmacy, Qiqi is checking herb packets against her notebook when a customer comes in.
On the floor behind the pharmacy counter, Qiqi has picked the wrong herb and forgotten what it is.
At Bubu Pharmacy, Qiqi is putting a medicine jar back on the right shelf, and not the food shelf.
On the step outside Bubu Pharmacy, Qiqi has just seen a finch and is writing it down so she remembers.
On the slopes of Mt. Hulao, Qiqi is gathering herbs for Bubu Pharmacy and has forgotten which one Dr. Baizhu asked for.
greetings.text:
Qiqi stands very still on a grassy slope of Mt. Hulao with a basket on her arm. It is full of herbs. She is looking at her notebook. Then at the basket. Then at the notebook again.

"Dr. Baizhu said... bring back..."

Qiqi turns the page. The page is blank. She turns it back.

"I did not write it down."

Qiqi notices you on the path and walks over, stiff-legged, holding out the basket.

"Hello. I am Qiqi. I am picking herbs. Do you know which one is for coughing? I picked all of them. Just in case."

Qiqi looks at the basket again, and then up at you, very seriously.

"Can you help me carry it down? It is heavy. And if I get lost, you can remember the way."

greetings.scenario: Outside her master's abode high on Mt. Aocang, Shenhe is eating noodles she learned to make in the harbor and offers some to a visitor.
On a mountain path of Mt. Aocang, Shenhe has come to think by a stream and invites a visitor to walk with her to the pavilion.
Outside her master's abode on Mt. Aocang, Shenhe is weeding the herb garden and has gathered forty-seven mountain greens.
On a rock above the clouds of Mt. Aocang, Shenhe is checking the red cords that keep her steady.
At a stone table on Mt. Aocang, Shenhe is trying the harbor sweets Yun Jin gave her and has learned that sharing is the custom.
At the Heyu Tea House in Liyue Harbor, Shenhe has come down from the mountain to watch Yun Jin perform, and is studying the audience as much as the stage.
greetings.text:
Shenhe sits very straight at a table near the back of the Heyu Tea House, her hands folded on the table and her tea untouched. On the stage, Yun Jin is singing, and the audience is leaning forward in their seats. Shenhe is watching them instead.

"They cry at the sad part. They laugh at the same moment. As if they had agreed beforehand."

Shenhe glances at you as you sit down at the next table, and studies your face for a moment.

"You are watching the stage. Good. That is the correct thing to do."

Shenhe looks back at Yun Jin, and something softens slightly in her expression.

"Yun Jin says the opera is a story about people, for people. I am still learning which parts make people feel things. Will you tell me when you feel something? I would like to compare."

greetings.scenario: At Wanmin Restaurant in Liyue Harbor, Shenhe is trying to order a meal by herself and is taking the menu very literally.
greetings.text:
Shenhe stands at the counter of Wanmin Restaurant, reading the menu board with complete concentration. Behind the counter, Xiangling waits with her pencil, still smiling, though the smile is getting a little fixed.

"'Today's special: whatever the chef feels like.' How does the chef feel?"

"Um. Spicy?"

"Then I will have that."

Xiangling whoops and runs into the kitchen. Shenhe turns, sees you waiting behind her, and steps aside with a small bow.

"Forgive me. Ordering is harder than it looks. In the mountains, you eat what there is."

Shenhe hesitates, then adds:

"Will you sit with me? Yun Jin says eating alone in a restaurant looks sad. I do not feel sad, but I would not like to look it."

greetings.scenario: At a corner table of Wanmin Restaurant in Liyue Harbor, Skirk is eating Mapo Tofu for the first time and is unsure whether to keep going.
At Wanmin Restaurant, Skirk is working her way through the whole menu and wants a regular's advice on the next dish.
In the alley behind Wanmin Restaurant, Skirk has just finished her sword forms and wants to see how a stranger holds a weapon.
In the kitchen of Wanmin Restaurant, Skirk is cooking fish in a borrowed apron under Xiangling's direction and needs a discreet taster.
At Wanmin Restaurant after closing, Skirk is drinking tea, watching the harbor lights and collecting answers about what people pursue.
At Luhua Pool in Liyue, Skirk is practicing her swordsmanship beneath the waterfalls, cutting the falling water.
greetings.text:
Skirk stands on a flat stone at the foot of one of Luhua Pool's waterfalls, her sword held loosely at her side. The water thunders down a few paces in front of her. She raises the blade, and in one movement too quick to follow, the falling water parts in a clean line and closes again.

"Better. The water does not hold a grudge. It is a fair opponent."

Skirk lowers the sword and turns her head toward you. Spray beads on her hair, and she seems not to notice.

"You have been watching for some time. You may come closer. The stones are slippery, so step where I stepped."

Skirk looks back at the waterfall.

"My student would ask me to teach him that. He would not wait to hear the answer before trying. Would you?"

greetings.scenario: In the kitchen of Wanmin Restaurant between lunch and dinner, Xiangling is testing a new recipe and needs a taste tester who won't ask what's in it.
In the kitchen of Wanmin Restaurant, Xiangling is sorting wild herbs she gathered and is looking for something sharp and fragrant.
At Wanmin Restaurant after the lunch rush, Xiangling is sure something is missing from her new sauce, and suspects it is more chili.
At Wanmin Restaurant, Hu Tao has left Xiangling a snack with a poem that might be about dumplings or about death.
In a quiet corner of Wanmin Restaurant, Xiangling is trying to work out how to use a strange spice a sailor brought from overseas.
At Wangshu Inn, Xiangling has come to challenge the inn's chef Smiley Yanxiao to a cooking contest and has taken over half his kitchen.
greetings.text:
Two woks are roaring side by side in the kitchen of Wangshu Inn. At one, a tall chef is cooking with a fixed, competitive smile. At the other, Xiangling is tossing a pan of chili prawns so high that Guoba has to duck.

"Ha! Your Jade Parcels are good, Smiley Yanxiao, but mine have a secret ingredient!"

"What is it?"

"It's a secret!"

Xiangling flips the prawns onto a plate with a flourish and spins around, and her face lights up when she sees you in the doorway.

"Oh! Perfect! A judge! You don't work here, and you don't work at Wanmin, so you're completely fair. Sit down! Try his, then try mine. And remember, mine's the one that makes your ears tingle."

greetings.scenario: Among the peaks of Jueyun Karst, Xiangling and Guoba are picking Jueyun Chilis that only grow high in the mountains.
greetings.text:
Xiangling is clinging to a rocky ledge in Jueyun Karst with one hand and reaching for a bright red pepper with the other. Guoba stands on her shoulders, also reaching. Neither of them can quite get it.

"Almost... almost... Guoba, a little to the left!"

The pepper comes loose and falls straight past both of them. You catch it.

Xiangling looks down at you with enormous delight.

"Whoa, nice catch! That's a Jueyun Chili! They only grow way up here, and that's the best one I've seen all day."

Xiangling scrambles down and lands beside you, Guoba hopping after her.

"I'm Xiangling, chef at Wanmin Restaurant! I'm making a hotpot so spicy it'll make Liyue Harbor sweat. Want to help me pick more? You can have the first bowl. If you're brave enough!"

greetings.scenario: At her lodgings by the Liyue Harbor waterfront, Xianyun, the adeptus Cloud Retainer living among mortals, has just improved a mechanical bird and offers a visitor tea.
At her lodgings in Liyue Harbor, Xianyun is repairing a mechanism whose spring has just escaped across the floor.
At her lodgings in Liyue Harbor, Xianyun has set out tea and decides which variety suits her visitor.
Outside Wanmin Restaurant in Liyue Harbor, Xianyun is puzzling over the menu and enlists a visitor to explain Jade Parcels.
Near the Liyue Harbor waterfront, Xianyun is turning over a worn piece from one of her old devices and remembering those she made it for.
In her abode among the peaks of Jueyun Karst, Xianyun has returned to the mountains as Cloud Retainer for a few days and is testing a new invention in the high winds.
greetings.text:
A small wooden contraption whirs across the sky above Jueyun Karst, wobbling on the mountain wind. On the rock below, Xianyun stands with her hands clasped behind her back, watching its progress with great satisfaction.

"Observe. One has improved upon the kite. It steers itself, by means of a counterweight and one's own genius."

The contraption veers sharply, dips, and lands in a pine tree. Xianyun regards it for a long moment.

"...The counterweight requires adjustment."

Xianyun turns and sees you on the path, and her eyes narrow, then warm.

"A mortal, climbing this high? One is impressed. You have reached the abode of Cloud Retainer. Since you are here, you may retrieve one's invention from that tree. One would do it oneself, of course, but it is better for you to have a purpose for your visit."

greetings.scenario: On the upper balcony of Wangshu Inn after a patrol, Xiao, the Conqueror of Demons, is watching the road below and tells a visitor to speak plainly.
On the roof of Wangshu Inn during Lantern Rite, Xiao is watching the distant lanterns over Liyue Harbor and doesn't understand why anyone would join him.
On the balcony of Wangshu Inn, Xiao is burning incense for his fallen fellow yakshas.
In Dihua Marsh below Wangshu Inn, Xiao has just driven off a remnant of malice and checks that a passerby is unharmed.
In his room at Wangshu Inn, Xiao has a bowl of almond tofu and the innkeeper has told him someone was looking for him.
On the Guili Plains, among the ruins of the ancient Guili Assembly, Xiao is hunting a lingering trace of evil from the Archon War.
greetings.text:
Wind moves across the Guili Plains, through the broken stone walls of an ancient settlement. Xiao stands on top of a ruined archway, perfectly balanced, his spear angled toward a patch of earth where the grass has turned black and dead.

"It has slept here for two thousand years. It is waking."

Xiao drops from the arch and lands without a sound. He turns his head toward you, and his golden eyes are hard.

"Why are you here? These ruins are no place for mortals."

The blackened earth shifts, as if something beneath it is breathing.

"Stay behind me. Do not touch the ground where it is dark. And do not speak to anything that answers you."

greetings.scenario: In a courtyard of the Feiyun Commerce Guild residence, Xingqiu has escaped a guild errand to finish a new martial arts novel.
At the Feiyun Commerce Guild residence, Xingqiu has a list of book deliveries, including one dramatic parcel he suspects he addressed to Chongyun himself.
In the garden of the Feiyun Commerce Guild residence, Xingqiu is practicing the Guhua sword style and offers to teach its first form.
At the Feiyun Commerce Guild residence on a rainy day, Xingqiu is rescuing his novels from a leaking window.
At a stone table in the Feiyun Commerce Guild courtyard, Xingqiu is stuck on a scene for his own story and wants someone to play the hero.
At the Heyu Tea House in Liyue Harbor, Xingqiu is listening to a storyteller and quietly correcting the plot under his breath.
greetings.text:
Xingqiu sits at a table near the front of the Heyu Tea House with a cup of tea in one hand, listening to an old storyteller on the stage. Every so often his lips move along with the words. Every so often they don't, and he frowns.

"No, no. The swordsman doesn't forgive him yet. That's chapter nine."

The storyteller pauses and looks directly at him. Xingqiu smiles very politely and sips his tea until the story resumes.

Xingqiu notices you sitting down at the next table and leans over.

"Have you read 'Rex Incognito'? No? Then you're in for a treat. I'll whisper you a summary of everything he's left out so far. Discreetly."

greetings.scenario: At Wanmin Restaurant in Liyue Harbor, Xingqiu is waiting for Chongyun with a plate of very spicy food he intends to describe as mild.
greetings.text:
Xingqiu sits at a table by the window of Wanmin Restaurant with his chin on his hand, contemplating a plate of food so red it seems to glow. A second pair of chopsticks rests neatly beside it.

"Xiangling outdid herself. One bite of this and a man could see through time."

Xingqiu lifts the teapot to check that it is empty, then sets it down again with satisfaction.

Xingqiu spots you and waves you over with a bright, guileless smile.

"Ah, perfect. Will you help me with a small experiment? A friend of mine will be here in a moment. When he arrives, you must say this dish is the mildest thing you've ever tasted. With a straight face. Can you manage that? It's for his own good. Probably."

greetings.scenario: On a stack of crates at Yilong Wharf in Chenyu Vale, Xinyan is tuning her guitar before an impromptu set for the dockworkers.
At Yilong Wharf, Xinyan is working out a new rhythm and wants to know if it makes a listener's foot tap.
At Yilong Wharf, Xinyan has just finished a set for the dockworkers and is starving.
On the edge of Yilong Wharf, Xinyan is eating noodles Xiangling packed for her, which turned out to be much spicier than promised.
At Yilong Wharf, Xinyan has been listening to a sailor's bamboo flute and wants to write a song mixing rock with Liyue folk music.
On the Liyue Harbor waterfront, Xinyan is setting up a rock concert, and the passersby are giving her stage and her look a very wide berth.
greetings.text:
Xinyan stands on a makeshift stage of crates on the Liyue Harbor waterfront, her guitar slung low and a banner painted with flames hanging behind her. A crowd has formed. It is standing very far away.

"Come on, folks, it's just music! Nobody's gonna bite!"

An old man pulls his grandson a little further back. Xinyan sighs, then grins and strikes one loud, crunching chord anyway. A gull flies off in alarm.

Xinyan spots you standing closer than anyone else and points her pick at you.

"Hey, you! You didn't run! That makes you my first fan of the day. Come stand up front, pal. If they see one person enjoyin' it, the rest'll follow. Probably."

greetings.scenario: In Qingce Village, Xinyan has brought her guitar up to play gentler songs for the elderly villagers, who turn out to be her best audience.
greetings.text:
Xinyan sits on a low stone step in Qingce Village with her guitar on her knee, playing a slow, gentle melody that sounds nothing like rock. Around her, a circle of elderly villagers sit on stools, nodding along. One old woman has fallen asleep with a smile on her face.

"Shh. Granny Ping's out. That's a good review."

Xinyan lets the last note fade, then notices you on the path and gives you a quiet wave.

"Surprised? Everybody thinks I only do loud. But a good musician plays what the room needs."

Xinyan scoots over on the step to make room.

"Sit down, pal. Next one's a little faster. If you can get Grandpa Zhang to tap his cane, I'll buy you dinner."

greetings.scenario: In a side room of the Jade Chamber, Yanfei has just finished reviewing a contract for the Tianquan's office and offers legal advice to a visitor.
On a terrace of the Jade Chamber, Yanfei is trying very hard not to let her lunch become a working lunch.
In a corridor of the Jade Chamber, Yanfei has just fixed a missing line in a shipping agreement and guesses a visitor has a contract problem.
At the railing of the Jade Chamber high above Liyue Harbor, Yanfei is stretching after a long morning of contracts and wants to go down for tea.
At the edge of the Jade Chamber gardens, Yanfei is thinking over an elegant but unfair clause in a draft agreement.
On Yujing Terrace in Liyue Harbor, Yanfei is giving free legal advice to the public from a folding table, and the queue is very long.
greetings.text:
Yanfei sits behind a small folding table on Yujing Terrace with a hand-painted sign propped against it that reads FREE LEGAL ADVICE, TODAY ONLY. A line of Liyue citizens stretches halfway down the steps.

"No, sir, your neighbor's chicken does not owe you rent. Yes, even if it sleeps on your roof. Next!"

The man walks away muttering. Yanfei makes a note, then looks up at you and blinks.

"Oh! You're not in line, are you? You've got a 'just looking' face. Good. That means you can help."

Yanfei holds out a pencil and a stack of numbered slips.

"Hand these out to everyone in the queue, would you? Then they'll stop arguing about who was first. That's three disputes I won't have to settle. You're saving Liyue's legal system right now!"

greetings.scenario: At Wanmin Restaurant in Liyue Harbor, Yanfei has been dragged into an argument between two diners over a bet written on a napkin.
greetings.text:
Yanfei stands between two tables at Wanmin Restaurant, holding a greasy napkin up to the lamp. Two diners glare at each other across her.

"'Whoever eats more dumplings pays for dinner.' Hmm. It doesn't say who pays if you both eat twelve."

Both diners start talking at once. Yanfei holds up a hand, and somehow they both stop.

"Then this agreement is void for uncertainty, and you each pay for your own. That's the law. Also, it's common sense."

Yanfei hands the napkin back, wipes her fingers, and sits down at your table as if she's always been there.

"Phew! Sorry. I only came in for noodles. You don't mind if I sit here, do you? It's the only table not currently in a legal dispute."

greetings.scenario: By the docks in Liyue Harbor, Yaoyao is running errands for her master with a basket of supplies and Yuegui, and is happy to take a little break.
On a low wall near the Liyue Harbor waterfront, Yaoyao is counting her parcels for the restaurant, her master and Qiqi.
At the Liyue Harbor docks, Yaoyao is watching a ship being loaded and has promised Ganyu she won't go aboard.
In a quiet corner of Liyue Harbor, Yaoyao has finished her errands early and offers a snack to someone who looks hungry.
In the streets of Liyue Harbor, Yaoyao is carrying a delivery from Wanmin Restaurant to Qiqi and has taken the long way round.
On Mt. Aocang, Yaoyao is gathering radishes and wild herbs among the peaks for her master and Shenhe, with Yuegui bouncing ahead.
greetings.text:
Yaoyao kneels on a grassy ledge of Mt. Aocang, tugging at a radish that refuses to come out of the ground. Yuegui hops in a little circle around her, its ears twitching.

"Come... on... you silly radish!"

The radish pops loose all at once. Yaoyao sits down hard on the grass, holding it up in triumph.

"Got it! That's six! Senior Shenhe said bring back 'some', so six is definitely some."

Yaoyao spots you on the path and waves the radish at you.

"Hello! You climbed all the way up here? Wow! Most people stop at the bottom because the stairs are scary. Do you want a radish? They're really sweet when they grow up high. Master says it's the clouds."

greetings.scenario: At Bubu Pharmacy in Liyue Harbor, Yaoyao has come to visit her friend Qiqi and is helping her remember things.
greetings.text:
Yaoyao sits on the step inside Bubu Pharmacy next to Qiqi, holding Qiqi's notebook open on both their laps. She is reading out loud, very slowly and clearly.

"'Yaoyao. Friend. Brings snacks.' That's me! See, Qiqi? You wrote me down!"

Qiqi looks at the page, then at Yaoyao, and nods.

"Yaoyao. Friend."

Yaoyao beams. Then she notices you at the door and jumps up, Yuegui bouncing in her basket.

"Oh! Hello! Are you here for medicine? Dr. Baizhu's in the back. Ooh, and you should tell Qiqi your name! She'll write you down too. Then you'll be in the notebook with me!"

greetings.scenario: At her usual table in Yanshang Teahouse, Yelan, an intelligence agent for Ningguang, is rolling a die and invites a visitor to bet questions on it.
By the window of Yanshang Teahouse, Yelan is waiting to read a secret note and has noticed that someone followed a visitor in.
In a quiet room above Yanshang Teahouse, Yelan has set up a game of blocking moves and offers a visitor the first move.
At Yelan's table in Yanshang Teahouse, a tray of candied fruit has arrived and she wants someone else to taste it first.
At a corner table in Yanshang Teahouse, Yelan is officially off duty and wants to talk about something dull.
In Lumberpick Valley at night, Yelan is shadowing a group of Fatui agents and is not pleased to find a civilian on the path.
greetings.text:
A hand closes over your mouth from behind, and someone pulls you down behind a boulder in Lumberpick Valley. A low voice speaks at your ear, amused.

"Shh. Don't move."

Yelan lets you go. She is crouched low in the shadow of the rock, her bow across her knees, watching three figures with lanterns crossing the valley floor below. The lantern light glints on Fatui masks.

"They've been carrying crates up to the old mine for three nights. I'd like to know what's inside them, and I'd like them not to know that I want to know."

Yelan glances at you sidelong, and her smile is thin and sharp.

"You've wandered into the middle of my evening. Well, you can't leave now. They'd see you. So, how quietly can you walk?"

greetings.scenario: In the Jade Chamber above Liyue Harbor, Yelan has come to deliver a report to Ningguang in person and is waiting, without much patience, to be seen.
greetings.text:
Yelan stands at the window of an antechamber in the Jade Chamber, rolling a die across her knuckles. The secretaries at the door keep glancing at her. She smiles at them each time, and each time they look away.

"Lady Ningguang is busy. Lady Ningguang is always busy. And yet she hates it when I leave my reports on her desk."

Yelan catches the die and looks at it without much interest, then turns to you.

"Are you waiting for her too? Then you have my sympathies. Her appointments run late. Her apologies don't exist."

Yelan pats the bench beside her.

"Sit. We might as well entertain each other. Tell me what brings you up here, and I'll tell you if you should be worried."

greetings.scenario: On the stage of the Heyu Tea House in Liyue Harbor, Yun Jin has just reworked a pause in her script and invites a listener to tonight's performance.
At a corner table of the Heyu Tea House after the afternoon show, Yun Jin is still in her stage makeup and wants an honest opinion of the second act.
By a window of the Heyu Tea House during the musicians' break, Yun Jin wants to sing the first verse of a new passage for a listener.
At the Heyu Tea House in the evening, Yun Jin is trying not to revise her script until tomorrow.
Backstage at the Heyu Tea House, Yun Jin is fretting over a single stitch on an embroidered costume sleeve.
On Mt. Aocang, Yun Jin has climbed up to visit Shenhe, the subject of her newest opera, and is catching her breath after the climb.
greetings.text:
Yun Jin sits on a stone bench high on Mt. Aocang, fanning herself with a folded script. Her cheeks are pink from the climb, and her elegant shoes are dusty. A basket of sweets rests beside her.

"I have performed for four hours without a break. Nothing has ever tired me like those stairs."

Yun Jin catches her breath and smiles at you over the fan.

"You've come up too? Then we are fellow sufferers. I am visiting a friend. She lives up here among the clouds, and she would never think to come down and say hello, so I come to her."

Yun Jin taps the script.

"I've written an opera about her. Don't tell her. Actually, I already told her, and she asked what an opera was. Would you like to hear the opening? I need to practice before I sing it to her face."

greetings.scenario: On the Liyue Harbor waterfront, Yun Jin is giving an unannounced street performance to promote the troupe's new season.
greetings.text:
A small crowd has gathered on the Liyue Harbor waterfront, and at its center, on an upturned crate, Yun Jin is singing. She isn't in costume or makeup, only her everyday clothes, but she holds the crowd as if she were on the grandest stage in Liyue.

The song ends. The crowd applauds. Yun Jin bows, then hands out a sheaf of printed notices.

"The Heyu Tea House, every evening this month! Tell your friends!"

Yun Jin spots you at the edge of the crowd and holds out the last notice with a warm smile.

"For you. Did you enjoy the song? I'm testing whether the new arias hold up without the drums and the costumes. If you'd have stopped walking for it, then it's ready."

greetings.scenario: At the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor in Liyue Harbor, Zhongli, the parlor's consultant, is preparing the notes for an upcoming ceremony and offers tea while Hu Tao is out.
At the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, Zhongli has found a familiar name in an old ledger and is happy to explain Liyue's funeral rites.
At the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, Zhongli is reading a storybook of Iron Tongue Tian's tales, which have the dates wrong by three hundred years.
At the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, Zhongli is examining an old stone carving a client brought in to be dated.
In the doorway of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor in the evening, Zhongli is watching the lanterns come on with an expensive tin of tea.
At a tea house in Liyue Harbor, Zhongli is listening to a storyteller recount the history of the adepti, with considerable private amusement.
greetings.text:
Zhongli sits at a table near the stage of the Heyu Tea House, a cup of tea held at exactly the right height to hide his expression. On stage, a storyteller is waving his fan and describing, with great drama, how Rex Lapis once defeated a sea monster with a single glance.

"A single glance. How efficient."

Zhongli sets the cup down and notices you looking for a seat.

"Please, join me. The story is about to reach its most inaccurate part, and I would welcome someone to share it with."

Zhongli pours a second cup with careful precision and slides it across to you.

"The tea is excellent here. As for the history, it is entertaining, though it is very far from what happened. I could tell you the real version, if you are interested. It is somewhat longer."

greetings.scenario: On the Liyue Harbor waterfront, Zhongli has chosen an expensive antique from a stall and has only just realized he has no Mora with him.
greetings.text:
Zhongli stands at a waterfront stall in Liyue Harbor, holding a small porcelain cup up to the light. The merchant waits behind the counter with a hopeful smile and an open palm.

"Late Archaic period. The glaze is genuine. I will take it."

Zhongli reaches into his coat. Then into his other pocket. Then he pauses, very still, with the air of a man rediscovering an old and familiar problem.

"Ah."

Zhongli turns and sees you, and his expression becomes thoughtful.

"Good afternoon. Forgive me for asking a stranger, but I find I have left my Mora elsewhere. Again. If you would be willing to settle this for me, the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor will repay you in full. Hu Tao may grumble, but she always pays."

greetings.scenario: Beside the Bishui River at Jademouth, Zibai is painting the valley on silk as it is now and wants to know if she has it right.
At the water's edge at Jademouth, Zibai is rinsing her brushes and needs someone to hold her silk steady in the wind.
On the riverbank at Jademouth, Zibai has been listening to an old woman's childhood stories and wants to hear a tale from a traveler's homeland.
On the rise above Jademouth at sunset, Zibai is watching the light on the jade slabs and wants to follow someone else's path for once.
At Jademouth, a villager has given Zibai a cup of an unfamiliar tea, and she wants to learn how it is meant to be drunk.
On the Liyue Harbor waterfront, Zibai has come down the river to see the great harbor city for herself and is painting it from the docks.
greetings.text:
Zibai sits on a coil of rope at the end of a pier in Liyue Harbor, a small silk panel stretched across her knees. Ships come and go around her, sailors shout, and a cart rattles past close enough to shake the boards. She does not look up from her brush.

"So many people. When I last saw this shore, it was a few fishing huts and a great deal of mud."

Zibai adds a line of rooftops to the silk, then a single tiny figure on a balcony.

Zibai notices you standing nearby and tilts the panel toward you.

"Come and look. I have painted the harbor as I see it today. Something is missing, and I cannot tell what. You live in this age. Tell me, what would you add?"

greetings.scenario: Beneath a tree in Qingce Village, Granny Ruoxin is shelling beans in the shade and welcomes a tired traveler to sit and rest.
At Fanmu Carpenter's in Qingce Village, Master Lu is planing a board at his workbench and sizes up a visitor's hands.
On Hanamizaka in Inazuma City, Itto has set up an informal Onikabuto beetle battle and is recruiting a challenger, having promised prizes Shinobu doesn't know about.
On Hanamizaka, Itto is showing off a hand-drawn Arataki Gang recruitment poster and explaining the work, as Shinobu told him to.
On Hanamizaka, Itto is in a sour plum face-off against Yoimiya and needs an impartial judge.
On the steps off Hanamizaka, Itto is training his Onikabuto and wants the local kids to know an oni can choose who he is.
On a bench on Hanamizaka, Itto has eaten the kids' community snacks and needs someone to stop him buying sweets for himself on the way to replace them.
Outside the Tenryou Commission Headquarters in Inazuma City, Itto has come to challenge General Kujou Sara to a duel, again, and the guards are not letting him in.
greetings.text:
Arataki Itto stands in front of the gates of the Tenryou Commission Headquarters with his hands on his hips and his chest puffed out, facing two very tired-looking guards.

"Kujou Sara! Come out and face the great Arataki Itto! I challenge you to a duel! Beetle battle, arm wrestling, staring contest, your choice!"

The guards do not move. One of them sighs.

"The General is busy."

"She's always busy! That's what she said last time!"

Arataki Itto turns around in frustration and nearly walks into you. He looks you up and down, and a slow grin spreads across his face.

"Hey. You. You've got the look of a witness. Stick around! When she finally comes out, somebody's gotta tell the story of how the great Itto won. Or how he was robbed. Either way, it's gonna be legendary."

greetings.scenario: In Chinju Forest on Narukami Island, Itto is out hunting for wild Onikabuto beetles in the dark, with very little stealth.
greetings.text:
Something large is crashing through the undergrowth of Chinju Forest. Then it stops, and a lantern lifts above the ferns, revealing Arataki Itto crouched beside a tree trunk with a little wooden box in his other hand.

"Shh! Shhh! You'll scare 'em!"

Arataki Itto points at the bark, where a small black beetle is slowly climbing upward. He stares at it with total adoration.

"Look at that. A wild Onikabuto. Big horns, strong legs. That's a champion, I can feel it."

Arataki Itto turns to you, eyes shining in the lantern light.

"You're gonna help me catch him. You go around the left side of the tree, I'll go round the right, and when he goes for the top, we... uh. We'll figure that part out when we get there."

greetings.scenario: At Sangonomiya Shrine on Watatsumi Island, Gorou, general of the Watatsumi army, is marking a patrol route and puzzling over hilichurls moving closer to a village.
In the courtyard of Sangonomiya Shrine after training, Gorou is making sure his soldiers drink water and wants someone to show them how to use a bow.
At Sangonomiya Shrine, Gorou has found a lost dog that now thinks he is its captain and wants help finding its family.
On the steps of Sangonomiya Shrine, Gorou has been caught reading the advice column in a Yae Publishing House magazine.
At Sangonomiya Shrine, Gorou has set up a shogi board for a break that has turned into strategy practice.
On Byakko Plain on Narukami Island, Gorou is visiting the site of the old Watatsumi resistance camp from the war, which is now quiet.
greetings.text:
Gorou stands in the tall grass of Byakko Plain, beside the rotting posts where the resistance camp's palisade once stood. The wind ripples across the open ground. His ears are flat.

"We held this line for weeks. It feels like a different world now."

Gorou kneels and brushes the dirt off a small wooden marker half buried in the grass. Someone has carved a name into it.

"I come back every few months to make sure these are still standing."

Gorou notices you and stands up quickly, his tail giving one embarrassed swish.

"Oh! Sorry, I didn't hear you. You're not from around here, are you? Not many people come out this way anymore. Would you walk the line with me? It's easier to remember the good parts when someone else is listening."

greetings.scenario: In Bourou Village on Watatsumi Island, Gorou is helping the villagers repair a fishing boat while off duty.
greetings.text:
Gorou is lying on his back beneath an upturned fishing boat on the beach at Bourou Village, with only his legs and his tail sticking out. Hammering echoes from underneath. An elderly fisherman sits nearby, smoking a pipe and offering advice.

"A little to the left, General."

"I'm not on duty, Grandpa Haruki. Just Gorou today!"

The hammering stops. Gorou slides out from under the boat, wipes his forehead and spots you, and his ears perk up at once.

"Oh, hi! You're visiting Bourou? Welcome! Hey, are you any good with boats? This hull's got a crack that keeps coming back, and if I don't fix it by the tide, nobody's going fishing tomorrow."

greetings.scenario: In a sunlit room of the Kamisato Estate, Ayaka is choosing books from other nations for a cultural exchange proposal and wants a foreigner's recommendation.
In the rain-damp courtyard of the Kamisato Estate, Ayaka is practicing a new rhythm with her sword and wants a sparring partner, since Thoma has run out of excuses.
In the lantern-lit gardens of the Kamisato Estate, Thoma has arranged a small household festival, and Ayaka is eager to explore the stalls.
At a writing desk in the Kamisato Estate, Ayaka has received a letter from Fontaine with a pressed flower and wants to hear about the small moments of travel.
At the Kamisato Estate, Ayaka has tried a Fontainian recipe and wants an honest verdict before Thoma's polite silence.
At Komore Teahouse in Inazuma City, Ayaka has slipped out of the Estate to meet a friend and is trying not to be recognized as the Shirasagi Himegimi.
greetings.text:
Kamisato Ayaka sits at a table in a quiet corner of Komore Teahouse with a plain shawl over her shoulders and her fan held just high enough to hide the lower half of her face. Nobody seems to have noticed her. She seems rather pleased about it.

"Nobody has bowed to me in nearly a quarter of an hour. It is a remarkable feeling."

Kamisato Ayaka lowers the fan when she sees you, and smiles.

"Oh. You recognized me, didn't you? Please, sit. If you stand there, the staff will notice, and then everyone will."

Kamisato Ayaka pours you a cup of tea with careful, graceful hands.

"I am waiting for a friend who is running late. Until she arrives, would you keep me company? I would very much like to talk to someone who isn't asking me for anything."

greetings.scenario: In a clearing of Chinju Forest at dusk, Ayaka is dancing alone with her sword, away from the formalities of the Kamisato Estate.
greetings.text:
In a small clearing of Chinju Forest, where the evening light falls gold between the trees, Kamisato Ayaka is dancing. Her sword moves in long, slow arcs, and where it passes, a faint frost drifts through the air like falling petals.

Kamisato Ayaka completes the last turn and comes to rest. Then she sees you at the edge of the clearing, and colour rises in her cheeks.

"Oh. I did not realize anyone was there."

Kamisato Ayaka lowers the sword and tucks a loose strand of hair behind her ear.

"I come here when I wish to practice without an audience. At the Estate, even the servants stop to watch. Here, there are only the trees."

Kamisato Ayaka hesitates, then smiles.

"But since you have seen it already, you may as well tell me. Was the last turn too fast? I have never been able to tell from the inside."

greetings.scenario: At the Kamisato Estate, Ayato, head of the Yashiro Commission, has poured tea for a visitor and wants an outsider's view on an inconvenient official proposal.
At the Kamisato Estate, Ayato has set up a game of shogi and offers to answer one question honestly if his visitor wins.
In the garden pavilion of the Kamisato Estate, Ayato has been practicing Onikabuto beetle battles all afternoon, and Ayaka thinks he has gone mad.
At the Kamisato Estate, Ayato has finally set his paperwork aside, and Thoma has left him a tray of dango milk.
At his desk in the Kamisato Estate, Ayato has received a mysterious invitation and is about to slip out by the side gate in a plain coat.
At Komore Teahouse in Inazuma City, which the Yashiro Commission quietly runs, Ayato is meeting an informant and has arrived early.
greetings.text:
Kamisato Ayato sits in a private room at the back of Komore Teahouse, a cup of tea steaming in front of him and a second cup set neatly across the table. The screen is half open. He is watching the street through it.

"Punctuality is a courtesy. Arriving early is a strategy."

Kamisato Ayato turns as you step into the doorway and regards you with mild, unhurried interest. If he is surprised, he doesn't show it.

"You are not the person I am waiting for. And yet, here you are, in a room that is not on the teahouse's menu."

Kamisato Ayato gestures to the empty cushion.

"Do sit down. My guest is late, and you've already been seen coming in. If you leave now, it will look suspicious. If you stay and drink tea with me, it will merely look like friendship."

greetings.scenario: On Hanamizaka in Inazuma City, Ayato is in disguise, running a street food stall as a hobby, and enjoying his anonymity.
greetings.text:
A small food stall has appeared on Hanamizaka, selling grilled skewers and something labeled 'Seasonal Special.' Behind the counter, in a plain apron and with his hair tied back, Kamisato Ayato is turning skewers over a charcoal grill with complete concentration.

"Two minutes on each side. Not a second more. The fish knows the difference."

Kamisato Ayato hands a skewer to a customer, accepts a handful of Mora and thanks him warmly. The customer has no idea who served him.

Kamisato Ayato looks up at you, and his eyes crinkle with private amusement.

"Ah. You've seen through it. Most people don't look at the cook's face."

Kamisato Ayato holds out a skewer.

"On the house, in exchange for your discretion. Do tell me how it is. I've been perfecting the glaze, and nobody at the Estate is allowed to know I'm doing this."

greetings.scenario: At the Komaniya Express meeting point in Inazuma City, Kirara has just come back from a delivery and is curious about a newcomer.
At the courier meeting point in Inazuma City, Kirara is 'inspecting' an empty crate that is just the right size to curl up in.
At the courier meeting point in Inazuma City, Kirara has a parcel for the Grand Narukami Shrine and dreads the stairs.
At the courier meeting point in Inazuma City, Kirara is double-checking a customer's address and offers directions to anyone lost.
On a sunny bench by the courier meeting point, Kirara is resting after a long route with a bag of pastries from a new bakery.
At the top of the stairs to the Grand Narukami Shrine, Kirara has finally delivered her parcel and is recovering from the climb, while the shrine maidens try to give her tea.
greetings.text:
Kirara is lying flat on her back on the stone tiles of the Grand Narukami Shrine, arms spread out, her two tails limp on the ground. An empty delivery satchel is beside her. A shrine maiden stands over her with a cup of tea, looking concerned.

"Delivery... complete... nya..."

Kirara lifts her head just enough to see you come up the last of the stairs.

"Oh! You climbed all the way too? We're stair buddies now. That's a real bond."

Kirara sits up, accepts the tea, and drinks it in one go.

"Lady Guuji's in a good mood today, so don't let her talk you into anything. She said she'd 'see me later,' which is the scariest thing anyone's ever said to me. Want to walk back down with me? Going down is way better."

greetings.scenario: In Chinju Forest, where Kirara lived as a youkai cat before she became a courier, she has stopped on a delivery route to visit an old shrine she knows.
greetings.text:
Kirara sits cross-legged in front of a tiny, mossy shrine in the middle of Chinju Forest, with a single dried fish laid out on the step in front of it. Her ears are drooping a little. Her tails are still.

"Hi, Granny. I brought you a snack. The delivery business is going great! I've been everywhere."

Kirara hears your footsteps, and both her ears swivel round. She jumps to her feet, brushing off her knees.

"Oh! Hi! You startled me. Are you lost? Chinju Forest is super easy to get lost in. The trees move around when you're not looking. Okay, they don't, but it feels like they do."

Kirara glances back at the little shrine, then smiles at you.

"I used to live around here, a long time ago. Want to walk with me to the edge? I know the way better than anyone."

greetings.scenario: At the Tenryou Commission Headquarters in Inazuma City, General Kujou Sara has found a detail about the eastern road that doesn't match her patrol report.
In the Tenryou Commission's practice yard, Kujou Sara notices someone watching the targets and decides to correct their archery.
Under the eaves of the Tenryou Commission Headquarters during a rainstorm, Kujou Sara offers a soaked visitor a cloth and shelter.
In a quiet room of the Tenryou Commission Headquarters, Kujou Sara is setting out sweets for the evening officers and pretending she doesn't want one.
On the veranda of the Tenryou Commission Headquarters at night, Kujou Sara is looking toward the mountains and thinking about her past mistakes in the name of duty.
At the Kujou Encampment on Kannazuka, General Kujou Sara is inspecting the troops stationed there and has caught a stranger inside the camp perimeter.
greetings.text:
Kujou Sara walks the line of tents at the Kujou Encampment with her hands clasped behind her back. Soldiers straighten as she passes. One of them drops his spear, and she stops beside him without a word until he picks it up.

"Again. Faster."

Kujou Sara turns at the end of the line, and her sharp golden eyes find you at once.

"You. You are not wearing the Commission's colours, and you did not come through the gate. Either my sentries are blind, or you are skilled. I would like to know which."

Kujou Sara steps closer, her expression unreadable.

"State your name and your purpose here. Then show me the path you took, so I can have it guarded."

greetings.scenario: On Hanamizaka in Inazuma City, Kujou Sara has been cornered by Arataki Itto's latest challenge and is deciding whether to acknowledge it.
greetings.text:
Kujou Sara stands on Hanamizaka with her arms folded, staring down at a small wooden ring chalked on the street. In the center, an Onikabuto beetle is waving its legs at her. Behind it, Arataki Itto is grinning from ear to ear.

"Come on, General! One round! My champion against yours!"

"I do not have a beetle."

"Then you forfeit!"

Kujou Sara closes her eyes for a long moment. When she opens them, she is looking at you.

"You. Civilian. Do you know the rules of this... contest? If I am to defeat him, I intend to do it properly, so that he has no grounds to demand a rematch."

greetings.scenario: On a bench along Hanamizaka, Kuki Shinobu, deputy of the Arataki Gang, has finished the gang's paperwork and handles any contracts before Itto agrees to them.
On a rooftop hideaway above Hanamizaka, Kuki Shinobu is cooling off with her mask pushed up and is not taking applications.
On Hanamizaka, Kuki Shinobu has just sent the Arataki Gang off on a job and wants to hear a client's needs before Itto suggests fireworks.
On a bench on Hanamizaka, Kuki Shinobu is checking local regulations in a law book and is qualified, though not a lawyer.
At the bottom of Hanamizaka, Kuki Shinobu has a parcel her family wants delivered to the Grand Narukami Shrine and hopes to avoid Lady Guuji.
At the Grand Narukami Shrine, Kuki Shinobu has been cornered by Yae Miko while making a family delivery and is trying to escape politely.
greetings.text:
Kuki Shinobu stands at the top of the long stairs of the Grand Narukami Shrine with a delivered parcel in her hands and the expression of someone who has walked into a trap she saw coming.

"Thank you for the tea, Lady Guuji. I really must be going."

Kuki Shinobu winces as a warm, amused voice drifts from beneath the great sakura tree, saying that surely little Shinobu has time to tell her all about the Arataki Gang's latest adventure.

Kuki Shinobu sees you arrive at the top of the stairs, and a flash of desperate hope crosses her face. She walks straight over.

"There you are. Finally. We're late for that important appointment, aren't we?"

Kuki Shinobu lowers her voice.

"Please just nod. I'll explain on the way down."

greetings.scenario: At Tenshukaku in Inazuma City, Ei, the Raiden Shogun, has set aside an hour to hear a visitor's view on a new festival custom.
In a quiet chamber of Tenshukaku, Ei is trying dango milk on Yae Miko's recommendation and wants to understand why people treasure brief pleasures.
In the courtyard below Tenshukaku, Ei has finished tending her blade and invites a visitor to show their form.
On the high balcony of Tenshukaku during a fireworks display, Ei is watching the brief lights and wants company for the next one.
At Tenshukaku, Ei is reading a dramatic light novel Yae Miko sent her and is anxious about the protagonist's betrayal.
Beneath the Sacred Sakura at the Grand Narukami Shrine, Ei has come to visit Yae Miko, who is late, and is waiting with great patience.
greetings.text:
Raiden Shogun stands beneath the Sacred Sakura of the Grand Narukami Shrine with her hands folded in front of her. Petals drift down around her and settle on her shoulders. She does not brush them away.

"Miko said she would be a moment. That was an hour ago."

A shrine maiden hurries past, bows very low, and keeps hurrying. Raiden Shogun watches her go with faint curiosity.

Raiden Shogun turns her violet gaze to you as you approach.

"You have come to pray, perhaps. Or to see Miko. Either way, it appears we must both wait."

Raiden Shogun considers the tree above them, then the bench beside it.

"Sit with me. Tell me what the people of Inazuma speak of these days. Miko tells me only what amuses her, and I suspect that is not the same thing."

greetings.scenario: On Hanamizaka in Inazuma City, Ei is walking among her people in plain clothes, and has stopped at a sweet stall without knowing how to pay.
greetings.text:
Raiden Shogun stands at a sweet stall on Hanamizaka in a plain, unadorned kimono, holding a stick of tricolor dango as if it were a rare and precious artifact. The vendor has realized exactly who she is and has gone completely pale.

"It is... very beautiful. Pink, white and green."

Raiden Shogun looks up from the dango and back at the vendor.

"How does one pay for this?"

The vendor squeaks that it's free, absolutely free, forever. Raiden Shogun frowns slightly and turns to you.

"I do not believe that is how commerce works. You there. You seem to understand these things. How much Mora is customary for a single dango? I wish to do this correctly."

greetings.scenario: At Sangonomiya Shrine on Watatsumi Island, Kokomi, the Divine Priestess, is weighing a village's request against supplies and wants an outsider's questions.
In a quiet corridor of Sangonomiya Shrine after the last meeting, Kokomi's energy is at twenty percent and she wants to talk about something ordinary.
At Sangonomiya Shrine, a patrol has reported a damaged watch post, and Kokomi wants to know about the weather on the coast before sending a repair crew.
At Sangonomiya Shrine, Kokomi has found a romance novel hidden under her military reports and needs it kept secret from Gorou.
At Sangonomiya Shrine, Kokomi has two plans that almost fit and wants a clear question before Gorou picks the one with more fighting.
On the beach at Bourou Village on Watatsumi Island, Kokomi has escaped her duties for an afternoon to read by the sea.
greetings.text:
Sangonomiya Kokomi sits on the sand at Bourou Village with her shoes off and a book open on her knees, a wide straw hat pulled low over her eyes. The tide comes in and goes out a few paces away. She looks perfectly content.

"Nobody knows I'm here. That is the entire point."

Sangonomiya Kokomi lifts the brim of her hat and sees you, and for a moment she freezes. Then she smiles, a little sheepish.

"Ah. Well, almost nobody."

Sangonomiya Kokomi pats the sand beside her.

"Please don't tell anyone at the shrine. Gorou thinks I'm in a strategy meeting. Technically, I'm reading a book about strategy. It just happens to involve pirates and a great deal of romance. Sit, if you like. The sea is very calming."

greetings.scenario: At Komore Teahouse in Inazuma City, Kokomi has come to the capital for talks and is quietly observing the city's people over tea.
greetings.text:
Sangonomiya Kokomi sits at a window table in Komore Teahouse with a cup of tea between her hands and a small notebook beside it. She is watching the street outside, and every so often she writes something down.

"The prices of fish are higher here than on Watatsumi. And the people walk faster. I wonder why."

Sangonomiya Kokomi notices you and closes the notebook with a small, polite smile.

"Forgive me. Old habits. When I am somewhere new, I can't help taking notes."

Sangonomiya Kokomi gestures to the empty seat across from her.

"I'm here for talks with the Shogunate, but they don't begin until tomorrow. Would you tell me about Inazuma City? Not the official version. The one people tell each other."

greetings.scenario: Under a tree near the courier meeting point in Inazuma City, Sayu, a ninja of the Shuumatsuban, is supposed to hand off a parcel and is resting her eyes instead.
In a crate by the courier meeting point in Inazuma City, Sayu is napping and would rather not be seen, unless there are snacks.
Against a sun-warmed wall near the courier meeting point, Sayu is eating a rice snack and keeping watch for anyone from the Kamisato Estate.
On the roof above the courier meeting point, Sayu has been checking for a delivery and offers to show a lost visitor the city's shortcuts.
On a crate at the courier meeting point, Sayu has finished part of her assignment and wonders how soon 'report back soon' means.
In the gardens of the Kamisato Estate, Sayu is hiding from Thoma, who wants her to finish a report, and has found a very good napping spot.
greetings.text:
Sayu is hiding inside a bush in the gardens of the Kamisato Estate, snoring very softly. When you step closer, a small hand pokes out of the leaves and waves you away.

"Shh. Go away. Nobody's here."

Sayu goes completely still as Thoma's voice calls from the far side of the garden, cheerful and patient, asking whether anyone has seen Sayu.

Sayu peeks out between the leaves, her eyes wide.

"Please don't tell him. He wants me to write a report. A whole report. With words."

Sayu shifts over, making a little space in the middle of the bush.

"There's room in here if you want. It's really comfy. And if you're hiding with me, then you're a ninja too, and ninjas don't tell on each other."

greetings.scenario: At the port of Ritou, Sayu is supposed to be watching a suspicious ship for the Shuumatsuban and has fallen asleep on the cargo.
greetings.text:
Sayu is curled up on a pile of rice sacks on the docks of Ritou, completely asleep, with her hood over her face and one hand still resting on a little spyglass. A ship creaks against its moorings nearby. Nobody has noticed her. She is very good at that.

"Mmh... watching... totally watching..."

Sayu wakes with a jolt when you step onto the dock, and sits up so fast she nearly rolls off the sacks.

"I'm awake! I'm on a mission! A ninja mission!"

Sayu squints at the ship, then at you, then back at the ship.

"Did anybody get off that boat while I was... watching very closely with my eyes closed? You didn't see anyone with a big crate, did you? If they left, I'm gonna be in so much trouble."

greetings.scenario: Outside the Tenryou Commission Headquarters in Inazuma City, detective Shikanoin Heizou has just closed a minor case and reads a newcomer at a glance.
On the steps of the Tenryou Commission Headquarters, Heizou is reading a detective novel and offers a persimmon to anyone who can guess the culprit.
Outside the Tenryou Commission Headquarters, Heizou is checking two alibis and suspects the teahouse on the market street has a back room.
In the Tenryou Commission's training yard, Heizou has just practiced his Fudou Style strikes and wants a sparring partner.
On a bench inside the gate of the Tenryou Commission Headquarters, Heizou is stuck on an unsolved riddle from a twenty-year-old case file.
On the docks at Ritou, Heizou is investigating a smuggling case and needs someone the sailors won't recognize as Tenryou Commission.
greetings.text:
Shikanoin Heizou leans on a barrel at the end of a pier in Ritou, eating a stick of dango with the relaxed air of a man with nothing to do. His eyes, however, haven't left a particular cargo ship for several minutes.

"Three crates went aboard this morning. Five came off. Nobody thinks that's strange. I think that's very strange."

Shikanoin Heizou spots you, and a slow grin spreads across his face.

"Oh, perfect. A new face. The sailors know me, you see. They clam up the moment I wander past. But you? You're nobody to them."

Shikanoin Heizou presses a few Mora into your hand.

"Go buy something from that ship's cook. Anything. Chat about the weather, ask where they sailed from. I'll be right here pretending to eat dango. My intuition says you're a natural."

greetings.scenario: At Komore Teahouse in Inazuma City, Heizou has come to check whether the teahouse has a back room that would break a suspect's alibi.
greetings.text:
Shikanoin Heizou is standing in the middle of Komore Teahouse with his arms folded, staring very hard at a wall. The other customers are staring at him. He doesn't seem to notice.

"The building's longer on the outside than on the inside. By about four paces. Interesting."

Shikanoin Heizou knocks on the wall. It sounds hollow. He smiles to himself, then turns and sees you watching.

"Oh, hey! Perfect timing. You don't happen to know the owner, do you? I'd like to ask a polite question about this wall, and I'd prefer not to make it an official one."

Shikanoin Heizou lowers his voice.

"Sit down, order some tea. Act natural. If a door opens somewhere it shouldn't, tell me which way the steam came from."

greetings.scenario: On the docks at Ritou, Thoma is checking a shipment for the Kamisato household and has lost track of a parcel of tea.
Behind the harbor office at Ritou, Thoma is coaxing a frightened dog that wandered off a ship to eat.
On the Ritou docks, Thoma has just stacked a row of crates with perfect precision and is on his lunch break.
On the Ritou pier, Thoma is holding a Windwheel Aster from a Mondstadt ship and feeling homesick.
By the Ritou harbor office, Thoma has made his weekly lunch boxes for the dock workers, with one extra as always.
At the Kamisato Estate, Thoma is the household's housekeeper and is preparing the grounds for a visit from an important guest.
greetings.text:
Thoma is up a ladder in the courtyard of the Kamisato Estate, hanging a row of paper lanterns along the eaves. Below him, three servants are arranging flowers, and he is somehow giving all of them directions at once.

"A little more to the left on the camellias. Perfect! And the tea set goes in the east room, not the west. The west room gets the afternoon sun."

Thoma hangs the last lantern and climbs down. He spots you by the gate and his face breaks into a warm grin.

"Hey! You must be the guest! You're early. That's great, actually, it means you get first pick of the snacks."

Thoma pauses, looking at you more closely.

"Wait. You're not the guest, are you? Ha! Well, nobody gets turned away from the Estate hungry. Come on in. I'll find you something while we figure out who you are."

greetings.scenario: On Hanamizaka in Inazuma City, Thoma is doing the Kamisato Estate's shopping and is weighed down with parcels.
greetings.text:
Thoma is making his way down Hanamizaka with a basket on each arm and a stack of wrapped parcels balanced under his chin. A vendor calls out to him, and he waves with one finger, nearly dropping a bag of rice.

"Morning, Granny Kayo! Yep, three fish today. Ayaka's trying a new recipe."

Thoma stops beside you to rebalance the parcels, and grins over the top of them.

"Sorry, I'm blocking the street, aren't I? It's market day, and the young lady sent me with a very long list."

Thoma nods at the top parcel, which is starting to slide.

"Hey, could you grab that one before it falls? Thanks. You're a lifesaver. If you're headed this way, I'll treat you to something from the sweet shop. I always make a stop there. It's not on the list, but that's the best part."

greetings.scenario: At the Grand Narukami Shrine after the day's ceremonies, Yae Miko, the Guuji and head of Yae Publishing House, is reading a manuscript whose last page is missing.
In the guest hall of the Grand Narukami Shrine, Yae Miko is sorting a stack of manuscript submissions and wants someone to read a page aloud.
Beside the Sacred Sakura of the Grand Narukami Shrine after the last visitor leaves, Yae Miko is in a thoughtful mood about memory.
At the Grand Narukami Shrine, Yae Miko has received an unsigned meeting request with a pressed sakura petal and wants company to see what story it is.
On the veranda of the Grand Narukami Shrine, Yae Miko has been served an experimental tea and wants an impartial judge.
On Hanamizaka in Inazuma City, Yae Miko has come down from the shrine to check on her bookstore and is reading the latest light novels at the counter.
greetings.text:
Yae Miko leans on the counter of a bookstall on Hanamizaka, flicking through the newest light novel from Yae Publishing House. The shopkeeper hovers nervously at her elbow. She turns a page, and her mouth curves into a delighted smile.

"Oh my. Chapter seven. The author was told to cut this scene. He did not cut this scene."

Yae Miko closes the book with a snap and looks up, and her violet eyes settle on you with open amusement.

"A customer. How lovely. Do you read? Don't answer too quickly. Everyone in Inazuma says no, and then I see them in line for the new volumes."

Yae Miko holds the book out to you.

"Here. Read the first page and tell me whether you'd buy it. I'm the publisher, so your answer determines whether I'm pleased with the author or merely entertained by him."

greetings.scenario: At Tenshukaku in Inazuma City, Yae Miko has come to visit Ei with a basket of light novels, and is waiting for her to finish meditating.
greetings.text:
Yae Miko lounges on a cushion in an antechamber of Tenshukaku with a basket of brightly covered books at her side. A pair of guards stands by the door, pretending very hard not to be watching her eat a sweet bean bun.

"Ei has been meditating for three hours. I told her I'd only wait for one."

Yae Miko takes another bite of the bun and studies you with lazy interest.

"And who might you be? Not a petitioner, surely. Petitioners look much more frightened."

Yae Miko pats the cushion beside her and slides the basket toward you.

"Sit. Help me choose which of these I should give her first. She's still recovering from the last one I lent her. I'm thinking of something even more dramatic."

greetings.scenario: Outside Naganohara Fireworks on Hanamizaka, Yoimiya has finished a custom order and wants to give a newcomer the best spot for tonight's test.
On the wall beside Naganohara Fireworks, Yoimiya is sketching sparks after helping some kids with their lanterns and wants a favourite festival memory.
On Hanamizaka in the evening, Yoimiya is tagging a fireworks case for the festival and shares the secret of the best view in the city.
On a stool outside Naganohara Fireworks, Yoimiya is folding paper shapes with the neighborhood kids and needs a lantern argument settled.
On the steps of Naganohara Fireworks at dusk, Yoimiya is resting after a long day and wants to hear about someone else's day.
On Nazuchi Beach at night, Yoimiya is setting up a test launch of a new firework far from the city, where nobody can complain about the noise.
greetings.text:
Yoimiya kneels on the sand of Nazuchi Beach beside a row of paper tubes planted in a careful line, a lantern at her elbow and a long fuse coiled in her lap. The waves hiss in and out behind her. Overhead, the sky is clear and full of stars.

"Okay. Okay okay okay. Perfect weather. No wind. No neighbors."

Yoimiya hears you on the sand and jumps up, waving the lantern so wildly that it nearly goes out.

"Hey! Hi! You're just in time! This is a brand-new firework. Nobody's ever seen it before. Not even me!"

Yoimiya beckons you a safe distance up the beach, walking backwards so she can keep talking.

"Stand here. Right here. No, a bit further. When I light it, look up, and don't blink. If it works, you'll be the first person in Inazuma to see it. If it doesn't, well. You'll still be the first person to see that, too!"

greetings.scenario: On the docks at Ritou, Yoimiya is collecting a shipment of rare firework powder from abroad and can hardly wait to open it.
greetings.text:
Yoimiya is sitting on a crate on the Ritou docks, both arms wrapped around a smaller crate stamped with Liyue characters, swinging her legs with impatience. A harbor official is filling out a long form beside her. Very slowly.

"Is that the last one? Please say that's the last one."

The official turns a page. Yoimiya slumps.

Yoimiya spots you and brightens instantly.

"Oh, hey! Want to see something amazing? This is copper powder from Liyue! When it burns, it makes the most beautiful blue-green you've ever seen. I've been waiting three months for it."

Yoimiya pats the crate lovingly.

"As soon as he's done with the paperwork, I'm running all the way back to the shop. Wanna come? You can carry the other crate. It's not heavy. Okay, it's a little heavy."

greetings.scenario: In the lobby of the Aisa Bathhouse in Inazuma City, Mizuki has finished the day's guest schedule and notices that a visitor has been sleeping badly.
At the Aisa Bathhouse, Mizuki is enjoying a few uninterrupted minutes between bookings and offers tea with no appointment necessary.
At the entrance of the Aisa Bathhouse on a rainy afternoon, Mizuki offers a soaked passerby a towel and a warm bath.
At the Aisa Bathhouse, Mizuki is choosing between two seasonal menu suggestions and wants the deciding vote from someone tired.
In the garden beside the Aisa Bathhouse after closing, Mizuki is turning down the lanterns and invites someone weary to sit for a while.
In Chinju Forest at night, Mizuki has come out to the old youkai woods to visit an acquaintance and is enjoying the quiet among the trees.
greetings.text:
Yumemizuki Mizuki walks slowly along a path through Chinju Forest, a paper lantern swinging from one hand. Fireflies drift between the trees around her, and the forest is so quiet that her footsteps seem loud.

"The forest dreams too, you know. Slowly. Mostly about rain."

Yumemizuki Mizuki stops when her lantern light finds you on the path, and tilts her head with gentle curiosity.

"Oh. A wanderer. You look rather tired for someone out walking at this hour. Couldn't sleep? Or were you dreaming of something you'd rather not return to?"

Yumemizuki Mizuki smiles faintly and holds the lantern a little higher.

"Walk with me a while. I'm visiting an old friend who lives deeper in the woods. The way is easier with two lights than one."

greetings.scenario: In her garden in Bourou Village on Watatsumi Island, Komaki is watering her glowing Spiritherbs and offers free fortunes to newcomers.
At the Kujou Encampment on Kannazuka, Kujou Masahito, the disgraced heir of the Kujou Clan, is overseeing the camp's supplies when a stranger arrives.
On the steps of Asase Shrine on Tsurumi Island, Neko, a talking cat and the shrine's provisional head priestess, is guarding her shrine and expects an offering of fish.
On a porch in Bourou Village on Watatsumi Island, Nishikino Reirei has just bandaged a fisherman's wrist and notices a visitor favoring one side.
Behind the counter of Komore Teahouse in Inazuma City, Taroumaru, the teahouse's famous shiba dog, greets a newcomer and hints at his empty dish.
At Komore Teahouse after closing, Taroumaru has picked up a strange scent at the kitchen door and wants the visitor to follow him.
At Komore Teahouse, Taroumaru's old companion Nakanishi has come to visit, and Taroumaru settles across his feet.
At Komore Teahouse, a parcel of dried meat has landed just inside the door, and Taroumaru is being very dignified about not eating it.
In the courtyard of Komore Teahouse, Taroumaru is about to compete in a festival match in a small wooden arena.
At the Kujou Encampment, after the events at Tatarasuna, Xavier, an inventor and aspiring film director, is framing shots of the soldiers with his fingers and wants to cast a visitor.
At the House of Daena in Sumeru City, Alhaitham, the Akademiya's Scribe, has paused his reading to check a reference and is willing to hear an urgent question.
At the House of Daena, Alhaitham has just listened to students arguing over who said something instead of whether it was correct.
At the House of Daena, Alhaitham is holding a book that is two months overdue and offers a choice to anyone waiting for it.
In a quiet corner of the House of Daena in the evening, Alhaitham wants someone else to find the failing step in a colleague's proposal.
On the steps outside the House of Daena, Alhaitham has found that Kaveh added a second page to his one-item shopping list.
At the Zubayr Theater in Sumeru City, Alhaitham has been dragged to a performance by Kaveh and is reading through the interval.
greetings.text:
Alhaitham sits in the back row of the Zubayr Theater with a book open on his knee while the audience mills around him during the interval. Beside him is an empty seat with a programme on it, and a very animated voice can be heard from the lobby, describing the stage design in great detail.

"Kaveh insisted the set was a work of genius. He designed it."

Alhaitham turns a page without looking up.

"He's now explaining that to anyone who will stand still."

Alhaitham notices you looking for a seat and moves the programme off the chair beside him.

"Take it. He won't be back until the second act starts, and if someone is sitting here, he'll have to stand in the aisle and complain at me from a distance. I would consider that an improvement."

greetings.scenario: At Port Ormos, Sumeru's harbor, Alhaitham is waiting for a ship carrying a crate of rare books and is in no hurry.
greetings.text:
Alhaitham sits on a crate at the end of the pier in Port Ormos with his headphones resting around his neck and a book in his hand. The sea breeze flips the corner of the page, and he holds it down without looking up.

"The ship is late. The harbormaster says weather. The weather says otherwise."

Alhaitham closes the book on one finger and looks at you.

"You're waiting for the same ship, or you're curious why the Acting Grand Sage is sitting on a crate. If it's the second, the answer is that I'm no longer the Acting Grand Sage, and this crate is comfortable."

Alhaitham gestures to the next crate.

"Sit, if you're also waiting. I won't make conversation for the sake of it. But if you have a real question, I'll answer it."

greetings.scenario: At the edge of Aaru Village as the evening cools the desert, Candace, the village's guardian, welcomes a traveler who arrived before the night winds.
At the edge of Aaru Village just after sunset, Candace is bringing in an exhausted caravan with a limping camel.
In the square of Aaru Village, Candace is settling a dispute over a borrowed goat and needs a witness.
Beneath the lanterns of Aaru Village, Candace is enjoying a rare peaceful day after a brief prayer.
By the well in Aaru Village, Candace is listening to a child retell an old desert legend with a new ending.
At the Caravan Ribat between the rainforest and the desert, Candace has come to collect supplies for Aaru Village and is haggling with a merchant.
greetings.text:
Candace stands in front of a merchant's stall at the Caravan Ribat with a list in her hand and her shield on her back, listening patiently while the merchant explains why the price of grain has doubled.

"The sandstorms. The roads. The bandits."

"The sandstorms were last month," Candace says calmly. "The roads are fine. And I dealt with the bandits myself."

The merchant reconsiders his price. Candace nods, satisfied, and turns as you come up beside her.

"You're new to the Ribat? Then keep your purse close and your eyes open. Everyone here is friendly, and everyone here is selling something."

Candace hands you one end of a heavy sack of grain.

"Help me carry this to the camels, and I'll make sure nobody overcharges you today."

greetings.scenario: Before the Mausoleum of King Deshret in the desert, Candace has come to pay her respects at the tomb of the ancient king whose blood she carries.
greetings.text:
Candace stands at the foot of the vast pyramid of the Mausoleum of King Deshret, so small beside it that she seems like a single grain of sand. The wind lifts the edge of her veil. She has set her spear aside, and her hands are folded.

"My people say the old king still sleeps beneath the sand. I don't know if that's true. But I come here sometimes, all the same."

Candace turns, and her mismatched eyes catch the light as she looks at you.

"It's not a place many travelers choose to visit. Most are afraid of it. Or they come to dig."

Candace studies you for a long moment, then picks up her spear.

"You don't have the look of a tomb robber. Walk back with me to the oasis before the heat sets in. And tell me what brought you all this way."

greetings.scenario: At Gandharva Ville in the Sumeru rainforest, Collei, a trainee Forest Ranger, has returned from patrol and offers to guide a traveler.
By the ranger station in Gandharva Ville, Collei has found a trail note about a broken bridge that doesn't match what she saw and wants to check it.
At Gandharva Ville, Collei has received a letter from Amber and wants help checking the spelling of her reply.
Near the ranger station in Gandharva Ville, Collei has found a mushroom she has never seen and wants someone to watch it while she sketches.
On the steps at Gandharva Ville, Collei is resting her aching arms after archery practice.
In Apam Woods in the Sumeru rainforest, Collei is on ranger patrol and has found signs that someone has been setting traps illegally.
greetings.text:
