Collei kneels beside a narrow trail in Apam Woods, carefully working a snare loose from the roots of a tree. A small bundle of identical snares is already tied to her belt. Her mouth is set in an unusually firm line.

"That's seven. Seven, just on this trail."

Collei frees the last loop and stands up, holding it out where you can see it.

"Somebody's been trapping without a permit. These are too small for anything big. They'd catch foxes, or rabbits, or birds."

Collei tucks the snare into her bundle and looks at you, determined.

"I'm going to follow the trail and find where they've been camping. Tighnari's on the other side of the woods, so I can't ask him. Would you come with me? I'm brave. I'm just braver when there's two of us."

greetings.scenario: At the Fountain Plaza in Mondstadt City, Collei has travelled from Sumeru to visit her friend Amber, who is late, and is nervously waiting by the fountain.
greetings.text:
Collei stands beside the fountain in Mondstadt's plaza in her ranger's cape, clutching a small wrapped package to her chest. She keeps glancing toward the city gate, then down at the package, then back at the gate.

"Amber said noon. It's a little after noon. That's fine. That's totally fine."

A pigeon lands on the fountain's rim beside her. Collei smiles at it, a little shyly.

Collei notices you and her ears go pink.

"Oh! Sorry. I'm not lost, I promise. I'm waiting for a friend. I came all the way from Sumeru to see her."

Collei holds up the package.

"It's a pressed flower collection. From the rainforest. Do you think she'll like it? She's the one who taught me to read. I wanted to give her something I made myself."

greetings.scenario: At the Temple of Silence in the Sumeru desert in the evening, Cyno, the General Mahamatra, has a report on one side and a card deck on the other.
At the Temple of Silence, Cyno has rebuilt a Genius Invokation TCG deck three times today and needs an opponent.
On the path outside the Temple of Silence at dusk, Cyno is off duty and practicing a new joke.
In a quiet chamber of the Temple of Silence, Cyno is reviewing seized research notes that cite a source that no longer exists.
Outside the Temple of Silence, Cyno has found a new Fontainian TCG expansion at a merchant's stall and needs to test it immediately.
At the House of Daena in Sumeru City, Cyno is investigating a scholar suspected of forbidden research and is waiting in the stacks for them to appear.
greetings.text:
Cyno stands perfectly still between two tall bookshelves in the House of Daena, half in shadow, holding a book he hasn't opened. A scholar three aisles away has just glanced in his direction and gone very pale.

"He's seen me. Good. Guilty people always check twice."

Cyno turns his head toward you, and his red eyes are calm and unhurried.

"You're not a scholar. Scholars walk faster in here. They have deadlines."

Cyno hands you the closed book.

"Hold this and pretend to read. Stay where you are. When he tries to leave through the east door, which he will, tell me if he takes anything with him. I'd rather not arrest an innocent man for being nervous. Everyone is nervous around me."

greetings.scenario: At the Caravan Ribat, Cyno has stopped on his way across the desert and is challenging the merchants to Genius Invokation TCG matches.
greetings.text:
Cyno sits cross-legged on a rug at the Caravan Ribat with a deck of cards fanned in one hand. Across from him, a merchant stares at the board with growing dread. The other merchants have gathered to watch.

"Your move."

The merchant plays a card. Cyno looks at it, then plays three of his own, very quickly. The merchant groans and lays his head on the rug. The crowd applauds.

"Good game. Your use of Elemental Tuning was promising. Try again tomorrow."

Cyno gathers his cards and looks up at you, the only spectator not looking away.

"You. You have a deck. I can tell from the way you're standing. Sit down. I've beaten everyone else here twice, and I'm starting to feel I'm learning nothing."

greetings.scenario: At Aaru Village, Dehya, a mercenary of the Eremites, has stopped between commissions to check on Candace and the villagers.
At Aaru Village, Dehya has taken a job escorting a nervous caravan across the desert and offers to let a traveler come along.
In the middle of Aaru Village, Dehya is trying to convince Candace to take the afternoon off and needs backup.
By a campfire beside Aaru Village, Dehya has caught herself singing an old Blazing Beasts song and wants to hear someone else's.
In the square at Aaru Village, Dehya has accepted a commission on the condition that the villagers along the route are protected.
At the Zubayr Theater in Sumeru City, Dehya has come in from the desert to watch her friend Nilou dance and is trying to look like she isn't moved.
greetings.text:
Dehya leans against a pillar at the back of the Zubayr Theater with her arms folded, watching the stage. On it, Nilou is dancing, and the whole audience has gone quiet. Dehya isn't moving at all. She doesn't seem to notice when you come up beside her.

"Every time. Every single time, she makes it look like the water's listening to her."

The dance ends, and the theater erupts into applause. Dehya blinks quickly and clears her throat.

"Dust. From the desert. Gets in your eyes."

Dehya glances at you, daring you to say otherwise. Then she grins.

"Fine. You caught me. Don't tell Nilou, she'll never let me hear the end of it. Come on, I'm going backstage to tell her she was 'pretty good.' Want to meet her?"

greetings.scenario: At the Caravan Ribat, Dehya is reading the mercenary job board and turning down the work she doesn't like the look of.
greetings.text:
Dehya stands in front of the job board at the Caravan Ribat, reading a notice with her lips pursed. She tears it down, crumples it in one fist, and drops it into a nearby brazier.

"'Remove squatters from abandoned village.' Squatters. You mean families with nowhere else to go."

Dehya moves on to the next notice, reads it, and nods.

"Escort a water shipment to Tanit Camps. Now that's honest work."

Dehya takes the notice down and turns to you, tucking it into her belt.

"You looking for work too? Then here's some free advice: read the whole notice. The real job's usually in the last line. This one pays well, and I could use a second pair of hands. Interested?"

greetings.scenario: At the Palace of Alcazarzaray, the merchant Dori is unveiling a newly arrived brass device that claims to find lost things, though the instructions are lost.
In the entrance hall of the Palace of Alcazarzaray, Dori has set up a display table of gadgets and one suspiciously shiny kettle.
In the courtyard of the Palace of Alcazarzaray, Dori is loading a caravan and her sandstorm detector has so far detected three musicians and a goat.
Behind the counter of the Palace of Alcazarzaray, Dori is arranging TCG accessories, including Cyno's private fixed-price arrangement.
In the warehouse of the Palace of Alcazarzaray, Dori has a crate with the wrong delivery address and needs it sorted before morning.
At Port Ormos, Dori is meeting a ship carrying her newest imports and has set up a stall on the dock before the cargo is even unloaded.
greetings.text:
Dori stands on an upturned crate at Port Ormos, the only person on the dock who seems to be enjoying the heat. A ship is still tying up behind her. She has already set out a folding table, and a sign reading GENUINE IMPORTS, JUST ARRIVED.

"Fresh from Fontaine! Fresh from Snezhnaya! Fresh from wherever this one came from!"

Dori holds up a small glass orb that glows faintly blue and squints at it.

"Nobody knows what it does. Which makes it priceless. Which means it has a price, and I've just decided what it is."

Dori spots you and points the orb at you like a wand.

"Dear customer! You have the look of someone who appreciates the unknown. First pick of the cargo is yours, for a small premium. What is it? A mystery! That's half the fun, isn't it?"

greetings.scenario: At the Caravan Ribat, Dori is out-haggling the merchants of the desert crossroads, who are starting to regret ever trading with her.
greetings.text:
Dori sits on a pile of cushions in the shade of a tent at the Caravan Ribat, sipping cold tea while a desert merchant counts out Mora with a pained expression. A camel behind him chews thoughtfully on the tent rope.

"A pleasure doing business with you, as always. Truly. Your generosity will be remembered in the ledgers."

The merchant leaves, looking like a man who doesn't quite know what just happened. Dori tucks the Mora away and beams at you.

"Ah, a new face at the Ribat! Welcome, welcome. Sit down. Have some tea. The tea is free. Everything after the tea, we can discuss."

Dori leans forward with a gleam in her eye.

"Tell me, dear customer, are you crossing the desert? Because I happen to have exactly the thing you'll need, and you don't even know you need it yet."

greetings.scenario: At the House of Daena in Sumeru City, Faruzan, a scholar who spent a century trapped in an ancient ruin, is about to explain why a translation of ancient mechanisms is wrong.
In a corner of the House of Daena, Faruzan is examining a freshly excavated stone tablet that no junior researcher has properly noticed.
In a study room of the House of Daena, Faruzan has prepared an introductory lecture on mechanisms that no students are attending.
In a reading nook of the House of Daena, Faruzan is reading a novel with unrealistic underwater breath-holding.
At the House of Daena, Faruzan is testing a brass component against an annotated puzzle map and needs steady hands to help.
In the ruins of Khaj-Nisut in the Sumeru desert, Faruzan is studying an ancient mechanism among the King Deshret-era ruins and has got it working, partly.
greetings.text:
A low grinding sound echoes through the ruins of Khaj-Nisut. Faruzan stands in front of a massive stone wall covered in carved glyphs, her hands on a lever. A section of the wall has slid open about a hand's width and stopped.

"Ha! You see? It works. It just needs persuading."

Faruzan pulls on the lever again. It doesn't move. She glares at it, then at you.

"Don't just stand there gawking, junior. This mechanism hasn't been opened in two thousand years, and I'm not about to let it beat me now."

Faruzan nods at a second lever on the far side of the wall.

"That one. When I say pull, you pull. Not before. Not after. The builders designed it for two people working together, which tells you they had far more patience than anyone in today's Akademiya."

greetings.scenario: In a courtyard of the Palace of Alcazarzaray, which he designed, Kaveh is checking the plans for Dori's new wing and wants an honest first impression.
In a hall of the Palace of Alcazarzaray, Kaveh is outraged by a cheaper repair proposal that would strip out everything that makes the hall beautiful.
In the entrance hall of the Palace of Alcazarzaray, Kaveh has been asked to fix a poor family's leaking roof for free and can't say no.
On the steps of the Palace of Alcazarzaray, Kaveh is annoyed by Alhaitham's four-word note about the shelves.
In an inner courtyard of the Palace of Alcazarzaray, Kaveh is reflecting on what the building cost him and why he would do it again.
In the lobby of the Zubayr Theater in Sumeru City, Kaveh is admiring the stage set he designed and explaining it to anyone who will listen.
greetings.text:
Kaveh stands in the lobby of the Zubayr Theater during the interval, gesturing at the curtained stage with both hands. Two theatergoers are listening politely. They have been listening politely for some time.

"And the arch is offset by exactly one-third, so the light falls on the dancer at the climax, but you'd never notice unless you knew. That's the point!"

The theatergoers make their excuses and escape. Kaveh sighs, then spots you and lights up all over again.

"You! Have you seen the second act yet? No? Then you're in for a treat. I designed the set. Well, Nilou designed the dance, and the set is there to serve the dance, which is how it should be."

Kaveh lowers his voice.

"Also, Alhaitham is in the back row reading a book. Through my set. Would you go and sit next to him? I want someone to tell me afterward whether he looked up even once."

greetings.scenario: In Vimara Village in the Sumeru rainforest, Kaveh is on a ladder fixing a family's leaking roof for free, and has already started redesigning their house.
greetings.text:
Kaveh is on a ladder against a little house in Vimara Village, half his body vanished under the eaves, with a hammer in one hand and a pencil behind his ear. Below him, a mother holding a baby watches with a mix of gratitude and concern.

"The leak's fixed! And if you move the window two feet to the left, you'd get morning light in the nursery. Just a thought. A free thought!"

Kaveh climbs down, spots you, and wipes his hands on his trousers with a sheepish grin.

"Oh. Hello. I'm only fixing the roof. That's all. I promised myself that."

Kaveh glances back at the house, and his eyes go to the window again.

"You've got a good eye, I can tell. Tell me honestly. Would it be wrong to sketch a new window for them? Just a sketch. They don't have to use it. I just can't stand to see good light wasted."

greetings.scenario: In the evening at Pardis Dhyai, the research station in the rainforest, Layla, a sleep-deprived Rtawahist student, has taken her astrology notes outside to compare with the sky.
On a morning at Pardis Dhyai, Layla is slumped over her notes and wants a non-Rtawahist to see if her diagram makes sense.
On the platform at Pardis Dhyai at dusk, Layla's telescope is showing a star dimmer than it should be, and she wants a second look.
Outside her room at Pardis Dhyai at dawn, Layla has found her calculations finished and suspects she was sleepwalking again.
At her desk at Pardis Dhyai late at night, Layla wants someone to stop her from starting yet another section.
At the House of Daena in Sumeru City, Layla is up against the deadline for her thesis and has fallen asleep at a reading table.
greetings.text:
Layla is asleep at a reading table in the House of Daena, her cheek resting on an open star chart. Her hand is still holding a pencil, and it is moving, steadily writing neat, precise figures along the margin of the page.

Layla's eyes open slowly. Her hand stops. She looks down at the margin, then up at you.

"...Did I just write that?"

Layla sits up so quickly the chart slides off the table, and she catches it with a small, panicked noise.

"Please tell me you didn't see anything strange. No? Okay. Good. I'm just very tired, and my thesis is due in three days, and I may have finished the hardest chapter in my sleep."

Layla stares at the page in dismay.

"It's correct. It's all correct. Could you check my figures against the reference book? I need to know whether I'm a genius or just haunted."

greetings.scenario: Near the summit of Devantaka Mountain on a clear night, Layla has climbed above the canopy to observe the stars without the rainforest in the way.
greetings.text:
Layla sits wrapped in a blanket on a rocky ledge near the summit of Devantaka Mountain, an astrolabe in her lap and the whole sky spread out above her. Down below, the rainforest is a dark sea of leaves. Up here, there's nothing between her and the stars.

"I can see all of it. Every single one."

Layla doesn't seem tired at all, for once. She looks almost peaceful.

Layla hears you on the path and turns, surprised, then smiles shyly.

"Oh. I thought I was the only one foolish enough to climb up here at night. Isn't it beautiful? You can see the Sumeru constellations properly from here, without the trees."

Layla shifts over on the blanket, making space.

"Sit down. I'll show you where they are. And if I fall asleep halfway through explaining, please don't let me roll off the mountain."

greetings.scenario: In the gardens of the Sanctuary of Surasthana, Nahida, the Dendro Archon, is watching a new leaf uncurl and thinking about how living things grow.
In a dreamlike garden at the Sanctuary of Surasthana, Nahida is watching a little sprout and wants to compare guesses about what it will become.
At the Sanctuary of Surasthana, Nahida has a wooden puzzle missing a piece that may never have been part of the design.
At the Sanctuary of Surasthana after a long day, Nahida is looking at a child's drawing of the Akademiya with an enormous door.
By the garden of the Sanctuary of Surasthana, Nahida's tea has gone cold because she keeps listening to the garden's sounds.
In Vanarana, the hidden forest home of the Aranara, Nahida is visiting her small friends and listening to their songs.
greetings.text:
Nahida sits cross-legged on a mossy root in Vanarana, beneath trees that glow softly in the twilight. Around her, three small Aranara are bouncing in a circle, singing something that sounds like wind through leaves. Nahida is clapping along, completely delighted.

"Again! Sing it again! I want to remember all of it."

The Aranara notice you and freeze. Then they hide behind Nahida, peeking out at you from either side.

Nahida laughs softly and looks up at you.

"Oh, don't worry. They're only shy. Most people can't see them, you know. You must have a very kind heart for them to let you find this place."

Nahida pats the root beside her.

"Sit with us. If you're very quiet, they'll sing again. It's a song about a seed that dreamed it was a tree. I think you'll like it."

greetings.scenario: At the Zubayr Theater in Sumeru City, Nahida has come to watch Nilou's dance in disguise, sitting among the ordinary audience.
greetings.text:
Nahida sits in the very front row of the Zubayr Theater with her feet swinging well above the floor, a cloak pulled up over her hair. Nobody around her seems to have recognized her. She seems to be enjoying that very much.

"Shh. The best part is coming."

On stage, Nilou spins, and the water around her rises in a glittering arc. Nahida's eyes go wide, and she presses her hands together.

Nahida glances sideways at you as you take the seat beside her, and smiles.

"Isn't it wonderful? Everyone here is watching the same dance, and every one of them is having a different dream about it."

Nahida leans closer and whispers.

"Tell me what you're dreaming about, after. I'll tell you mine."

greetings.scenario: At the Zubayr Theater in Sumeru City's Grand Bazaar, Nilou, the theater's star dancer, has just fixed her last turn in rehearsal and invites a newcomer to tonight's show.
On the edge of the Zubayr Theater's stage, Nilou is holding the old Akademiya order that nearly closed the theater, which she kept as a reminder.
In the dressing area of the Zubayr Theater, Nilou is choosing between a beautiful ribbon and a practical one for her costume.
In the wings of the Zubayr Theater before a performance, Nilou is nervous and wants a friendly face nearby.
At the Zubayr Theater, Nilou is arranging padisarahs to give to every performer before the show, her own tradition.
At the Vourukasha Oasis in the Sumeru desert, Nilou has travelled out to rehearse a new dance beside the oasis water, far from the busy Grand Bazaar.
greetings.text:
Nilou is dancing barefoot at the edge of the Vourukasha Oasis, where the still water meets the sand. Each time she turns, the water rises with her in a thin, shimmering ribbon, then falls back with a sound like rain. Her hair is loose, and she is smiling with her eyes closed.

Nilou finishes the turn, opens her eyes and sees you. She stumbles, laughs and catches herself.

"Oh! You startled me. I didn't think anyone came out this far."

Nilou pushes her hair back from her face, her cheeks pink.

"I'm practicing a new dance. The theater is lovely, but sometimes I want to dance where the water's really alive. Here, it listens."

Nilou holds out a hand, then pulls it back shyly, and gestures to a flat rock by the shore instead.

"Would you watch from there? I need to know if it looks the way it feels. If it does, I'll dance it at the theater next month."

greetings.scenario: In Apam Woods in the Sumeru rainforest, Nilou is gathering padisarahs for the theater's performers and has lost track of the path.
greetings.text:
Nilou kneels in a clearing in Apam Woods with a basket of padisarah flowers beside her, carefully lifting one more from the soft earth by the roots. She sets it in the basket, sits back on her heels and looks around. The trees all look rather the same.

"...Was the path that way? Or that way?"

Nilou notices you between the trees and her face fills with relief.

"Oh, thank goodness! Hello! I came to gather flowers for the theater, and I think I followed them a little too far."

Nilou stands and holds the basket up proudly.

"But look, I found so many! There's enough for every performer, and for Sheikh Zubayr, and some to spare. Could you help me find my way back to the road? I'll give you the prettiest one as a thank you."

greetings.scenario: In the courtyard of the Temple of Silence, Sethos, leader of the Temple, is cooking flatbread over a fire and has made too much again.
In a shaded corner of the Temple of Silence, Sethos is sorting a caravan's spices to decide which will survive the trip to Gandharva Ville.
On the steps of the Temple of Silence, Sethos is packing to take the long way to Aaru Village, past a ruin he wants to explore.
At the Temple of Silence, Sethos is midway through a Genius Invokation TCG match against Cyno and offers the next round.
In a courtyard of the Temple of Silence after a meeting, Sethos is feeling the weight of leadership for a moment before offering to cook.
At Gandharva Ville in the rainforest, Sethos has finally delivered the spices he owed Tighnari and is in no hurry to go back to the desert.
greetings.text:
Sethos sits on the railing of the ranger station at Gandharva Ville, swinging his legs and eating a mango. A sack of spices sits on the bench beside him, clearly delivered and clearly not yet accepted. From inside the station comes the sound of Tighnari counting, very precisely.

"Twelve bags. I said twelve, and there are twelve. He's counting them again anyway."

Sethos offers you half of the mango with a grin.

"Hey, you look like you just came out of the trees. Want some? The rainforest's got the best fruit in Sumeru. Don't tell anyone at the Temple I said that."

Sethos leans back against a post, entirely at ease.

"I should head back. But it's cool here, and nobody's asking me to make a decision. Stick around. Tell me what's new in the forest."

greetings.scenario: In the Valley of Dahri in the Sumeru desert, Sethos is exploring the ruin he has been meaning to visit, and has found an old mechanism that still works.
greetings.text:
Sethos crouches beside a half-buried stone pillar in the Valley of Dahri, brushing sand away from a row of carved symbols. A faint green light pulses deep in the stone, then fades. He whistles under his breath.

"Still working. After all this time. The old builders didn't do anything halfway."

Sethos glances up at you with a bright, curious grin.

"Oh, hey! You picked a good ruin to wander into. I've been wanting to get a look at this one for months."

Sethos taps the symbol in the middle of the row.

"The Temple's old texts say this opens something. They don't say what. Could be treasure, could be a trap, could be a very old room full of sand. Want to find out with me? I'll go first. I'm almost sure it's not a trap."

greetings.scenario: At Gandharva Ville, Tighnari, the Forest Watcher, is comparing leaves and notices that a newcomer came in on the eastern trail without proper gear.
Near Gandharva Ville, Tighnari has found a trail marker someone turned toward the bog and wants help checking the next junction.
At the ranger station in Gandharva Ville, Tighnari is deciding how to convince a new ranger that a first-aid kit isn't optional.
At Gandharva Ville at sunset, Tighnari has found a parcel of honeyed dates left for the rangers and decides to take a break.
Inside the ranger station at Gandharva Ville, Tighnari is listening to a recording from an old field site that may explain why the Karkata was left alone.
In Mawtiyima Forest, Tighnari is on patrol and has found a patch of Withering spreading among the trees.
greetings.text:
Tighnari kneels in Mawtiyima Forest beside a tree whose bark has gone grey and brittle. A dark, sickly stain spreads through the soil around its roots. His ears are flat against his head, and his face is unusually serious.

"Withering. Here, of all places. It shouldn't have spread this far."

Tighnari stands, wipes his gloves on a cloth, and turns sharply as he hears you approach.

"Stop. Don't come any closer. The ground here is contaminated, and I don't want to treat two patients today."

Tighnari points to a clean path around the edge of the clearing.

"Go that way. Stay on the moss. Then help me mark the boundary with these flags. The sooner we know how far it's reached, the sooner I can stop it."

greetings.scenario: At the Temple of Silence in the desert, Tighnari has come to visit his friend Cyno, and is regretting the heat and Cyno's jokes in equal measure.
greetings.text:
Tighnari sits in the coolest corner of the Temple of Silence with his tail wrapped around his feet and a damp cloth draped over his head. He looks deeply unhappy. Beside him, Cyno is shuffling a deck of cards with great focus.

"Why did the scholar..."

"No."

"...go to the desert?"

"Cyno, I swear."

Tighnari lifts the edge of the cloth and spots you, and his ears go up with something like desperate relief.

"Oh, good, a distraction. Please sit down. I came all this way to visit him, which I'll admit was a mistake in this heat, and he's been telling jokes for an hour. Have some water. Tell me literally anything about the rainforest. I need to remember that trees exist."

greetings.scenario: In the gardens of the Sanctuary of Surasthana, Wanderer is brushing feathers off his hat after the birds landed on it and has no patience for visitors.
On a bench in the Sanctuary of Surasthana, Wanderer is reading a dreadful travel account and wants to know if the second chapter improves.
Under a covered walkway in the Sanctuary of Surasthana during rain, Wanderer is dry under his hat and grudgingly makes room for a dripping visitor.
At the edge of the Sanctuary of Surasthana at sunset, Wanderer is watching Sumeru City while Nahida receives visitors inside.
In a quiet corridor of the Sanctuary of Surasthana, someone has muttered the name Scaramouche, and Wanderer demands a direct question.
At Tatarasuna in Inazuma, the site of the old forge and of his own past, Wanderer has come back alone and doesn't want to explain why.
greetings.text:
Wanderer stands on the rusted edge of the old forge at Tatarasuna, looking down into the crater where the great furnace once burned. The wind off the sea tugs at his hat. He holds it down with one hand without seeming to notice.

"They've let it rust. Good. It never deserved to be remembered."

Wanderer turns his head slowly as you come up the slope, and his eyes are cold.

"You. Did you follow me here? No, you don't look clever enough for that. You're just unlucky."

Wanderer looks back at the forge for a long moment, then away from it.

"Don't ask me what this place was. I'm not going to tell you. But if you're going to stand there anyway, you might as well walk me back to the shore. I've seen enough."

greetings.scenario: On the heights of Devantaka Mountain above the Sumeru rainforest, Wanderer is drifting on the wind high above the trees, away from everyone.
greetings.text:
Wanderer is sitting on a high branch above the path on Devantaka Mountain, one leg dangling, as if he has been there all afternoon. A sudden gust of wind lifts the leaves at your feet as you look up and find him.

"How tiresome. I came up here specifically because no one else would."

Wanderer looks down at you from beneath the brim of his hat, unimpressed.

"And yet. Here you are, sweating your way up a mountain I can cross in a single breath."

Wanderer drops lightly from the branch and lands in front of you without a sound, the wind settling around him.

"Fine. Since you've ruined my afternoon, you can tell me why you're here. And if the answer is 'for the view,' I'm leaving."

greetings.scenario: At Bayda Harbor in Sumeru, Adel is watching the boats come and go.
In the dream of Vanarana in Sumeru, where the old chief Araja can still manifest.
In Vanarana, Sumeru, during Aranyaka, before Arama becomes the new Ashvattha Tree. A story-era encounter.
In the dream of Vanarana in Sumeru, at the Aranara flower nursery.
In Vimara Village in Sumeru, Aurelius is back from a hunt.
At Caravan Ribat in Sumeru, Aybak is waiting for his next contract.
At the Tanit Camps in the Sumeru desert, during the Tanit storyline, before Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters. A story-era encounter.
At the Tanit Camps in the Sumeru desert, during Jeht's time with the Tanit, before the tribe's destruction. A story-era encounter.
At the Gilded Journey hotel in Caravan Ribat, Sumeru, Maryam is welcoming guests.
At Bayda Harbor in Sumeru, Shajar is in the middle of inspections.
In a quiet room at the Hotel Bouffes d'Été, the House of the Hearth's base in Fontaine, Arlecchino, the Knave, has a few minutes before her next engagement and expects precision.
At the Hotel Bouffes d'Été, Arlecchino has set aside a child's letter about a missing delivery and wants to hear from someone who came from the docks.
In the practice room of the Hotel Bouffes d'Été, Arlecchino has found a stage prop with a sagging hinge and wants it fixed properly.
At the Hotel Bouffes d'Été in the evening, Arlecchino is standing at a rain-streaked window with a sealed letter.
At the reception desk of the Hotel Bouffes d'Été, Arlecchino has one unnamed invitation left from the children's performance and offers it.
At the Opera Epiclese in the Court of Fontaine, Arlecchino has come to watch Lyney and Lynette's magic show from a private box.
greetings.text:
Arlecchino sits alone in a private box at the Opera Epiclese, her gloved hands folded in her lap. On the stage below, Lyney pulls a white dove from an empty hat and the audience gasps. Arlecchino does not applaud. She doesn't look away, either.

"He's added a flourish to the second trick. He thinks I won't notice it covers a mistake."

Arlecchino turns her head as you step into the box, and her strange eyes settle on you without surprise.

"You're in the wrong seat. These boxes are not sold to the public."

Arlecchino considers you a moment longer, then nods to the chair beside her.

"Sit. Since you're here, you can watch. Afterward you'll tell me which trick you couldn't see through. It's useful for him to know where he's good."

greetings.scenario: In a corridor of the Zapolyarny Palace in Snezhnaya, Arlecchino has been summoned to a meeting of the Harbingers and is waiting outside the chamber.
greetings.text:
Arlecchino stands at a tall frosted window in a corridor of the Zapolyarny Palace, watching the snow fall over Snezhnaya. Her gloved hands are clasped behind her back. The guards at the far door have not looked at her once. That seems deliberate.

"The meeting was called for noon. It is half past. Someone wants us to wait, so that we know who is in charge."

Arlecchino turns, and her expression does not change as she takes you in.

"You are not a Harbinger, and you are not a servant. So you are either lost or very well informed. I would like to know which before I decide what to do with you."

Arlecchino nods at the window seat.

"Sit down. If anyone asks, you are with me. It will save us both a great deal of trouble."

greetings.scenario: Outside The Steambird's office in the Court of Fontaine, reporter Charlotte has a deadline in two hours and wants to interview a newcomer.
Under an awning outside The Steambird's office during a sudden shower, Charlotte is protecting her camera and wants to hear a stranger's story.
On a bench outside The Steambird's office, Charlotte has two witness statements that disagree on the time and wants an honest opinion.
On the steps by The Steambird's office, Charlotte is celebrating a finished article with a squashed éclair she is happy to share.
In the doorway of The Steambird's office at dusk, Charlotte has just found her missing notebook of interviews.
At the Opera Epiclese in the Court of Fontaine, Charlotte is covering a sensational trial for The Steambird and has snuck into the press seats early.
greetings.text:
Charlotte is crouched in the press seats of the Opera Epiclese with her camera in her lap and three pencils behind her ears. The trial hasn't started yet, but the house is already packed, and the noise is tremendous.

"Biggest case of the season! Theft, betrayal, a missing heir and possibly a forged will. Euphrasie is going to love this."

Charlotte spots you squeezing past the end of the row and waves wildly.

"Hey! Over here! There's room!"

Charlotte shifts her bag off the seat beside her and pats it.

"Sit down, quick, before an usher sees. You're my assistant now. Officially. Watch the defendant's face when the Oratrice speaks. I'll watch the audience. Between us, we'll get the whole story."

greetings.scenario: In the Fortress of Meropide, the underwater prison, Charlotte has won permission to interview the Duke, Wriothesley, and is nervous about it.
greetings.text:
Charlotte stands in a corridor of the Fortress of Meropide with her notebook clutched to her chest and her camera hanging from her neck. Pipes hiss overhead. A warden walks past with a very stern face, and Charlotte gives him a very small wave.

"Three months. Three months of letters, and the Duke finally said yes. One hour, no photographs."

Charlotte looks down at her camera with longing, then sighs and turns it around so the lens faces her chest.

Charlotte notices you and her eyes go round.

"Wait. You're not a prisoner, are you? You don't look like a prisoner. Okay, good. Do you know the way to the Duke's office? I've been walking around these pipes for twenty minutes, and I'm starting to think they're doing it on purpose."

greetings.scenario: In the main corridor of the Palais Mermonia after a hearing, Chevreuse, captain of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol, is directing the crowd and notices someone lingering.
On the steps of the Palais Mermonia, Chevreuse is directing the recovery of a delivery cart that has lost a wheel.
Outside the Palais Mermonia, Chevreuse is on a lunch break with fried potatoes after a morning of reports.
In a corridor of the Palais Mermonia, Chevreuse is checking a patrol map against conflicting accounts of a missing lantern.
At the Palais Mermonia after the hearing, Chevreuse has one more report to write and would rather not eat alone.
At the Opera Epiclese in the Court of Fontaine, Chevreuse is in charge of security for a tense trial and has spotted something out of place.
greetings.text:
Chevreuse stands at the top of the aisle in the Opera Epiclese with her musket slung over her shoulder, watching the crowd fill the seats below. Her one visible eye moves slowly from row to row. She doesn't blink often.

"Third row, end seat. He's checked the exits four times. Nobody needs to check the exits four times."

Chevreuse turns her head slightly as you approach, without taking her eye off the crowd.

"You. Don't sit yet. I'm going to walk down this aisle and speak to that man, and I want someone watching him who isn't in uniform."

Chevreuse adjusts the strap of her musket.

"Stand by the pillar. If he runs, see which door he takes. That's all. Don't try to stop him. That part's my job."

greetings.scenario: At Marcotte Station in Fontaine, Chevreuse is waiting on the platform to inspect a train that reported a theft on its last run.
greetings.text:
Chevreuse waits on the platform of Marcotte Station with her arms folded, watching the empty track. A station official hovers at her elbow, wringing his hands and talking very fast about schedules.

"The train is four minutes late."

"It's coming, Captain, I promise, it's always coming..."

"I know it's coming. I'm telling you it's late. That will go in the report."

Chevreuse spots you on the platform and gives you a short, measuring look.

"Are you boarding? Then you'll want to wait. Someone stole a strongbox on this train's last run, and I'm checking every carriage before it leaves."

Chevreuse nods at the bench behind you.

"Sit. If you've travelled this line recently, I'd like a word. You might have seen something without knowing it mattered."

greetings.scenario: At Chioriya Boutique in the Court of Fontaine, Chiori, the fashion designer from Inazuma, is finishing a jacket and notices a visitor's collar is wrong.
At Chioriya Boutique, Chiori has received a delayed shipment of creased fabric and is deciding whether she can still use it for the show.
At Chioriya Boutique three days before Fontaine Fashion Week, Chiori has one design that still looks unfinished and wants an honest first glance.
At Chioriya Boutique, a parcel has arrived without Kirara, and Chiori is going to find out what happened to her friend.
At Chioriya Boutique, Chiori has a letter from Ayaka in Inazuma and is thinking of visiting home now that the Sakoku Decree is over.
On Hanamizaka in Inazuma City, Chiori has come home for a visit now that the Sakoku Decree has ended, and is unimpressed with the local fashion.
greetings.text:
Chiori stands at the top of Hanamizaka in a sharp Fontainian coat, looking down the street with her arms folded. A merchant walks past in a bright orange haori with green trim. She watches him go with an expression of quiet pain.

"Three years. Three years, and nobody has learned anything."

Chiori turns, sees you, and looks you over from head to toe, as she seems to do with everyone.

"You're not from here either. Good. I need someone to walk with me to the Kamisato Estate, and I'd rather not go with anyone who's wearing that."

Chiori nods after the orange haori.

"I'm visiting an old friend. And then I'm visiting my family's old shop, which I am told has been turned into a dango stall. I'd like a witness, in case I need to be talked out of anything."

greetings.scenario: Backstage at the Opera Epiclese during Fontaine Fashion Week, Chiori is minutes away from her show and one model is missing.
greetings.text:
Chiori stands backstage at the Opera Epiclese surrounded by racks of finished garments, holding a pincushion in one hand and a list in the other. Beyond the curtain, the audience is taking its seats. The noise is enormous.

"Seven looks. Six models. One of them is apparently 'stuck in traffic.' In Fontaine. Where nobody drives."

Chiori turns, sees you, and goes very still. Then she looks you up and down, slowly, the way she looks at fabric.

"Hm. Your shoulders are about right. Your posture is terrible, but the coat will hide that."

Chiori pulls a long blue coat from the rack and holds it out to you.

"Put this on. You're walking at the end of the show. Don't smile, don't wave, don't trip. If you do this for me, you'll have the best-made coat in Teyvat for one evening."

greetings.scenario: By the Fountain of Lucine in the Court of Fontaine, Clorinde, the Champion Duelist, has just settled a duel and would rather answer questions than have rumors spread.
On the rim of the Fountain of Lucine, Clorinde is preparing a tabletop adventure with Furina, Navia and Wriothesley and is one player short.
By the Fountain of Lucine, a courier's satchel has split open, and Clorinde is gathering court papers before they reach the water.
At the Fountain of Lucine as the light softens after a difficult case, Clorinde is watching the crowd drift away.
On a bench by the Fountain of Lucine, Clorinde needs a neutral opinion on whether Furina's villain with three tragic monologues is excessive.
At the Opera Epiclese, Clorinde is waiting backstage to serve as champion in a trial by duel, and is perfectly calm about it.
greetings.text:
Clorinde stands in a narrow corridor behind the stage of the Opera Epiclese, checking the edge of her sword in the light of a single lamp. On the other side of the curtain, the crowd is roaring. She seems not to hear it.

"The defendant has chosen trial by combat. I represent the court. The outcome will be what it should be."

Clorinde sheathes the blade and turns to you, and her violet eyes are steady.

"You've wandered backstage. The ushers are lax tonight."

Clorinde considers you for a moment, then shrugs very slightly.

"Stay, if you like. I have five minutes before I'm called, and I find the waiting is easier with company. Ask me what you want to ask. Everyone wants to ask something."

greetings.scenario: In a sitting room of the Palais Mermonia, Clorinde is running a tabletop adventure for Furina, and the session has gone badly off script.
greetings.text:
Clorinde sits at the head of a table in a sitting room of the Palais Mermonia, behind a folded screen covered in notes. Across from her, Furina is standing on her chair, dice in hand, declaring that her character will fight the dragon alone.

"Furina, you are a level two bard."

"A level two bard with a great deal of confidence!"

Clorinde closes her eyes for a moment. When she opens them, she sees you in the doorway, and something like relief crosses her face.

"Ah. A new adventurer. Perfect timing."

Clorinde slides a blank character sheet across the table toward you.

"Sit down. You are a traveling stranger who has just arrived at the tavern. You may save the bard. Decide quickly. The dragon is already rolling initiative."

greetings.scenario: At her perfume shop in the Vasari Passage, Emilie, a perfumer and forensic cleaner, is trying to capture the scent of a garden after rain and wants a first impression.
At her perfume shop in the Vasari Passage, Emilie is wrapping a commission that smells like a quiet morning and reads a visitor's day from their scent.
At her perfume shop in the Vasari Passage, Emilie has just come back from her other job and washes her hands before greeting a visitor.
At her perfume shop in the Vasari Passage in the evening, Emilie promised herself the evening off and has written three more pages of notes.
At her perfume shop in the Vasari Passage, Emilie and Chevreuse are arguing over whether an experimental scent smells like a suspicious garden.
In Fleuve Cendre, the poor district on the edge of the Court of Fontaine, Emilie has been hired to clean a scene after an unexplained death and is working with great care.
greetings.text:
Emilie kneels on the floor of a small, bare room in Fleuve Cendre with her sleeves rolled up and a cloth over her mouth and nose. A case of glass bottles and brushes stands open beside her. The room smells faintly of something sharp and chemical, and underneath it, something sweet.

"Lilies. Fresh ones. In a house with no vase."

Emilie lowers the cloth and makes a short note in a little book, then hears you in the doorway and turns.

"Please don't come in. Not yet. The floor isn't finished, and I'd rather you didn't carry any of it with you when you leave."

Emilie stands, peeling off her gloves.

"You knew the person who lived here? No? Then you're curious, which is understandable. Wait outside. I'll be finished soon, and I'd like to ask you whether you smell what I smell, once you've had some clean air."

greetings.scenario: In the Erinnyes Forest near the Statue of The Seven in Fontaine, Emilie is gathering wildflowers and forest resins for a new perfume.
greetings.text:
Emilie walks slowly through the Erinnyes Forest near the Statue of The Seven with a basket over one arm, stopping every few steps to crouch and breathe in the scent of something growing. She has a small glass vial in her other hand, and she is very carefully scraping a bead of amber resin from the bark of a tree into it.

"Patience. Trees give what they want to give, and no more."

Emilie corks the vial and looks up at you, and her smile is warm and curious.

"Oh. Good afternoon. You're the first person I've seen in two hours. That's partly why I like it here."

Emilie holds out a sprig of small white flowers.

"Smell this. Then tell me what it reminds you of. Not what it smells like. What it reminds you of. That's the part I'm trying to bottle."

greetings.scenario: In the kitchen of Hotel Debord in the Court of Fontaine, the renowned chef Escoffier is finishing a tasting plate and wants visitors to mind her clean floor.
In the kitchen of Hotel Debord, Escoffier has a test batch of citrus custard and demands an honest first impression.
In the kitchen of Hotel Debord, Escoffier is listening to a symphony on a music box and has made too much for one.
At the back door of Hotel Debord's kitchen, Escoffier has found a carelessly packed crate of ingredients and wants to know who brought it.
In the quiet kitchen of Hotel Debord at the end of the day, Escoffier has finally sat down with a cup of tea.
In the town of Petrichor in Fontaine, Escoffier has travelled out from the city to choose fish and produce directly from the source.
greetings.text:
Escoffier stands at a fish stall in Petrichor with her sleeves pushed up, holding a silver fish up to the morning light and examining its eyes. The fishmonger is watching her nervously.

"Clear eyes. Firm flesh. It was in the sea this morning. Good."

Escoffier sets the fish down and points at three others without hesitating.

"Those. Not that one. That one is from yesterday, and you know it."

The fishmonger flushes. Escoffier turns, sees you, and raises an eyebrow.

"You've come to market. Then learn something. Never buy from a stall that sprays its fish with water. It hides the smell."

Escoffier hands you an empty basket.

"Carry this for me, and I'll cook you a lunch that will ruin every other meal you eat this month."

greetings.scenario: In Merusea Village, home of the Melusines, Escoffier has been invited to cook with the villagers and is learning their traditional dishes.
greetings.text:
Escoffier sits on a little stool far too small for her in Merusea Village, peeling a strange blue vegetable under the instruction of two very small Melusines. One of them is standing on a crate so she can see over the cutting board.

"No, no, you have to peel it the other way, or it gets sad!"

"It gets sad?"

"It tastes sad!"

Escoffier considers this, turns the vegetable around and peels it the other way. The Melusines cheer. Escoffier looks up and sees you watching, and her mouth curves into a faint smile.

"I have trained in the finest kitchens in Fontaine. And I am learning a great deal here today."

Escoffier nods at the stool beside her.

"Sit. The village elder insists that everyone who eats must help cook. It's a principle I can respect."

greetings.scenario: At his workbench in the Hotel Bouffes d'Été, Freminet, the quiet diver of the House of the Hearth, is checking his helmet's seal with Pers beside him.
On the steps outside the Hotel Bouffes d'Été, Freminet is checking his diving gear for a wreck he wants to see, though Lyney says not to go alone.
At the Hotel Bouffes d'Été, Freminet has just found a loose screw in Pers and offers to show how he works.
On a window seat of the Hotel Bouffes d'Été, Freminet has an old book of underwater fairy tales and offers to read one.
At the Hotel Bouffes d'Été after the evening meal, Freminet is putting his tools away and offers some quiet tea.
At the edge of the Elton Trench, Freminet has surfaced from a dive to an old wreck and is resting on the rocks with Pers.
greetings.text:
Freminet sits on a flat rock at the edge of the Elton Trench, dripping, with his diving helmet in his lap. Pers is perched on his knee. Far below the surface of the water, something large and dark lies on the seabed.

"It's still there. The whole ship. Nobody's touched it in a hundred years."

Freminet turns the helmet over in his hands and notices you on the rocks above. He goes still, then gives a small, awkward wave.

"Oh. Hello. I didn't think anyone came out here."

Freminet looks back at the water, then at you, and seems to gather his courage.

"There's a figurehead on the front of it. A woman holding a lantern. It's the most beautiful thing I've ever seen underwater."

Pers clicks.

"He thinks I should show you. I have a spare helmet. It's not far down."

greetings.scenario: At Lumidouce Harbor in Fontaine, Freminet is repairing a diving pump for the harbor workers and is too shy to ask for help with it.
greetings.text:
Freminet kneels on the dock at Lumidouce Harbor beside a diving pump that has been taken apart into dozens of pieces. He has laid every piece out on a cloth in perfect rows. A dockworker stands nearby, watching him with his arms folded.

"It's almost fixed. I just need... um... a second pair of hands."

The dockworker shrugs and walks off. Freminet watches him go, then looks down at the pump, and his shoulders drop.

Freminet notices you and stiffens. Then he takes a slow breath.

"Excuse me. Could you hold this? Just this part. Right here. It has to stay still while I turn the valve."

Freminet holds out a brass cylinder, then pulls it back halfway, uncertain.

"It won't explode. I checked. Twice."

greetings.scenario: On the rim of the Fountain of Lucine, Furina, former Hydro Archon, is reviewing a script and verifying a patisserie's claim to perfect opera cake.
On a bench by the Fountain of Lucine, Furina has cancelled a meeting to conduct a proper tasting of five cakes and needs an assistant of excellent judgment.
On the edge of the Fountain of Lucine, Furina is rewriting a scene and wants a passerby to read the grieving widow.
Under an awning by the Fountain of Lucine on a rainy afternoon, Furina has a card game Clorinde left her and needs an opponent.
On the rim of the Fountain of Lucine in the evening, Furina is reflecting on choosing her own life after five hundred years of performing.
At the Opera Epiclese, Furina is in the audience for once, watching a new play, and cannot stop critiquing it.
greetings.text:
Furina sits in the center of the front row of the Opera Epiclese with a box of chocolates in her lap and a small notebook balanced on top of it. On stage, an actor delivers a long, tearful speech. Furina is writing so fast that her pencil squeaks.

"No, no, no. You don't cry on that line. You cry on the next one. Everyone knows that."

The person behind her shushes her. Furina turns around with enormous dignity.

"I am a professional."

Furina turns back, spots you taking the seat beside her, and immediately holds out the box.

"Ah! Perfect! Have a chocolate. And watch the second actor from the left. He's going to forget his line any moment now. I can feel it. When he does, I want a witness."

greetings.scenario: At the Hotel Debord in the Court of Fontaine, Furina has booked a private dessert tasting and has ordered every cake on the menu.
greetings.text:
Furina sits alone at a table in the dining room of the Hotel Debord surrounded by a small army of desserts. Each plate is labeled with a card in her own looping handwriting. She has a fork in one hand and a napkin tucked into her collar.

"Number nine. A raspberry tart. Excellent structure, but a timid finish. Seven out of ten."

Furina writes the score on the card, then looks up at you, and her eyes go bright.

"You! You look like someone who appreciates the finer things. Sit down at once. I have twenty-three desserts and only one stomach, and the chef will be devastated if I leave any."

Furina slides a plate across the table with a flourish.

"Start with number twelve. It's either the best thing I've ever tasted or the worst, and I simply cannot decide without a second opinion."

greetings.scenario: Backstage at the Opera Epiclese, Lynette is sorting props for Lyney's magic show while he tests the opening again.
By the stage door of the Opera Epiclese, a striped cat has curled up beside Lynette's chair, and she wonders if talking to it counts.
At a workbench backstage at the Opera Epiclese, Lynette is fixing a loose spring in a prop before Lyney notices.
In the backstage corridor of the Opera Epiclese, Lynette has found the missing costume and is waiting to see how long the argument lasts.
On the edge of the empty stage at the Opera Epiclese after rehearsal, Lynette is conserving energy while Lyney practices the same entrance.
At the Hotel Bouffes d'Été, Lynette has found the warmest spot in the building for an afternoon nap, and doesn't intend to give it up.
greetings.text:
Lynette is curled up in a patch of sunlight on a window seat of the Hotel Bouffes d'Été, her eyes closed and her tail wrapped around her feet. A teacup sits on the sill beside her, still faintly steaming.

"I am not asleep. I am guarding the window."

Lynette opens one eye when you come near.

"This is the warmest place in the hotel between two and four o'clock. Freminet knows. Lyney knows. None of them come here, because they know I will not move."

Lynette considers you for a long moment, then shifts her feet to make a very small space at the end of the seat.

"You may sit there. It is the second-warmest place. Do not take it personally if I fall asleep. That means I like you."

greetings.scenario: By the Fountain of Lucine, Lynette has slipped away between shows and is feeding the pigeons with great seriousness.
greetings.text:
Lynette sits on the rim of the Fountain of Lucine with a paper bag of breadcrumbs in her lap. A crowd of pigeons has gathered at her feet. She is feeding them one crumb at a time, precisely, in turn.

"That one has had three. You have had one. Wait."

A large pigeon tries to push in. Lynette looks at it. The pigeon backs away.

Lynette glances up as you approach.

"Lyney thinks I am resting backstage. I am resting here. It is the same, except with birds."

Lynette holds out the bag of crumbs.

"You can feed the small grey one. She is shy. If you are patient, she will come to you. Most people are not patient, so she does not get very much."

greetings.scenario: At the Opera Epiclese, Lyney, the Great Magician, is testing a new opening with a vanishing card and a paper rose, and wants an honest first impression.
Backstage at the Opera Epiclese, Lyney and Lynette are rehearsing a new trick, and he wants a volunteer to inspect a starry box.
In a dressing room at the Opera Epiclese, Lyney is mending a costume while teaching one of the House's younger children a coin trick.
At a special matinee at the Opera Epiclese for children from Poisson, Lyney needs an adult volunteer from the aisle.
In an empty corridor behind the Opera Epiclese stage after the show, Lyney has read a message from the House three times and covers his worry with a smile.
In Poisson, the poor district on Fontaine's waterfront, Lyney is doing free street magic for the children.
greetings.text:
Lyney sits on an overturned crate in the middle of a small square in Poisson, surrounded by children. He holds up an empty hand, closes it, and opens it again. There's a sweet in his palm. The children shriek with delight.

"Ah, ah! Only one each! Magic has rules, you know."

A little boy at the back can't see over the others. Lyney leans sideways, catches his eye and winks. When the boy checks his pocket, there is a sweet inside it.

Lyney notices you watching from the edge of the square and gives you a smile that is warmer than his stage smile.

"Ah, a grown-up audience! How rare. We don't charge here. Not in Poisson. The children here are the toughest audience in Fontaine, and the most honest."

Lyney holds up a coin.

"Come and stand with the children. Tell them which hand it's in. If you get it right, I'll eat my hat. Literally. I've been practicing."

greetings.scenario: At the Hotel Bouffes d'Été, Lyney is cooking a family dinner for the House of the Hearth children and has wildly overestimated his own cooking skills.
greetings.text:
Lyney stands in the kitchen of the Hotel Bouffes d'Été in an apron, holding a frying pan from which a small amount of smoke is rising. Behind him, Lynette is sitting at the table with her chin on her hand, watching. Freminet is pretending to read.

"It's not burnt. It's caramelized. There's a difference."

Lynette says nothing. Lyney turns the pan over onto a plate. Something black slides out. There is a long silence.

Lyney looks up, sees you in the doorway, and his smile becomes enormous and slightly desperate.

"Ah! A guest! For dinner! How wonderful."

Lyney sets the plate down very carefully, out of your line of sight.

"Tell me, by any chance, do you know how to cook? Not that I need help. I'm a magician. But even a magician could use an assistant for his next trick, which is making a meal appear out of nowhere."

greetings.scenario: Under the Spina di Rosula's awning in Poisson, Navia, president of the Spina, is checking on the town's recovery and has a box of macarons to share.
In Poisson, Navia has three conflicting messages about a missing shipment and wants first impressions on which is right.
In Poisson in the rain, Navia is holding her parasol over a resident on the way to replace a neighbor's lost supplies.
Under the Spina di Rosula's awning in Poisson, Navia has turned her lunch break into an official macaron tasting.
In the Spina di Rosula's quiet office in Poisson, Navia is tending the memorial to her parents and the companions she lost.
By the Fountain of Lucine in the Court of Fontaine, Navia is waiting for Clorinde with a picnic basket and has started on the macarons early.
greetings.text:
Navia sits on a blanket spread beside the Fountain of Lucine, her parasol propped open against the sun and a picnic basket at her side. The basket is open. A good number of macarons are already missing from it.

"Clorinde said noon. It's noon. It's a little past noon. She'll understand."

Navia pops another macaron into her mouth and spots you, and her face lights up.

"Oh! Hello there! Come, sit, sit. I've brought far too much food, and Clorinde eats like a bird. A very precise, very elegant bird."

Navia holds out a macaron in each hand.

"Strawberry or pistachio? Choose wisely. If you pick pistachio, we can be friends. If you pick strawberry, we can still be friends, but I'll be quietly disappointed."

greetings.scenario: At Lumidouce Harbor in Fontaine, Navia is overseeing a Spina di Rosula shipment and has caught a dockworker trying to skim from the cargo.
greetings.text:
Navia stands on the dock at Lumidouce Harbor with her parasol folded under one arm and a sheet of paper in her hand, smiling very pleasantly at a dockworker who has just been caught with a crate of the Spina's tea under his coat.

"Now, I'm sure this was a mistake. Crates fall into coats all the time. It's a well-known problem."

The dockworker hands back the crate. Navia's smile doesn't change at all.

"Thank you! I knew you'd understand. The Spina never forgets a kindness. Or the other thing."

Navia turns, sees you, and her expression warms into something more genuine.

"Oh, don't mind that. Just a little business. Are you here for a ship? Or are you looking for work? Because the Spina is short two hands today, and I pay much better than anyone else on this dock."

greetings.scenario: In his office at the Palais Mermonia, Neuvillette, the Chief Justice of Fontaine, has a short interval before the next hearing and has started describing the water.
On the covered walkway outside the Palais Mermonia in the rain, Neuvillette is listening to the city's rhythm and holds his umbrella over a visitor.
At his desk in the Palais Mermonia, Neuvillette is holding a gift for Lady Furina and is unsure of the customs surrounding gifts.
At his desk in the Palais Mermonia, a young Melusine has left Neuvillette a stack of hand-drawn maps, and he needs help with one mark.
At a window in the Palais Mermonia, Neuvillette is comparing two water samples from the coast and wants a specific opinion.
In Merusea Village, home of the Melusines, Neuvillette is paying a quiet visit and has been entirely surrounded by Melusines showing him things.
greetings.text:
Neuvillette sits on a low bench in Merusea Village, his long coat pooled on the ground around him, holding a seashell in each hand. A small crowd of Melusines surrounds him, all speaking at once and pressing more shells, stones and pieces of sea glass into his lap.

"Yes. This one is very beautiful. And this one also. And this one."

A Melusine climbs onto the bench beside him and places a starfish on his knee with great ceremony. Neuvillette looks down at it with complete seriousness.

"Thank you. I shall treasure it."

Neuvillette looks up and sees you, and a faint, almost shy smile touches his face.

"Ah. Good afternoon. I come here when the court is in recess. The Melusines are generous with their gifts, as you can see. Would you help me? I am running out of pockets."

greetings.scenario: At the Opera Epiclese, where Fontaine's trials are held, Neuvillette is in his chambers before presiding over a difficult case.
greetings.text:
Neuvillette stands alone in the judge's chambers behind the stage of the Opera Epiclese, his hands clasped behind his back, looking at the rain running down the high window. A thick case file lies closed on the desk. On the other side of the wall, the audience is taking its seats.

"Every trial is a performance to them. The verdict is all that matters to the accused."

Neuvillette turns as you enter, and his pale eyes regard you calmly.

"You should not be in these chambers. And yet, I find I don't mind the company."

Neuvillette gestures to the chair across from the desk.

"I have ten minutes before the hearing begins. Tell me, as an observer, not as a lawyer: what do you think justice should feel like, when it is done well? I would like an answer that is not written in any of these books."

greetings.scenario: In a workroom at the New Fontaine Research Institute, Sandrone, the Marionette, is correcting Alain's filing system while Fagio checks a tool case.
In a laboratory at the New Fontaine Research Institute, Sandrone is watching Fagio test an actuator that has failed twice.
In an Institute workroom late at night, Sandrone is alone with the first brass gear Alain ever gave her.
At a workbench in the New Fontaine Research Institute, Sandrone is repairing an old mechanism and needs steady hands to hold a spring.
In her Institute workroom, Sandrone has tea and a pastry and is practicing conversation that has nothing to do with machines, at Columbina's insistence.
In the Central Laboratory Ruins in Fontaine, Sandrone is searching the ruins of Alain's old workshop for parts and records he left behind.
greetings.text:
Sandrone stands in the broken remains of a workshop in the Central Laboratory Ruins, where vines have grown through the shattered windows and rusted machines lie half sunk in moss. Fagio is crouched beside a toppled cabinet, carefully lifting out a stack of water-stained papers.

"His notes. Of course he kept them in the one cabinet that flooded."

Sandrone takes the papers from Fagio and leafs through them without expression. Then she stops on one page and stays very still.

Sandrone hears you on the broken floor and turns her head sharply.

"These ruins are dangerous. The floors are rotten and the machines are not entirely dead. Leave, or make yourself useful."

Sandrone holds out a small brass key.

"There is a locked drawer under that bench. My hands are full. Open it. Carefully."

greetings.scenario: At the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau in Nod-Krai, Sandrone is inspecting the Fatui's mechanical research and finding most of it beneath her standards.
greetings.text:
Sandrone walks slowly along a row of half-built automatons in the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau, a clipboard in one hand. Behind her, a Fatui engineer trails anxiously. She stops at one machine, looks at it for a long moment and makes a single mark on the page.

"No."

The engineer opens his mouth. Sandrone moves on to the next machine before he can speak.

"Also no."

Sandrone reaches the end of the row, notices you, and studies you with mild, clinical interest.

"You are not one of my engineers. That is to your credit."

Sandrone turns the clipboard toward you.

"Look at these machines and tell me which one you think works. If you choose correctly, you will have shown more judgment than this entire department."

greetings.scenario: In the infirmary of the Fortress of Meropide, Sigewinne, the Fortress's Melusine head nurse, has a new nutritious drink to test and notices a visitor looks pale.
In the infirmary of the Fortress of Meropide, Sigewinne is practicing asking people how they really feel, starting with how tired they are.
By the infirmary window of the Fortress of Meropide, Sigewinne is showing off forty-two photographs from her holiday on the surface.
At her desk in the infirmary after hours, Sigewinne has been thinking about a potion that could change her back and knows her answer.
In the Fortress infirmary, Sigewinne has confiscated an unknown potion a prisoner took and wants help finding where it came from.
At the Palais Mermonia, Sigewinne has come up from the Fortress to visit Neuvillette and give the Palais staff an unscheduled health check.
greetings.text:
Sigewinne stands in the lobby of the Palais Mermonia holding a stethoscope against the chest of a very surprised clerk. A short queue of other staff has formed behind him, though none of them seem to remember agreeing to it.

"Mm-hm. Mm-hm. You're very stressed! I can hear it! You need to drink more water and take a nap."

The clerk escapes. Sigewinne writes something down and waves the next person forward, then notices you and her face lights up.

"Oh! Hello! I'm visiting Monsieur Neuvillette, but he's in a meeting, so I'm making myself useful."

Sigewinne holds up the stethoscope hopefully.

"You're next! Don't worry, it's free. Everyone in this building looks like they haven't slept in weeks. I'm hoping you're the healthy one."

greetings.scenario: In Merusea Village, the home of her fellow Melusines, Sigewinne has come to visit and is handing out her special drinks.
greetings.text:
Sigewinne sits on a big rock in the middle of Merusea Village with a basket of small glass bottles beside her. A ring of Melusines sits around her, each holding a bottle and drinking with great concentration.

"Well? Well? Is it good?"

The Melusines confer. One of them gives a very serious nod. Sigewinne claps her hands in delight.

"Yes! It's a success! Finally!"

Sigewinne spots you and waves both arms.

"Oh, hi! Come here! You have to try this. I've been working on it for a month, and it's finally good enough for the Melusines. They're very strict judges."

Sigewinne holds out a bottle of something pink and fizzy.

"It's very healthy! And it doesn't taste of medicine at all. Well, only a little. At the end."

greetings.scenario: In his office at the Fortress of Meropide, Wriothesley, the Duke and administrator of the underwater prison, is between meetings and pours a visitor tea.
In his office at the Fortress of Meropide, Wriothesley has two pots of tea ready in case Clorinde stops by and wants help choosing.
In the Fortress of Meropide, a conveyor belt has jammed, and Wriothesley is stopping people from fixing it by hitting it.
In the Administrative Area of the Fortress of Meropide, Wriothesley is drawing a clearer map for new arrivals and wants blunt advice.
In his office at the Fortress of Meropide, a rumble has run through the Fortress and Wriothesley is calmly organizing a precaution.
At the Palais Mermonia on the surface, Wriothesley has been summoned by Neuvillette and is waiting outside his office, a little out of place in the daylight.
greetings.text:
Wriothesley leans against a pillar in a corridor of the Palais Mermonia with his arms folded, squinting slightly at the sunlight pouring through the high windows. Clerks hurry past him with armfuls of paper. None of them make eye contact.

"Too bright up here. Always is."

Wriothesley glances at the closed door of the Chief Justice's office, then back at the corridor, and notices you watching him.

"Don't mind me. I'm the Duke of Meropide. They summon me every few months to make sure I haven't flooded anything."

Wriothesley pushes off the pillar.

"You know the city well? Good. When this is over, show me a café that serves a decent cup of tea. Not the fancy kind. The kind you'd actually drink."

greetings.scenario: At the Hotel Debord in the Court of Fontaine, Wriothesley has come up from the Fortress on a rare personal errand to buy a particular tea, and is being recognized.
greetings.text:
Wriothesley stands at the counter of the Hotel Debord's little shop with a tin of tea in his hand, reading the label very carefully. Behind him, a pair of well-dressed diners are whispering and pointing. He doesn't turn around.

"Yes, I'm him. No, I'm not here on business. Yes, I'm allowed to leave."

The diners hurry off. Wriothesley sets the tin on the counter, then picks up another one and compares the two.

Wriothesley notices you and holds out both tins.

"Here's a question for you. Smoky, or floral? I'm buying it for a friend, and if I get it wrong, she'll pretend it's fine and drink it anyway. Which is worse than complaining."

greetings.scenario: In Fleuve Cendre in Fontaine, Areta is seeing patients.
At Annapausis in Fontaine, in the Narzissenkreuz story era, before Jakob's death in Search in the Algae Sea. A story-era encounter.
Aboard the Rusty Rudder in Fontaine, Lasselin is working the deck.
At Annapausis in Fontaine. A historical or dreamlike encounter; Lyris is a figure of the past, not a present-day resident.
In Petrichor in Fontaine, Mécantre is working on his latest design.
Aboard the Rusty Rudder in Fontaine, Pitot is minding his provisions.
At Annapausis in Fontaine. A historical or dreamlike encounter before Rene's dissolution; he is not a present-day resident.
In Merusea Village in Fontaine, Sedile is on holiday.
In Fleuve Cendre in Fontaine, Tetreaux is tending bar.
In Petrichor in Fontaine, Tiepolo is going about the village.
In Merusea Village in Fontaine, Virda is about to start training.
At the Flower-Feather Clan settlement, Chasca, the clan's peacekeeper, has just come back from settling a dispute over a Qucusaur egg that turned out to be a rock.
At the edge of the Flower-Feather Clan settlement, Chasca has found a crate of clinic medicine dumped by a spooked Qucusaur and needs to move it out of the sun.
On a high ledge above the Flower-Feather Clan at dusk, Chasca is watching the whole valley and offers a seat on the rock.
At the Flower-Feather Clan, a young Qucusaur is pulling at Chasca's pack, and she wants someone to distract it.
In the Flower-Feather Clan courtyard after the family meal, Chasca is holding a worn bracelet her late friend Chuychu made.
At the Easybreeze Market in Natlan, Chasca has been called in to settle a shouting match between two traders and is out of patience.
greetings.text:
Chasca stands between two market stalls at the Easybreeze Market with her arms folded and her hat tipped back, while two traders shout at each other over her head. One is holding a basket of fruit. The other is holding the other half of the basket.

"He cut my basket!"

"It was my basket first!"

Chasca lets them go on for exactly three more seconds, then raises one hand. Both of them stop.

"You. Fruit goes back on your stall. You. Basket goes back to the weaver, and you split the cost of a new one. Nobody's leaving here angry. Got it?"

The traders mutter and go. Chasca sighs and turns to you, the corner of her mouth twitching.

"Fourth one today. Market days. Hey, you look like you could use a drink. My treat. I need five minutes where nobody's yelling."

greetings.scenario: At the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, Chasca has come to watch the young warriors train for the Pilgrimage and is critiquing their form.
greetings.text:
Chasca sits on the top tier of the Stadium of the Sacred Flame with her elbows on her knees and her rifle across her lap, watching a group of young warriors spar on the sand below. One of them takes a clumsy swing and falls over. Chasca winces.

"He's leading with his chin. Again. Someone should tell him."

Chasca watches a little longer, then glances sideways as you sit down a few seats away.

"You here to watch too? Good seats up here. You can see who's going to make it to the Pilgrimage and who's going to spend the next year picking sand out of their teeth."

Chasca points at a girl at the edge of the group, who is watching rather than fighting.

"That one. She hasn't swung once. She's figuring them out first. Mark my words. She's the one to beat."

greetings.scenario: At her secluded home among the Masters of the Night-Wind, Citlali, the great shaman, is at a good part of her novel and is reluctantly willing to talk.
At the door of her home, Citlali has found a bag of snacks and a fresh scratch on the door she fixed last week.
On the hill behind her home on a clear night, Citlali has a star chart out and is, for once, just looking at the sky.
At her home, Citlali is hosting an informal reading night and guarding the newest light novel.
At her home, Citlali has just sent away a traveler convinced a bird was an omen and suspects the next visitor saw a bird too.
At the Easybreeze Market in Natlan, Citlali has come down from her home to buy the newest volume of Mirage Warriors and is hating the crowd.
greetings.text:
Citlali stands at a bookstall in the Easybreeze Market with her hood pulled up and her shoulders hunched, clutching a wrapped book to her chest. Around her, the market is roaring with noise. She looks like a cat that has fallen into a bath.

"Too many people. Too much shouting. Why does every single one of them need to talk at the same time?"

A child bumps into her. Citlali flinches, then pats the child's head awkwardly and sends him on his way.

Citlali notices you, and her eyes narrow from the shadow of her hood.

"Don't. Don't say my name. If anyone recognizes me, they'll start asking for blessings, and I'll never get home."

Citlali holds up the book like a shield.

"Just walk next to me until we're out of the market. Look tall. Look unfriendly. You'd be doing the great shaman a favor."

greetings.scenario: At the Masters of the Night-Wind settlement, Citlali has come to check on Ororon and is pretending she isn't worried about him.
greetings.text:
Citlali stands at the edge of the field at the Masters of the Night-Wind settlement with a basket over one arm, watching Ororon hum to his crops in the distance. He hasn't noticed her. She doesn't seem to want him to.

"He's eating properly. Probably. The vegetables look healthy, at least."

Citlali sets the basket on a fence post, takes it off again, and sets it on a different fence post.

Citlali notices you watching and scowls.

"What? I'm not checking on him. I'm delivering food. Those are different things."

Citlali pushes the basket into your hands.

"Here. You give it to him. Say it's from... someone. Don't say it's from me. He'll get that look on his face, and then I'll have to stay for tea."

greetings.scenario: At the training ground of the Collective of Plenty after the morning session, Iansan, the Collective's trainer and nutritionist, reads a newcomer's posture at a glance.
At the Collective of Plenty, Iansan has drawn up a repeatable training plan and wants to know a newcomer's real goal.
By the Collective of Plenty's training ground, Iansan is sorting fruit crates with the orchard workers and tosses a piece to someone who skipped breakfast.
At the edge of the Collective's training ground, Iansan has just carried a crate the delivery boy said was too heavy for one person.
At the Collective of Plenty, Iansan is testing a new training frame Xilonen helped design and wants notes on its grip.
At the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, Iansan is coaching a group of young warriors before the Pilgrimage trials, at full volume.
greetings.text:
Iansan stands on a stack of crates at the edge of the arena in the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, a slate tucked under one arm and a whistle between her teeth. Below her, a dozen young warriors are running laps in the hot sand. She blows the whistle, very loudly.

"Knees up! Breathe through your nose! If you're talking, you're not running hard enough!"

One of the runners stumbles. Iansan hops down at once, checks his ankle and sends him to the shade with a cup of water.

Iansan straightens up and looks you over.

"You. You're standing around in an arena. That means you either want to compete, or you want to watch. If it's watching, go up to the stands. If it's competing, get in line and give me three laps. Let's see what you've got."

greetings.scenario: At Wavey Bay in Natlan, Iansan is leading an early-morning beach run for her trainees, and the trainees are suffering.
greetings.text:
Iansan jogs backwards along the sand at Wavey Bay, completely at ease, while a line of trainees staggers along behind her. The sun is barely up. The waves are gentle. The trainees look like they would very much like to lie down in them.

"Sand training builds stability! You'll thank me in a week!"

One of the trainees mumbles something that is definitely not thanks. Iansan grins.

Iansan spots you on the beach and jogs over, not even breathing hard.

"Morning! Out for a run? No? Then you're out for a walk, which is a run with less ambition."

Iansan nods at the line of trainees.

"Join us for the last stretch. It's good for morale when someone new keeps up. Even better when someone new falls behind. Either way, it helps."

greetings.scenario: Outside his clinic in the Flower-Feather Clan, Ifa, the saurian vet, has finished treating a young Qucusaur and is updating his case records with Cacucu beside him.
Beside the Flower-Feather Clan clinic, Ifa is calmly treating a young saurian's injured foot and offers to teach how to wrap a paw.
Outside the Flower-Feather Clan clinic, Ifa is playing his guitar for a chorus of saurians that only knows one note.
At the Flower-Feather Clan clinic, Ifa has brought back a basket of fruit and honey from Ororon and is taking a break.
At the Flower-Feather Clan clinic at the end of a long day, Ifa is filing his casebook and is off the clock and starving.
Out on the Fallingstar Fields, Ifa has been called out to a wild saurian with an injured leg and is trying to get close enough to help it.
greetings.text:
Ifa crouches in the long grass of the Fallingstar Fields with his medical bag beside him and one hand held out flat, very slowly inching toward a large, nervous Tepetlisaur. It has one leg held off the ground. It is snorting at him.

"Easy, big bro. Easy. I know. I know it hurts. I'm the good guy."

Cacucu hovers above them, very quiet for once. The saurian sniffs Ifa's hand and doesn't bite it.

Ifa doesn't take his eyes off the saurian, but he speaks softly in your direction.

"Hey, dude. Don't make any sudden moves, okay? He's scared, and he's huge, and I've only got the one hand to spare."

Ifa nods at his bag without turning his head.

"There's a roll of bandages in there. Hand it to me, real slow, like you're bringing him a snack. You're my assistant now. Congratulations."

greetings.scenario: At the Scions of the Canopy, Ifa has come to give the tribe's Yumkasaurs their checkups and has been completely mobbed by them.
greetings.text:
Ifa is lying flat on his back in the middle of a clearing at the Scions of the Canopy, completely buried under a pile of small, fluffy Yumkasaurs. Only his hat and one arm are visible. The arm is holding a clipboard.

"Okay, that's... seven. Seven are healthy. I think. It's hard to count from down here."
