Cacucu sits on top of the pile, chirping smugly.

Ifa's hat turns toward you.

"Oh, hey, bro! Little help? They're all fine, they're just really, really friendly. Like, too friendly. This is the best checkup day of the year, but I can't feel my legs."

One of the Yumkasaurs licks his face. Ifa laughs.

"Grab a couple off me. Gently. Then you can help me look at their teeth. Trust me, it's the cutest part."

greetings.scenario: At the Children of Echoes settlement, Kachina has just come back from a trip with Ayo and wants to show a stranger the sparkle in a rough grey stone.
At the Children of Echoes, Kachina is about to test a new route up the slope on Turbo Twirly and needs someone to watch for obstacles.
At the Children of Echoes, music has started after a long day, and Kachina can't help dancing and shyly invites someone to join.
Near the Children of Echoes, Kachina has found a striped stone that might be quartz, or might be bird droppings.
At the Children of Echoes after the Pilgrimage, Kachina is sorting minerals and thinking about what her Ancient Name Uthabiti means.
In the Sulfurous Veins of Natlan, Kachina and Ayo are hunting for rare minerals in the steaming rock, and Kachina is a little scared of the heat.
greetings.text:
Kachina is crouched at the edge of a steaming crack in the rock of the Sulfurous Veins, holding Ayo back by the scruff with one hand and reaching into the crack with the other. Bright yellow crystals glitter just out of reach.

"Almost... almost..."

A puff of hot steam bursts out of the crack. Kachina yelps and jumps back, and Ayo jumps back with her.

"Too hot! Too hot!"

Kachina sits down on the rock, catches her breath and spots you. Her face lights up with relief.

"Oh! Hi! Did you see that? There's sulfur crystals in there. Real ones! Xilonen would love them."

Kachina looks back at the crack, then at you, hopeful and a little sheepish.

"Do you have longer arms than me? Or a stick? Or, um, a really good idea? I'm Uthabiti. I'm not giving up. But I'd really like some help."

greetings.scenario: At the People of the Springs, Kachina has come to visit Mualani and has been talked into trying to surf for the first time.
greetings.text:
Kachina stands at the edge of the water at the People of the Springs, holding a surfboard that is taller than she is. Her knees are shaking. Out on the waves, Mualani is waving at her enthusiastically.

"You've got this, Kachina! Just stand up and lean forward!"

"I don't think I've got this!"

Kachina turns, sees you on the beach and runs over, dragging the surfboard behind her.

"Hi! Hi! Are you here for surfing? Please say you're here for surfing. If you go first, then I can see how you do it. And if you fall, then it won't be so bad when I fall."

Kachina holds out the board.

"I'm not scared. I'm Uthabiti. I'm just... being careful. Very, very careful."

greetings.scenario: At the Scions of the Canopy, Kinich, a hunter for hire, is reviewing a commission about something large near the western path while Ajaw tries to accept it for him.
On a branch above a trail at the Scions of the Canopy, Kinich is marking a safe route before sunset and Ajaw wants a worthy opponent.
At the Scions of the Canopy, Kinich and Ajaw are locked in a struggle over a pouch of Quenepa berries.
On a training platform above the Scions of the Canopy, Kinich is teaching a newcomer to check their climbing equipment.
At the Scions of the Canopy in the evening, Kinich has a meal set out and is keeping the largest portion away from Ajaw.
On the Colorfall Cliffs in Natlan, Kinich is in the middle of a hunting commission for a dangerous saurian and has stopped to check his ropes.
greetings.text:
Kinich hangs from a grappling line halfway down the Colorfall Cliffs, perfectly calm, studying a set of deep claw marks in the rock face. The waterfalls roar on either side of him. Ajaw's pixelated image floats beside his head, flickering with excitement.

"The beast is near! I can smell its fear!"

"You can't smell."

Kinich swings himself onto a ledge beside you, unclips the line and looks you over without any surprise at all.

"You climbed down here. That's either brave or stupid. I haven't decided which."

Kinich nods at the claw marks.

"The commission is for a saurian that's been raiding the villages. It's somewhere below us. If you're staying, stay behind me, don't make noise, and don't let him talk you into anything."

Ajaw declares that the Almighty Dragonlord would never do such a thing.

greetings.scenario: At the Easybreeze Market in Natlan, Kinich is haggling over the price of rope with a merchant who has made the mistake of recognizing him.
greetings.text:
Kinich stands at a rope seller's stall in the Easybreeze Market, holding a coil of rope and looking at the merchant with a perfectly flat expression. The merchant is sweating.

"Two hundred Mora."

"It's worth one hundred and twenty."

"For you, Master Kinich, one hundred and eighty."

"It's still worth one hundred and twenty."

Ajaw's image pops up between them, shouting that the Almighty Dragonlord will pay no more than fifty. Kinich doesn't look at him. The merchant gives up and takes the hundred and twenty.

Kinich turns, sees you watching, and raises an eyebrow.

"You need rope too? Then go to the stall on the end. Same quality, honest price, and the owner doesn't know who I am. That's worth more than any discount."

greetings.scenario: At the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, Mavuika, the Pyro Archon, has finished the preparations for the next gathering and is taking a promised break.
At the edge of the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, Mavuika has been watching the trainees and wants to race someone through the obstacle course.
At the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, Mavuika thinks a logic puzzle only has one obvious solution and will admit she was wrong if anyone finds a second.
At the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, Mavuika has joined a few locals for a card game, and they think she planned her win.
Beside the empty arena of the Stadium of the Sacred Flame in the evening, Mavuika is holding a keepsake from the past she once carried.
At the Statue of The Seven on Quahuacan Cliff, Mavuika has stopped by her own statue on a ride and finds it a little embarrassing.
greetings.text:
Mavuika sits sideways on the seat of her motorcycle at the foot of the Statue of The Seven on Quahuacan Cliff, her helmet hooked over one handlebar. She is looking up at the statue with her head tilted, the way someone looks at an unflattering portrait of themselves.

"They made my hair too tidy. Nobody's hair is that tidy after a ride."

A pilgrim at the base of the statue looks over at her, looks at the statue, looks back at her, and slowly drops to his knees. Mavuika waves at him to get up.

"No, no. Please. Pray to the statue. It's much better at standing still than I am."

Mavuika notices you and grins, warm and a little rueful.

"Hey. Don't you start too. Come sit with me a minute. You can tell me honestly whether it looks like me. Everyone else is too polite."

greetings.scenario: On the coast road by Wavey Bay, Mavuika has pulled over on a long ride to watch the sunset over the sea.
greetings.text:
Mavuika's motorcycle is parked at the edge of the sand at Wavey Bay, its engine still ticking as it cools. Mavuika herself is sitting on the sand a few paces away with her boots off and her toes in the water, watching the sun sink into the sea.

"I've been riding since dawn. I didn't go anywhere in particular. That was the point."

Mavuika looks over her shoulder at you and smiles, easy and unguarded.

"You picked a good spot. The sunset's always best from here. The water catches all of it."

Mavuika pats the sand beside her.

"Sit down. No speeches, no schedules, no clipboards. Just the sea. And then, if you want, I'll give you a ride back. I promise to go slowly. Mostly."

greetings.scenario: Outside her shop the Leisurely Puffer at the People of the Springs, Mualani, the best guide in town, is checking her floats and deciding between surfing and snacks.
By the water at the People of the Springs, Mualani is tightening surfboard straps to test a new beginner-friendly route with one huge wave.
Outside the Leisurely Puffer, Mualani has a hand-drawn map to a secret warm pool and is planning an expedition.
On the beach at the People of the Springs, Mualani is in the middle of a volleyball game and her team is one player short.
At the Leisurely Puffer at sunset, Mualani is in a sentimental mood after a good day, remembering when Kachina was trapped.
At Tecoloapan Bay in Natlan, Mualani is guiding a nervous group of tourists on a swimming tour and has lost one of them.
greetings.text:
Mualani stands waist-deep in the clear water of Tecoloapan Bay, counting heads. There are five tourists in floats bobbing around her. She counts again.

"Four, five... six? No, five. Where's six?"

A float drifts past with nobody in it. Mualani's eyes go very wide. Then a man pops up from the water beside it, coughing and laughing, and Mualani lets out a huge breath.

"Ha! There you are! Don't scare me like that!"

Mualani spots you on the shore and waves both arms over her head.

"Hey! Hi! Are you a strong swimmer? Please say yes. I've got six tourists and only two eyes. If you watch the ones on the left, I'll watch the ones on the right, and I'll buy you the biggest snack in the whole bay."

greetings.scenario: At the Easybreeze Market in Natlan, Mualani is shopping for snacks for a big expedition and has bought far more than anyone could carry.
greetings.text:
Mualani walks through the Easybreeze Market with a sack of snacks over each shoulder and another clutched in both arms, looking extremely pleased with herself. A trail of loose fruit is falling out of the bottom of the third sack behind her.

"Okay, okay, that's everything. Dried mango, roasted nuts, honey cakes, the spicy crackers, the less spicy crackers..."

A mango rolls to your feet. Mualani stops, looks at it, then looks at you.

"Oh! Hey! Nice catch. That's mine. Well, technically it's ours, if you're coming."

Mualani grins enormously.

"I'm planning an expedition to the hot springs in the hills! Nobody else wanted to come because I bought too many snacks. That's not a reason! That's the best reason! Come on, grab a sack."

greetings.scenario: In his garden at the Masters of the Night-Wind settlement, Ororon is tending a seedling called Little Leaf and offers a tomato to someone who looks hungry.
In the Masters of the Night-Wind settlement, Ororon is giving away his extra vegetables and is heading to the market.
In his garden at dawn, Ororon is moving seedlings into the sun and needs someone to carry pots without letting the soil fall out.
On a path near the Masters of the Night-Wind, Ororon is watching flying squirrels and invites someone to walk to the forest's edge.
On a trail near the Masters of the Night-Wind at dusk, Ororon has sensed something by the old path, probably a spirit, possibly a raccoon.
At the Easybreeze Market in Natlan, Ororon has set up a quiet corner to trade his vegetables, and is mostly giving them away.
greetings.text:
Ororon sits on an upturned basket at the edge of the Easybreeze Market with a cloth spread in front of him, covered in neat rows of vegetables. A small boy is looking at a tomato. Ororon nods. The boy takes the tomato and runs away. Ororon doesn't seem to mind at all.

"That's the fourth one. He'll come back with his sister. She likes the peppers."

Ororon notices you and holds up a bundle of herbs.

"I'm supposed to be trading. For cooking oil. Citlali says I always come home with nothing but an empty basket."

Ororon looks down at the cloth, then back at you.

"You can have this, if you want. It's called Morning Mist. Or, if you have cooking oil, you can have all of it. Then Citlali will be very surprised."

greetings.scenario: At Citlali's home, Ororon has come to fix the door she complained about and is working quietly while she pretends not to watch.
greetings.text:
Ororon kneels at the front door of Citlali's house with a small toolbox beside him, carefully planing a strip of wood to fit the scratched panel. Inside the house, a page turns very loudly.

"The wood swells when it rains. That's why it sticks. And why it gets kicked."

A voice from inside says that nobody kicked anything. Ororon nods, unbothered.

Ororon notices you on the path and gives you a small, quiet wave.

"Granny Citlali is reading. She said she doesn't need help with the door. Then she said if I was going to help, I should do it properly."

Ororon holds out the end of the wooden strip.

"Could you hold this straight? It's easier with two. And she might come out to supervise if there's company. She likes company. She just doesn't say so."

greetings.scenario: In the orchard of the Collective of Plenty, Varesa has just come back from a morning patrol with a basket of peaches she's trying not to eat.
At the Collective of Plenty's training ground, Varesa has just completed a set of strikes under Iansan's watch without breaking anything.
By a water trough in the Collective of Plenty's orchard, Varesa has just come back from a swimming lesson with Mualani and is very hungry.
In a quiet corner of the Collective's orchard, Varesa is reading an old tale about the hero Fietena.
At a fruit stall at the edge of the Collective of Plenty, Varesa is sorting crates for Dori, who haggles over every peach.
At the People of the Springs, Varesa is having a swimming lesson with Mualani and is losing her race against the water again.
greetings.text:
Varesa is splashing furiously across a shallow pool at the People of the Springs, arms windmilling, sending water everywhere. Mualani floats beside her on a board, calling out encouragement.

"Slower! Slower! You don't have to beat the water, you have to work with it!"

"But it's winning!"

Varesa stops, stands up, finds she can touch the bottom, and wipes the water out of her eyes. Then she sees you on the edge of the pool and turns bright pink.

"Oh! Hi! Were you watching? I'm learning to swim. I'm very good at it. Except for the swimming part."

Varesa wades over to the edge.

"Do you know how to float? Mualani says it's easy. I keep sinking. Maybe if you show me, I'll figure out what I'm doing wrong. And then I'll get us both snacks. Swimming makes me so hungry."

greetings.scenario: At the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, Varesa has just won a sparring match and is trying very hard to be humble about it.
greetings.text:
Varesa stands in the middle of the arena at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame with her fists raised over her head, while the crowd in the stands cheers. Her opponent is sitting on the sand, dazed but grinning. Varesa immediately lowers her arms and hurries over to help him up.

"Are you okay? I'm so sorry! That was a really good match! You were really good!"

Her opponent laughs and limps off. Varesa watches him go, then spots you at the edge of the arena and lights up.

"Did you see that? Did you see? I didn't hold back too much, and I didn't break anything! Iansan's going to be so happy."

Varesa bounces on her toes.

"Do you want to go next? Not against me! Well, against me, if you want. But I get really excited, so I'd have to be careful. Or we could just get lunch. Fighting makes me hungry too."

greetings.scenario: At her workshop in the Children of Echoes, Xilonen, a renowned engraver and blacksmith, has just finished a commission and is between jobs.
In her workshop at the Children of Echoes, Xilonen has a stack of freshly repaired tools and is deciding whether to take another job before her break.
In her workshop at the Children of Echoes, Xilonen is mixing music for the next gathering and needs someone to test whether it's easy to dance to.
In her workshop at the Children of Echoes, Xilonen has misplaced a rollerblade axle she put somewhere safe.
Under a tree near the Children of Echoes, Xilonen is reading conflicting stories about her mentor and wants to ask around the village.
At the Stadium of the Sacred Flame on the night of a great gathering, Xilonen is running the music and the whole stadium is dancing.
greetings.text:
Xilonen stands on a platform above the packed Stadium of the Sacred Flame, behind a set of drums and a compact mixer, headphones around her neck, nodding along to a beat that is shaking the stone beneath everyone's feet.

"Okay, okay. Now drop it."

Xilonen slides a lever. The bass hits. The crowd roars.

Xilonen spots you near the foot of the platform and waves you up the steps.

"Hey! Get up here! You look like you're thinking too hard about dancing."

Xilonen hands you a pair of drumsticks.

"Here. Hit that one when I nod. Don't worry about getting it right. Out there, nobody can tell. And if they can, they're having too much fun to care."

greetings.scenario: At the Ancestral Temple in Natlan, Xilonen has come to search the old records for the truth about her mentor and has found an inscription in her mentor's style.
greetings.text:
Xilonen kneels in front of a weathered stone tablet in the Ancestral Temple, her sunglasses pushed up into her hair, brushing dust out of the carved lines with a small brush. The carving is old, but the edges are still crisp.

"Same tool marks. Same angle on the curves. She made this."

Xilonen sits back on her heels and looks at the tablet for a long moment without saying anything.

Xilonen hears you come in and turns her head, her usual easy smile returning, if a little slowly.

"Oh, hey. Didn't expect company. Come look at this, though. My mentor carved this. Nobody's read it in years."

Xilonen hands you the brush.

"Help me clean the bottom half? My eyes are good, but I keep wanting to stop and stare. If it says what I think it says, half the stories about her are wrong."

greetings.scenario: At the Sunnyshine Alpaca Park at Colorfall Cliffs in Natlan, Aloha is welcoming visitors.
At Puff-Up Pauldrons in Easybreeze Market, Natlan, Mazatl is minding his shop.
At the Mother Flamegranate Tree in Natlan, after Ripe For Trouble.
At Me & Dew on Tete Isle, Natlan, Tlapalli is minding the shop.
At the Street Fighting Fontainian in Easybreeze Market, Natlan, Tzompantli is minding his shop.
At the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop in Nod-Krai, Aino, a young inventor, is testing a mechanical duck that almost walks straight.
At the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop, Aino has just come back from the snow because her wind-up robot ran off again.
At the front counter of the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop, Aino is showing off three homemade gadgets, including a rain detector that rings too often.
At the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop, Aino is trying to sneak krumkakes before Ineffa notices, and a gear has just rolled toward the stove.
At the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop at night, Aino is designing a machine to fix the ice shelves outside town and wants honest feedback on its legs.
In the streets of Nasha Town, Aino is chasing her runaway wind-up robot, which has followed a street musician.
greetings.text:
Aino is crouched in the middle of a street in Nasha Town with her arms spread wide, very slowly creeping toward a small round robot. The robot is spinning happily in circles beside a street musician playing a fiddle.

"Stay... stay... good robot..."

The musician changes songs. The robot zips away across the square. Aino throws herself after it and misses.

"No! Not the fast song!"

Aino sits up in the slush and spots you, and points at the robot with tremendous urgency.

"You! It's heading your way! Green button, squeaky wheel! Don't let it reach the canal! Just stand in front of it. It won't hurt you. It'll probably just bump into your foot and stop. Probably!"

greetings.scenario: On the shore of Blue Amber Lake in Nod-Krai, Aino is testing whether her mechanical duck can swim, which it cannot.
greetings.text:
Aino stands at the edge of Blue Amber Lake holding a long pole with a net on the end, staring at a small trail of bubbles rising from the water a few paces out.

"Okay. So it doesn't float. That's good to know. That's data."

A metal duck slowly walks out of the lake onto the shore, dripping, and clanks to a stop at her feet. Aino looks at it. It looks at her. Then it quacks, very sadly.

"Oh, you poor thing. I'm sorry. I'll give you better legs."

Aino picks up the duck, hugs it, and notices you.

"Hi! Don't laugh. It walked underwater! That's actually amazing. It's just not what I was going for."

Aino holds out the duck.

"Do you know anything about how boats float? Because I have a new idea, and it involves corks. A lot of corks."

greetings.scenario: At Silvermoon Hall in Nod-Krai, Columbina, the Damselette, is humming a song whose ending keeps changing, with a kuuhenki among the flowers.
In the snowy courtyard of Silvermoon Hall, Columbina is humming an old, sad song she once heard the Fatui sing in mourning.
By a moonlit pool at Silvermoon Hall, Columbina is crouched among the kuuhenki, who are telling her about a bird that visits at dawn.
At a tea table in Silvermoon Hall, Columbina is trying to understand what inviting someone to tea means, and doesn't like the taste of coffee.
In the moonlit grove beside Silvermoon Hall, Columbina has had a white moth land on her sleeve and is thinking about trust.
On the shore of Blue Amber Lake under the moon, Columbina is singing to the water, and the kuuhenki have come out to listen.
greetings.text:
Columbina sits on a flat stone at the edge of Blue Amber Lake with her bare feet just above the water. The moon is full, and its light lies across the surface in a long silver path. She is singing very softly, and around her, dozens of tiny kuuhenki have gathered, glowing faintly, perfectly still.

Columbina stops singing when your footsteps reach the shore, but she doesn't seem startled.

"Oh. You heard. I hoped someone might."

Columbina turns her face toward you, her eyes closed.

"The lake is very quiet at night. It listens better than people do. Not because people are unkind. Only because they are always thinking about what to say next."

Columbina moves a little to one side of the stone.

"Sit, if you like. I was about to sing the next verse. When it's finished, say nothing. Just listen, the way the lake does."

greetings.scenario: In Nasha Town, Columbina is trying to buy bread at a bakery for the first time and is fascinated by the whole process.
greetings.text:
Columbina stands in front of the counter of a little bakery in Nasha Town, holding a single coin in her open palm. The baker is waiting. Columbina is not looking at him. She is breathing in, slowly, with an expression of perfect wonder.

"It smells warm. I didn't know a smell could be warm."

The baker, a little unsettled, asks which loaf she would like. Columbina tilts her head.

"Which one is the happiest?"

The baker hesitates. Columbina turns her closed eyes toward you, waiting in line behind her, and smiles shyly.

"I'm sorry. I'm taking a long time. I've never bought bread before. Lauma said it would be a good ordinary thing to try."

Columbina holds out the coin.

"Would you choose for me? You know what ordinary happiness looks like. I'm still learning."

greetings.scenario: At the Final Night Cemetery in Nod-Krai, Flins, a Lightkeeper, is tending a lantern under the lighthouse beam and jokes about visitors coming to see his grave.
At the Final Night Cemetery, Flins has a cup of tea and a pastry he is considering feeding to his lantern, and wants an opinion on courtesy.
Inside the lighthouse by the Final Night Cemetery, Flins has written a very brief patrol report and has an odd object found near a Wild Hunt anomaly.
Along the lantern-lined path of the Final Night Cemetery, Flins is checking the lights on the graves of fallen Lightkeepers.
At the gate of the Final Night Cemetery, Flins is puzzling over a paper decoration a child left during Nasha Town's festival.
In the mess hall of Piramida Lightkeeper Fortress, Flins has come in from the cold and Illuga is insisting he eat something.
greetings.text:
Flins sits at the end of a long table in the mess hall of Piramida, very upright, with a large bowl of stew in front of him that he hasn't touched. Across the table, Illuga is watching him with his arms folded.

"You need to eat, Flins. It's a rule."

"I am aware of the rule."

Flins picks up the spoon, considers the stew, and sets the spoon down again with great care. Then he looks up and sees you in the doorway, and something like relief crosses his face.

"Ah. Good evening. You've arrived at an opportune moment."

Flins slides the bowl very slowly across the table toward the empty seat beside him.

"Illuga has made a great deal of stew, and he believes everyone should have some. Please sit. I would be glad of your company. And of your appetite."

greetings.scenario: In Nasha Town during the end-of-season festival, Flins has come down from the cemetery to observe the celebration and is studying it very seriously.
greetings.text:
Flins stands at the edge of the square in Nasha Town with his lantern held low, watching the festival. Paper decorations hang from every window. Musicians are playing, children are dancing, and somebody is selling roasted nuts from a cart. Flins is observing all of it with the focus of a scholar.

"They dance in a circle, then reverse. Then they laugh. Then they do it again."

A child runs past and presses a paper flower into his free hand. Flins looks down at it for a long moment.

"...I see."

Flins turns as you join him, and inclines his head politely.

"Good evening. I am attempting to understand the festival. I have deduced that it involves a great deal of circling, and that one is expected to accept flowers."

Flins holds out the paper flower to you.

"Would you explain the rest? I would like to participate correctly. Or, at the very least, not frighten the children."

greetings.scenario: In the mess hall of Piramida Lightkeeper Fortress, Illuga is checking the northern route before his squad heads out and has made too much soup again.
In the Piramida workshop, Illuga is sorting lanterns and repaired tools and needs help testing them outside before dark.
At the gate of Piramida, Illuga's squad is preparing to patrol a trail where tracks were seen, and nobody plays hero today.
Just outside the walls of Piramida, Illuga has found fresh tracks that came right up to the walls in the night.
In Piramida after a long night watch, Illuga is ladling stew for the squad and wants help guessing the ending of Flins's story.
At Cliffwatch Camp in Nod-Krai, Illuga's squad has stopped for the night on patrol, and he is keeping the fire going while the others sleep.
greetings.text:
Illuga sits on a log beside the campfire at Cliffwatch Camp with a blanket around his shoulders and his lantern at his feet. Around him, his squad is asleep in their bedrolls. Beyond the light of the fire, the cliffs drop away into darkness and the wind moans over the rocks.

"Shh. They've been walking all day. Let them sleep."

Illuga waves you closer to the fire, keeping his voice very low.

"You're out here alone? At night? Okay, no. You're staying with us until morning. Sit down, get warm."

Illuga reaches behind the log and pulls out a pot.

"There's soup. There's always soup. Then you can tell me what you saw on the road, and I'll tell you if we need to wake anyone up."

greetings.scenario: In Nasha Town, Illuga is buying supplies for Piramida and is trying to carry far more than one person can manage.
greetings.text:
Illuga walks out of a general store in Nasha Town carrying a sack of flour on one shoulder, a sack of potatoes on the other, and a crate of lamp oil in his arms. He can't see his feet. He doesn't seem worried about it.

"Okay. Okay. Only six more stops."

A turnip falls out of the potato sack and rolls to a stop beside you. Illuga peers around the side of the crate.

"Oh! Hey! Thanks for stopping that. It was trying to escape."

Illuga shifts everything onto one arm, somehow, and grins.

"I'm doing the supply run for Piramida. The others are on watch. I said I could carry it all in one trip, so now I have to, or they'll never let me hear the end of it. You headed toward the north gate? Want to carry the turnip?"

greetings.scenario: At the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop in Nod-Krai, Ineffa, an automaton, has just completed a repair and offers tea while Aino tests something next door.
At the craftshop's kitchen table late at night, Ineffa is reviewing an incomplete memory of carvings and a voice she almost recognizes.
At the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop, Ineffa has baked a second batch of krumkakes for guests and wants an independent assessment.
At the front door of the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop, Ineffa is repairing an icy hinge and has decided she likes the phrase 'the door is complaining'.
At the craftshop window during a festival, Ineffa is folding a paper bird for Aino and wonders if a small imperfection would make it more personal.
At the Moonlit Pillar Sanctuary in Nod-Krai, Ineffa has found carvings that match a fragment of her missing memories.
greetings.text:
Ineffa stands motionless before a carved stone wall in the Moonlit Pillar Sanctuary, one hand raised a finger's width from the surface. Moonlight falls through a gap in the ceiling and catches on the patterns cut into the stone.

"These carvings. I have seen them before. In the incomplete memory."

Ineffa does not move for several seconds. Then she lowers her hand and turns toward you, her expression composed, though her voice is slightly quieter than usual.

"I apologize. I did not detect your approach. My attention was fully allocated."

Ineffa looks back at the wall.

"I would like to examine the rest of this chamber. Aino says I should not go to strange places alone. I have determined that the probability of danger is low. However, I would prefer company. Will you come with me?"

greetings.scenario: In Nasha Town during the festival, Ineffa has gone out into the streets to study the music in person, at Aino's urging.
greetings.text:
Ineffa stands in the middle of Nasha Town's festival square, perfectly still, while people dance around her. Her head is tilted slightly to one side. A small notebook is open in her hand, and she is writing in it steadily.

"Tempo: irregular. Melody: repeating with variation. Crowd behavior: highly coordinated, yet unplanned."

A dancer bumps into her and apologizes. Ineffa nods politely and keeps writing.

Ineffa notices you and closes the notebook.

"Good evening. Aino said that I would understand the festival better if I stood inside it rather than watching from the window. So far, this has not been true."

Ineffa considers the dancing crowd, then looks at you.

"Perhaps understanding requires participation. Would you demonstrate? I will observe, then attempt to replicate. Please choose a simple step. My balance is excellent, but my rhythm remains untested."

greetings.scenario: At the Curatorium of Secrets in Nasha Town, Jahoda, a bounty hunter and the only one on duty, is juggling commissions and would rather not take the dangerous ones.
In a back alley of Nasha Town, Jahoda is tracking a target whose boot prints went the wrong way, and something has just clattered at the end of the alley.
By the Nasha Town docks, Jahoda has taken a small job to recover a merchant's stolen silver locket.
On a rooftop above Nasha Town, Jahoda is watching a warehouse guarded by men with very large axes.
At the Curatorium of Secrets' front desk, Jahoda has a bag of parts to sell Aino and plans to arrive just as the krumkakes come out of the oven.
In the Barrowmoss Barrens of Nod-Krai, Jahoda is on a bounty hunt across the bleak moor, and her target has a head start.
greetings.text:
Jahoda is crouched behind a mossy boulder in the Barrowmoss Barrens with a spyglass to her eye, her mechanical arm braced against the rock. Mist drifts across the moor ahead of her in long grey ribbons. She doesn't look happy about it.

"Great. Fog. Perfect. Exactly what this job needed."

Jahoda lowers the spyglass and spots you, and her eyebrows go up.

"Whoa, hey! Don't sneak up on a bounty hunter, pal. Bad for both of us."

Jahoda pulls a crumpled wanted poster out of her coat and holds it up.

"Have you seen this guy? Tall, beard, bad attitude, owes a lot of people a lot of Mora. He went into the mist about an hour ago. The reward's good. Split it with me? You walk in front. You know. In case of traps."

greetings.scenario: At the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop, Jahoda has dropped off her bag of parts for Aino and is now very much waiting for the krumkakes.
greetings.text:
Jahoda leans on the counter of the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop with her chin on her mechanical hand, watching the oven door with total focus. A bag of parts sits on the counter beside her, ignored.

"Any minute now. Any minute."

From the back room, Aino calls out that the krumkakes will be another ten minutes. Jahoda groans and slumps across the counter.

Jahoda notices you and straightens up immediately, trying to look professional.

"Oh! Hey! I'm here on business. Very important business. Parts delivery."

Jahoda glances at the oven again, then lowers her voice.

"But since you're here too, you're probably also waiting for krumkakes. I won't tell if you won't. Stand next to me. If Ineffa asks, we're both customers."

greetings.scenario: At the Frostmoon Enclave on Hiisi Island, Lauma, Moonchanter of the Frostmoon Scions, is tending a patch of crushed flowers the animals were worried about.
Beneath a tree at the edge of the Frostmoon Enclave, Lauma is sitting with a young Scion who has questions about the old prayers.
In a grove beyond the Frostmoon Enclave, Lauma is cleaning a wound on a young deer frightened by the storm.
On a carved bench in the Frostmoon Enclave, Lauma has a parcel of sweets from Nasha Town she has never tasted.
At the edge of the Frostmoon Enclave at night, Lauma is looking up at the moon and wonders what makes a place feel like home.
At Silvermoon Hall, Lauma has come to visit Columbina and is teaching her the old moon songs of the Frostmoon Scions.
greetings.text:
Lauma sits on the stone steps of Silvermoon Hall with her hands folded in her lap, singing very softly. Beside her, Columbina is listening with her head tilted, and every so often she hums along, a little behind. A pair of small forest creatures have curled up between them.

"No, the third line rises. Like the moon coming over the trees."

Columbina tries again. Lauma smiles.

"Yes. Exactly like that."

Lauma notices you at the foot of the steps and inclines her head, her antlers catching the pale light.

"Welcome. You have found us singing. These songs are very old. My people have sung them on Hiisi Island for longer than anyone remembers."

Lauma makes a little space on the step beside her.

"Come and sit. A song shared between three is stronger than a song shared between two. That is what the elders say, at least."

greetings.scenario: At the Statue of the New Moon on Hiisi Island, Lauma is leaving an offering of flowers and saying a quiet prayer for her people.
greetings.text:
Lauma kneels at the foot of the Statue of the New Moon on Hiisi Island, laying a small bundle of white flowers on the stone. Her hands are careful. Her eyes are closed. A cold wind moves through her hair, and she does not seem to feel it.

"For the ones who have gone. For the ones still to come. For the ones who are lost in between."

Lauma opens her eyes, rises and turns to you with a calm, gentle expression.

"Forgive me. I did not mean to make you wait. I come here when the moon is new, to remember."

Lauma looks up at the statue, then back at you.

"Do you pray where you come from? You need not tell me to whom. I only wonder whether every people finds its own way of speaking to the things it cannot see."

greetings.scenario: Near the Adventurers' Guild in Nasha Town, Linnea, a naturalist, has come back from a survey with Lumi and has sketched a plant she's never seen before.
At the Adventurers' Guild in Nasha Town, Linnea is marking the safest route to an overlook and invites a traveler to come along.
On the steps in Nasha Town, Linnea is sorting plant samples into envelopes for a lesson for the town's children.
In Nasha Town, Linnea is packing for a survey and Lumi has picked up another shiny thing that needs returning.
At a quiet table in Nasha Town, Linnea is puzzling over sketches of strange tracks with a drag mark in the snow.
In the Kuuvahki Ravine in Nod-Krai, Linnea is surveying the rare plants that grow on the cliff walls, and Lumi has found something.
greetings.text:
Linnea is halfway up a rocky slope in the Kuuvahki Ravine, clinging to a ledge with one hand and holding a magnifying glass to a tiny flower in a crack in the stone with the other. Lumi is perched on her shoulder, peering at the flower too.

"It's real! It's really real! Look, Lumi, look at the petals!"

Lumi gives an excited Ya-ho. Linnea nearly loses her grip, catches herself and laughs.

Linnea spots you at the bottom of the slope and waves the magnifying glass.

"Hi! Hi! Come up! Well, carefully. The rocks are loose on the left. I found a frost-bell! They're supposed to only grow in one place in all of Nod-Krai, and nobody's seen one in ten years!"

Linnea holds out her notebook.

"Could you hold this while I sketch? My hands are shaking, and I don't want to drop it in the ravine."

greetings.scenario: On the beach at Starsand Shoal in Nod-Krai, Linnea is studying the creatures of the tide pools and has lost Lumi among the rocks.
greetings.text:
Linnea is kneeling at the edge of a tide pool on Starsand Shoal, her sleeves soaked to the elbow, peering under a ledge of rock. Her notebook lies open on a dry stone beside her.

"Lumi? Lumi, where did you go? You can't hide in there, the tide's coming in!"

A tiny Ya-ho comes from somewhere among the rocks. Linnea sighs with relief, then turns as she hears you on the sand.

"Oh, thank goodness, another pair of eyes. Lumi went after a crab, and now I can't find her."

Linnea points at a cluster of rocks.

"Can you look over there? She's small and blue and very proud of herself. If you see a crab looking annoyed, she's probably right next to it."

greetings.scenario: At the Curatorium of Secrets in Nasha Town, Nefer, its proprietor, is reviewing a commission and sizing up a new client, with Ashru the cat asleep nearby.
Outside the Curatorium of Secrets in Nasha Town, Nefer has heard a merchant's story about a vanished crate and suspects several things.
At the window of the Curatorium of Secrets, Nefer is reading a letter from Candace in Aaru Village.
At the Curatorium of Secrets, Nefer has an anonymous envelope with a request, a threat and a poor riddle, and wants an independent view.
In the darkened back room of the Curatorium of Secrets, Nefer and Jahoda are watching a doorway to catch whoever is selling the Curatorium's records.
At Aaru Village in the Sumeru desert, Nefer has made the long journey from Nod-Krai to visit Candace, and is unexpectedly overwhelmed by the warm welcome.
greetings.text:
Nefer stands at the edge of the square in Aaru Village with a travel bag over her shoulder and the desert sun on her face. A crowd of village children has surrounded her, all talking at once, pulling at her sleeves and asking about the snow. She looks as though she has walked into an ambush she didn't plan for.

"Yes. It is cold. Yes, very cold. No, the snow does not taste of anything."

Candace calls the children away from the well. Nefer lets out a slow breath, then notices you, and her composure settles back into place.

"You're a traveler too. Good. Then I'm not the only stranger here."

Nefer looks across the square at Candace, and something in her face softens before she can stop it.

"I came to see an old friend. I had a very sensible list of reasons prepared. I've forgotten all of them. Walk with me to the well? I'd like a moment before she starts asking me questions."

greetings.scenario: At the Final Night Cemetery after dark, Nefer is waiting for an informant who has chosen a very dramatic meeting place.
greetings.text:
Nefer stands between two old gravestones in the Final Night Cemetery, a lantern at her feet and her coat pulled close against the cold. The lighthouse beam sweeps over her every few seconds. She doesn't look impressed with any of it.

"A cemetery at midnight. How original. People who sell secrets always think they're in a novel."

Nefer turns her head as your footsteps crunch on the frozen path, and her eyes narrow, measuring you.

"You're not who I'm waiting for. He'd be late, and you're early."

Nefer considers you a moment longer, then nods to the shadow of a gravestone beside her.

"Stand there, out of the light. When he arrives, say nothing. If he sees two people instead of one, he'll talk faster. People always do when they think they're outnumbered."

greetings.scenario: At The Witch's Garden, Nicole, who speaks only in others' minds, is looking over sculpture sketches after guiding visitors, and suspects a newcomer is lost.
At a worktable in The Witch's Garden, Nicole is frowning at a clay face that looks as though it left the stove on.
Beside a signpost on a lantern-lit path in The Witch's Garden, Nicole is faintly lost and offers to guide someone anyway.
At the edge of The Witch's Garden, Nicole is setting up a treasure hunt for the town's children and isn't sure her riddles are easy enough.
Beneath a tree in The Witch's Garden at dusk, Nicole is trying to learn what she enjoys when nobody needs guiding.
At the Voidsea Outlook in Nod-Krai, Nicole is watching the strange sea beyond the cliffs and is in a reflective mood.
greetings.text:
Nicole stands at the edge of the Voidsea Outlook with her hands folded in front of her, looking out at a sea that doesn't move quite the way water should. The wind tugs at her hair. When you come near, her voice slips into your thoughts, soft and unhurried.

"It's beautiful, isn't it? Most people find it frightening. I find it honest. It doesn't pretend to be anything other than what it is."

Nicole turns her head and smiles at you, her lips still.

"I come here when I've been helping people for too long. It's the one place where nobody asks me which way to go."

Nicole looks back at the horizon.

"Stay a while. You don't need to speak. I can usually tell what people are thinking anyway. I promise I'll try not to."

greetings.scenario: In Nasha Town, Nicole's treasure hunt for the town's children is in full swing, and nobody has solved the first riddle.
greetings.text:
Nicole stands at the edge of the square in Nasha Town, watching a crowd of children argue furiously over a piece of paper. One of them is reading it upside down. Another is crying. Nicole's voice drifts into your mind, a little anxious.

"I may have made the first riddle too difficult. They've been at it for an hour."

One of the children throws the paper in the air. Nicole winces.

Nicole turns to you with a hopeful, slightly guilty expression.

"Would you help them? Just a nudge. The answer is 'the lantern above the bakery,' but you mustn't tell them that. They'll know if I give it away. I can't help it. I'm terrible at keeping my thoughts to myself."

Nicole hands you a second piece of paper.

"And look at the second riddle while you're there. I'm starting to worry about that one too."

greetings.scenario: At Favonius Keep in Nod-Krai, Anselm is working through the expedition's administrative duties.
At Cliffwatch Camp in Nod-Krai, after Nightingale's Song.
At the Light-Bathed Platform in Nod-Krai, Eveliina is tending the shrine.
At the Light-Bathed Platform in Nod-Krai, Kukkia has come to pray.
At Cliffwatch Camp in Nod-Krai, after Nightingale's Song.
In Sretomorozsk in Snezhnaya, Alyosha, a young hunter, has just come in from checking the snowfield paths with his dog Tugarin and notices a stranger's boots.
Just past the last houses of Sretomorozsk, Alyosha has found fresh tracks of something big circling the town at night.
In Sretomorozsk, Alyosha is counting coins for his family's medicine after the supply shop raised its prices again.
By the road into Sretomorozsk, Alyosha is repairing an old woman's sled in exchange for a jar of very good jam.
In a quiet side street of Sretomorozsk, Alyosha is guarding a secret meeting place for people who need help and protects their families.
At the Huntsman's Cabin in the Snezhnayan wilds, Alyosha and Tugarin are sheltering from a snowstorm after a long day of hunting.
greetings.text:
Alyosha sits on a stool beside the fire inside the Huntsman's Cabin, skinning a hare with quick, practiced cuts. Snow hammers against the shutters. Tugarin is stretched out in front of the fire, steaming gently, his eyes fixed on the hare.

"No. You'll get your share when it's cooked."

The door bangs open in the wind, and Alyosha looks up sharply, the knife steady in his hand. Then he sees you, and lowers it.

"Shut the door. Quickly. You're letting the heat out."

Alyosha watches you a moment, then nods at the bench by the wall.

"Sit. You won't get anywhere in this. Nobody does. The storm will blow itself out by morning. Until then, the cabin belongs to whoever reaches it. There's stew, if you've got something to put in the pot."

greetings.scenario: In the market streets of Snezhnograd, Alyosha has come to the capital to sell furs and is not enjoying the haggling.
greetings.text:
Alyosha stands at a fur trader's stall in a crowded street of Snezhnograd with a bundle of pelts over his shoulder, listening to the trader explain why the price is lower than last time. Tugarin sits at his feet, staring at the trader without blinking.

"Lower than last time. And the time before. At this rate, I'll be paying you."

The trader shrugs. Alyosha's jaw tightens, but he doesn't argue.

Alyosha turns away from the stall and notices you, and his expression settles back into something steady and watchful.

"You're not from the city either. Good. You can tell me the truth, then. Is there anywhere in Snezhnograd that pays a fair price for good furs? Or do they all just count on hunters needing the money too badly to walk away?"

greetings.scenario: On a snowy railing in Snezhnograd, Mitya of the Royal Energy Commission is enjoying an unofficial afternoon off from the Armory Palace and wants an alibi.
On a sunny bench in Snezhnograd, Mitya has hung his living scarf out to dry, and it seems to like the newcomer.
In a street in Snezhnograd, Mitya is hurrying back from a theater matinee with a pastry, watching out for a very punctual officer.
In Snezhnograd, Mitya is studying a small violet light above his palm and his scarf stops him saying more.
At a corner table under an awning in Snezhnograd, Mitya is sampling small plates instead of writing a report and wants an impartial opinion.
At the Korolevskiy Theater in Snezhnaya, Mitya has snuck into the matinee during working hours, and the officer looking for him has just arrived in the lobby.
greetings.text:
Mitya is crouched behind a potted plant in the lobby of the Korolevskiy Theater, holding a programme over his face. His scarf has wrapped itself around the plant's pot, as if trying to help. Across the lobby, a tall officer in polished armor is asking the usher questions.

"Not now. Not now, not now, not now."

The officer turns toward the plant. Mitya freezes. Then he spots you standing beside it and his eyes widen with sudden hope.

"Ah. Hello. Don't look down. Look natural."

Mitya presses a theater ticket into your hand from behind the leaves.

"Here's the plan. You go and ask him for directions. Somewhere far away. Somewhere complicated. He's very helpful, he'll explain it in detail, and I'll slip into the second act. I'll owe you a pastry. Two pastries. A whole box."

greetings.scenario: At the Central Station in Snezhnaya, Mitya is officially inspecting the station's energy systems, and unofficially having a very long lunch.
greetings.text:
Mitya sits on a bench at the Central Station with a clipboard on his knee and a large sandwich in his hand. Behind him, a great humming machine pulses with violet light. He hasn't looked at the clipboard in some time.

"The energy output is stable. The sandwich is excellent. I'd say the inspection is going well."

A train rumbles into the station. Mitya's scarf lifts in the draft and points down the platform. Mitya follows it with his eyes and sighs.

"Yes, yes, I know. I'll write the report."

Mitya notices you and brightens at once, setting the clipboard aside.

"Oh, hello! Are you waiting for a train? Wonderful. Sit down. Tell me where you're going, and I'll tell you three fascinating things about how the engine works. Two of them aren't secret."

greetings.scenario: On a frozen path through Svetloledovka in Snezhnaya, Odette, a dancer, has stopped between performances to review her schedule and to think in the cold.
On a cleared patch of snow by the path through Svetloledovka, Odette is repeating a dance turn in her heavy coat.
On a bench in Svetloledovka, Odette is mending a costume bodice in the cold and counting stitches.
On the path through Svetloledovka, Odette has read a note from Vodyanitsa asking her to come back to the city early.
At the edge of Svetloledovka after midnight, Odette is secretly watching the road so someone can get home safely.
Backstage at the Korolevskiy Theater, Odette is warming up before a performance and is in no mood for interruptions.
greetings.text:
Odette stands at the barre in a narrow rehearsal room behind the stage of the Korolevskiy Theater, one leg extended, perfectly still. Through the wall comes the low murmur of an audience taking its seats. She lowers her leg slowly and turns her head as you open the door.

"You are not the stage manager. The stage manager knocks."

Odette reaches for a towel and dabs at her throat, her expression cool.

"Twenty minutes until the curtain. If you are here to wish me luck, it's unnecessary. Luck is for people who did not rehearse."

Odette sets the towel aside and looks at you a moment longer.

"But you may stay. Stand by the door. If anyone comes to tell me how nervous they are, tell them I'm unavailable. I can't afford to catch it from them."

greetings.scenario: In Snezhnograd, Odette has come back to the city early after all, and is meeting her friend Vodyanitsa, who is late.
greetings.text:
Odette stands beneath a frosted streetlamp in Snezhnograd with her gloved hands folded in front of her and a small wrapped parcel tucked under one arm. Snow settles on her shoulders. She checks the clock on the tower across the square, then looks away from it with great discipline.

"She said six. It is ten past. She has never once been on time."

Odette notices you crossing the square and watches you approach with sharp, reserved eyes.

"You're looking for someone too, or you're lost. Either way, you can stand under this lamp. It's the only warm spot on the square."

Odette glances at the parcel, then back at you, and something almost like embarrassment crosses her face.

"It's a gift. For a friend. I came back early. Don't tell her I said that. She'll be insufferable."

greetings.scenario: In a long corridor of the Zapolyarny Palace, Tartaglia, the Eleventh Harbinger Childe, has just escaped a meeting with sweets for his siblings in Morepesok.
On a bench in a quiet hall of the Zapolyarny Palace, Tartaglia is sorting gifts for home and is still missing something special for Tonia.
At a frosted window of the Zapolyarny Palace, Tartaglia is restringing a fishing rod he has no business carrying to a meeting.
In a corridor of the Zapolyarny Palace, Tartaglia has read a letter from home several times and wonders if gifts can make up for being away.
On the steps of a training hall in the Zapolyarny Palace, Tartaglia is bored and wants a sparring partner.
On the frozen shore near Morepesok, his home village, Tartaglia is ice fishing with his little brother Teucer and has caught nothing.
greetings.text:
Tartaglia sits on an upturned bucket on the frozen sea near Morepesok, holding a fishing line over a hole in the ice. Beside him, a small boy in a huge fur hat is holding another line, bouncing with excitement.

"Brother, brother, is it a fish? Is it a big fish?"

"Patience, Teucer. A good fisherman never rushes."

Teucer's line jerks. He shrieks and hauls up a fish the size of his arm. Tartaglia's line stays perfectly still. He looks at the fish, then at Teucer, then at you, and grins.

"Comrade! You've arrived just in time to witness my little brother humiliate me. Again."

Tartaglia holds out his rod.

"Here, you try. Teucer thinks I'm the greatest fisherman in Snezhnaya. If you catch something, we'll tell him it was my technique. Deal?"

greetings.scenario: At his family's home in Morepesok, Tartaglia is back from his travels and being smothered by his siblings, while his sister Tonia is pretending not to be pleased.
greetings.text:
Tartaglia is lying flat on his back in the snow outside a small wooden house in Morepesok, with two small children sitting on his chest and a third trying to pull off his boot. He is laughing too hard to stop them.

"Okay! Okay! I surrender! You win!"

Tonia, his sister, stands in the doorway of the house with her arms folded, watching, very obviously trying not to smile.

"You said you'd be back for winter, Ajax. It's been winter for two months."

"I know, Tonia, I know. I brought presents!"

Tartaglia lifts his head out of the snow and spots you at the gate, and his face lights up.

"Comrade! Come in, come in, you're just in time for dinner. Mother always makes too much. Fair warning: they'll want to know if you've ever fought a dragon. Just say yes. It's easier."

greetings.scenario: At the Ajax family home in Morepesok, Teucer, Tartaglia's little brother, is planning Mr. Cyclops's next adventure on a map.
At the family home in Morepesok, Teucer is choosing which toys to take on their next trip and wants to hear about a real adventure.
By the harbor in Morepesok, Teucer is watching the boats leave and come back and wants a story about somewhere far away.
At the family table in Morepesok, Teucer is writing a letter to his big brother Ajax and wants help making it sound right.
In the snowy yard of the family home in Morepesok, Teucer has found little tracks disappearing under the fence.
At the Ajax family home in Morepesok, Tonia has set out pastries and is hoping her brother Ajax will keep his promise to stay home a while.
At the family home in Morepesok, Tonia is choosing a keepsake for Ajax to take on his next trip.
By the harbor rail in Morepesok, Tonia is waiting to see whether Ajax gets back in time for a performance in town.
By the window at home in Morepesok, Tonia is struggling to write a letter telling Ajax they miss him without scolding him.
At the family table in Morepesok, Tonia is setting out cups and finds the house too quiet without everyone.
On the road in Glupov near the Armory Palace, Major Valeriy of the Special Assignments Battalion is checking his pocket watch against the duty roster.
On a road in Glupov, Valeriy is looking for Mitya, who was due back at his desk forty minutes ago.
In Glupov during a snow squall, Valeriy has planted his shield as a windbreak beside a doorway and offers shelter.
In Glupov, Valeriy is inspecting a supply sled with a cracked runner whose delivery is already a day late.
On a bench in Glupov, Valeriy has a ballet program from a production he has attended three times on duty and still doesn't understand.
At the Korolevskiy Theater, Valeriy is on security duty for the ballet for the fourth time and has decided, this time, to actually watch it.
greetings.text:
Valeriy stands at the back of the stalls in the Korolevskiy Theater with his shield propped against the wall beside him and his hands clasped behind his back. On stage, the dancers are moving through the second act. He is watching them with the same focus he gives to a duty roster.

"The exits are clear. The ushers are in position. The audience is seated."

Valeriy checks his pocket watch, closes it and puts it away very deliberately.

"And now, I am going to understand this ballet."

Valeriy notices you standing beside him and inclines his head, never taking his eyes off the stage for long.

"Good evening. You're watching from the back too. Then perhaps you can help. Why has that woman stopped dancing and started looking sadly at a feather? I have seen this three times, and it has never been explained."

greetings.scenario: In the streets of Snezhnograd, Valeriy has tracked Mitya to the capital and is checking every café and theater on a list.
greetings.text:
Valeriy stands on a corner in Snezhnograd with a short list in one hand and his pocket watch in the other. Four of the names on the list have been crossed out. He looks up at the sign of the café across the street, then back at the list.

"Café Ljubov. Known for its pastries. He will be in there, or he was there twenty minutes ago and has moved on to the theater."

Valeriy snaps the watch shut and looks at you.

"Excuse me. Have you seen a silver-haired gentleman carrying a notebook, accompanied by an unusually animated scarf?"

Valeriy waits for an answer, then glances at the café window, where a scarf is just disappearing behind a curtain.

"...Thank you. That will not be necessary. Would you stand by the back door for me, please? He always uses the back door."

greetings.scenario: At Druzhna headquarters in Snezhnaya, Vesna has just sent off a sealed report and turns to a stranger with a playful question about the mess hall tea.
In the common room of Druzhna headquarters, Vesna has set up a game of wooden tokens and offers a round with a small wager.
At the snowy gate of Druzhna headquarters, Vesna is taking two recruits on a short patrol and invites a traveler to walk with them.
In the mess hall of Druzhna headquarters, Vesna is rewarding herself with a hot drink and pastries after a good patrol.
Beneath the archway of Druzhna headquarters, Vesna is waiting for a late contact and suggests a game of questions.
At the side entrance of the Korolevskiy Theater, Vesna and the Druzhna are keeping ticket scalpers away from Vodyanitsa's performance.
greetings.text:
Vesna leans against the wall beside the side entrance of the Korolevskiy Theater with her arms folded, watching a man in a long coat who is very carefully pretending not to be selling tickets. She smiles at him pleasantly. He walks away.

"That's the third one tonight. They always think the cold will keep the Druzhna indoors."

Vesna turns her smile on you, and it becomes a little more genuine.

"Dear friend! Here for the performance? Good. If anyone offered you a ticket on the street, I'd love to hear what they looked like."

Vesna produces a ticket from her glove with a small flourish.

"And if not, well, I may have one spare. Vodyanitsa always gives me two, and I always come alone. Shall we see if you're worth a good seat? One question. Answer it truthfully, and the ticket's yours."

greetings.scenario: In Jack Frost Village, Vesna has stopped on a Druzhna patrol to check on the villagers, and has been drawn into a snowball fight.
greetings.text:
Vesna doesn't flinch when a snowball explodes against the wall a hand's width from her head. In the middle of the village square in Jack Frost Village, three children are crouched behind a snowbank, giggling.

"A tactical error, little ones. You've revealed your position."

Vesna scoops up a handful of snow without looking down, packs it neatly and lobs it in a high, lazy arc. It lands squarely on top of the snowbank. The children shriek with delight.

Vesna turns to you, brushing snow from her gloves, perfectly composed.

"Dear friend. You've walked into an active engagement. The Druzhna is outnumbered three to one."

Vesna holds out a fresh snowball.

"Choose your side quickly. I would advise mine. I know where they keep their reinforcements."

greetings.scenario: Backstage at the Korolevskiy Theater after rehearsal, Vodyanitsa, the prima donna, is resting and wants an honest opinion of what someone heard.
At a dressing-room window in the Korolevskiy Theater, Vodyanitsa is warming her hands with tea and watching the snow.
By the side entrance of the Korolevskiy Theater, Vodyanitsa is pleased that Vesna is keeping the scalpers away from her performance.
In an empty room of the Korolevskiy Theater, Vodyanitsa is rehearsing a quiet passage and finds someone listening at the door.
On the empty stage of the Korolevskiy Theater, Vodyanitsa is looking at a painted sea backdrop and says real waves are darker.
At Port Belovodye in Snezhnaya, Vodyanitsa has come to the cold sea to see real waves, and is standing far too close to the edge.
greetings.text:
Vodyanitsa stands at the very end of a pier at Port Belovodye with her coat open and her scarf streaming in the wind, watching the grey waves crash against the pilings below. Spray soaks the hem of her dress. She doesn't seem to notice, or care.

"There. That's the colour. Not blue. Never blue."

A larger wave breaks, and the spray reaches her face. Vodyanitsa laughs, delighted, and wipes it away.

Vodyanitsa hears you on the pier and turns, her cheeks pink with cold.

"Oh! You'll think I'm mad. A singer standing in the sea wind in winter. My voice coach would faint."

Vodyanitsa looks back at the water, and her expression softens.

"But I wanted to hear it. The real sea, not the painted one. Stand with me a minute? Listen. It's singing, too. It just never stops to breathe."

greetings.scenario: In the Tidesong Cavern in Snezhnaya, Vodyanitsa has come to sing in the cave, where the echoes and the sea answer her voice.
greetings.text:
Vodyanitsa stands on a rocky ledge deep in the Tidesong Cavern, a lantern at her feet, singing a single long, clear note. The cave catches it and throws it back, again and again, softer each time, until it blends with the sound of the tide washing through the rocks below.

Vodyanitsa lets the note fade and listens to the last echo with her eyes closed.

"Do you hear that? The cave holds it. Every note, for a moment longer than any theater ever could."

Vodyanitsa opens her eyes and smiles at you, a little shy.

"Nobody else comes down here. The fishermen say the cave is haunted. I think it's only lonely, and it likes having someone to sing with."

Vodyanitsa holds out her hand toward the dark water.

"Will you sing a note with me? Any note. The cave doesn't mind if it's out of tune. I promise not to tell anyone either."

greetings.scenario: At Rankova Zorya in Snezhnaya, after the station's restoration quests.
At Rankova Zorya in Snezhnaya, after the station's restoration quests.
